docs.title: Draw Steel Codex Wiki
docs.text:
Welcome to the code documentation for the Draw Steel Codex — the Lua mod for DMHub that implements MCDM's Draw Steel tabletop RPG system.

This wiki is for anyone who wants to understand how the codebase works: new contributors, modders looking to extend it, or anyone curious about the architecture.

docs.title: What is this project?
docs.text:
Draw Steel Codex is a Lua mod that runs inside DMHub, a virtual tabletop (VTT) platform. It implements the full Draw Steel RPG system, including:

  • Character creation and progression
  • Abilities, conditions, and combat mechanics
  • Monster stat blocks and AI
  • A rich compendium browser and editors
  • Custom UI panels (action bars, character sheets, initiative tracking)
  • GoblinScript, a formula expression language for game mechanics
  • A document/journal system with embedded dice rolls and encounters

docs.title: Tech stack
docs.text: Component Technology Language Lua (99.8%), Python (validation tooling) Runtime DMHub engine UI Declarative panel system (gui.Panel{}, gui.Label{}, etc.) Formulas GoblinScript (custom expression language) Data Named tables with cloud persistence Modules 42 modules, 517 files loaded via main.lua

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This page will help you orient yourself in the Draw Steel Codex codebase. By the end, you'll understand the project layout and know where to look for any piece of functionality.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• DMHub installed (the VTT engine this mod runs inside)
  • A text editor with Lua support (VS Code with the Lua Language Server extension recommended)
  • Git (to clone the repository)

docs.title: Cloning the repo
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/VerisimLLC/draw-steel-codex.git
cd draw-steel-codex

docs.title: Understanding the project layout
docs.text:
This is not a typical application with a build step. The entire codebase is Lua source files that DMHub loads at runtime. There is no compiler, no bundler, and no test runner.

The root of the repo looks like this:

draw-steel-codex/
  main.lua                          # Entry point — loads all 517 files
  CLAUDE.md                         # AI development guide
  GoblinScript_Guide.md             # Formula language reference
  UI_BEST_PRACTICES.md              # UI control reference
  monster-reference.md              # Monster stat blocks
  Definitions/                      # Engine API type stubs (209 files)
  DMHub_Utils_5b73/                 # Shared utilities
  DMHub_Core_UI_752e/               # UI framework
  DMHub_Game_Rules_fc51/            # Base game rules (foundation)
  Draw_Steel_Core_Rules_1b8f/       # Draw Steel system (domain)
  Draw_Steel_Character_Builder_45c3/  # Character creation
  Draw_Steel_UI_bd58/               # Draw Steel UI panels
  ... (42 modules total)

docs.title: The module naming convention
docs.text:
Every directory follows the pattern ModuleName_XXXX where XXXX is a hex module ID assigned by DMHub. For example:

  • DMHub_Game_Rules_fc51 — the base game rules module (ID: fc51)
  • Draw_Steel_Core_Rules_1b8f — the Draw Steel system (ID: 1b8f)
  • DMHub_Core_UI_752e — the UI framework (ID: 752e)

The hex suffix is just an identifier. Don't worry about memorizing them — focus on the human-readable name before the underscore.

docs.title: How files are loaded
docs.text:
Open main.lua. You'll see 517 require() calls like:

require('DMHub_Utils_5b73.Utils')
require('DMHub_Utils_5b73.CoroutineUtils')
require('DMHub_Utils_5b73.GoblinScript')
require('DMHub_Core_UI_752e.Gui')
require('DMHub_Core_UI_752e.Hud')
-- ... 512 more

Order matters. Dependencies must be loaded before the files that use them. This is why utilities and core UI load first, game rules load next, and Draw Steel-specific code loads last.

Every Lua file starts with the same line:

local mod = dmhub.GetModLoading()

This gives the file access to its parent module's lifecycle. You'll see mod used throughout for things like checking if the module has been unloaded (mod.unloaded).

Do not create new Lua files

Lua files must be registered through DMHub's module system. Simply placing a file on disk and adding a require to main.lua will cause a load failure. If you need to add code, add it to an existing file in the appropriate module.

docs.title: The four architecture layers
docs.text:
The codebase is organized into four layers, from lowest-level to highest:

  1. Engine API (Definitions/) — Type stubs documenting what DMHub provides. You never edit these, but they're invaluable for understanding what functions are available.

  2. Foundation (DMHub_Game_Rules_fc51/, DMHub_Core_UI_752e/, DMHub_Utils_5b73/) — Generic, system-agnostic game rules and UI framework. Creatures, abilities, conditions, and the panel system live here.

  3. Domain (Draw_Steel_Core_Rules_1b8f/, Draw_Steel_Ability_Behaviors_aef5/, Draw_Steel_Modifiers_d18e/) — Draw Steel-specific implementation. This layer extends the foundation with MCDM's game mechanics.

  4. UI/Integration (Draw_Steel_UI_bd58/, Draw_Steel_Character_Builder_45c3/, DMHub_Core_Panels_65a9/) — User-facing panels, character creation, compendium browsers, and HUD elements.

See Architecture Overview for a detailed diagram.

docs.title: Journal Stylesheets
docs.text:
Stylesheets let you re-skin a journal's look -- heading sizes, colors, bullets, callout boxes -- without touching the journal's text. You define a stylesheet once, then point any journal at it. Change the stylesheet and every journal using it updates instantly.

Tip: assign the MCDM stylesheet to this very page to see it rendered the way it's described. {.emphasis It styles itself.}

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Open a journal and click Edit.
  2. In the editor toolbar, use the Stylesheet: dropdown to pick a stylesheet (or Default for the plain look).
  3. Save. The journal now renders in that style.

To build or change a stylesheet, open the Compendium -> Journal Stylesheets.

docs.title: Creating and editing a stylesheet
docs.text:
In Compendium -> Journal Stylesheets:

  • Add a new stylesheet, then give it a Name.
  • Set Inherits from to base it on another stylesheet -- it keeps everything from the parent and only changes what you override (see Inheritance below).
  • Edit the base skin (headings, body, bullets) and add named classes (callouts and emphasis spans).

Every change saves immediately and any open journal using the stylesheet re-renders live.

docs.title: The base skin
docs.text:
The base skin controls the journal's structural typography:

  • Headings 1-6 -- font, size, color, weight (Regular / Bold / Black), and caps (None / Small Caps / All Caps).
  • Body -- font and text color.
  • Bullet -- the marker glyph and its color.
  • Quote -- blockquotes can take their own font, text color/italic, a panel background, a colored left accent bar, and an inset.
  • Page -- the journal's overall background color (e.g. a cream/parchment page), and a margin that insets the content from the page edges. When you set a light page, also set dark heading and body colors so the text reads -- the page does not auto-adjust text contrast.

You can pick a different font for headings, body, lists, quotes, and your named classes. Fonts come from the set configured for this build (book/display faces like the ones used in the printed book, plus utility faces). If you pick a font that isn't available it simply falls back to the standard face. Note: the book display faces don't include the straight typewriter apostrophe/quote, so use curly/typographic quotes in text that uses those faces, or the straight ones show as empty boxes.

You only set what you want to change. Anything you leave alone keeps inheriting -- from the parent stylesheet, or from the built-in default.

docs.title: Inheritance
docs.text:
A stylesheet can inherit from a parent. It starts as an exact copy of the parent, and any field you set overrides just that one field. This is how you keep a family of related looks in sync:

  • Make a base "House Style" stylesheet.
  • Make "House Style - Dark" that inherits from it and only overrides colors.
  • Fix a heading size on "House Style" and both update.

docs.title: Named classes
docs.text: Beyond the base skin, you can define named classes and apply them to specific pieces of text. There are two kinds.

docs.title: Inline classes -- {.name text}
docs.text:
An inline class styles a span inside a line. Define a class (e.g. emphasis) with a text color / weight / italic, then write:

The water is rising. {.emphasis Move quickly.}

Here, Move quickly. picks up the emphasis styling while the rest of the sentence stays normal. Unknown class names just render the plain text -- nothing breaks.

docs.title: Block classes -- :::name
docs.text:
A block class wraps several lines in a styled box -- perfect for read-aloud text, sidebars, or stat-block frames. Define a block class (e.g. read-aloud) with a background color, border, and padding, then fence your text:

:::read-aloud The door groans open. Dust hangs in the still air, and far below, something stirs. :::

Open the fence with ::: followed by the class name, write your lines, and close with a bare ::: on its own line.

docs.title: Buttons and embeds
docs.text:
A stylesheet can also skin a few non-text pieces:

  • Macro buttons (the clickable buttons from [[macro:...]]) take a button skin -- background, border, corners, padding, and text color/weight -- with optional hover and pressed looks.
  • Embeds and content blocks (embedded documents/monsters/maps, images, power rolls, tables, collapsible sections) can be given a frame -- background, border, and padding.

docs.title: The MCDM stylesheet
docs.text:
The MCDM stylesheet is modeled on the printed MCDM book: dark ink text on a warm parchment page, inset from the edges, with bronze-gold accents throughout. It uses the book typefaces -- a display face for the all-caps chapter title and the Newzald face for the rest of the heading hierarchy, with Berling for body text. The headings get gold underline rules (heaviest under the title, thinning down the hierarchy), the sub-heads are gold small-caps, and bullets are gold. Blockquotes render as a tan panel with a gold left accent bar. Power rolls, tables, rollable tables, and collapsible sections are all framed in gold-bordered cream boxes (tables use cream rows with a slightly darker alternating tint), and macro buttons get a matching gold-bordered tan look. It ships with two ready-to-use classes:

  • {.emphasis text} -- bronze-gold, bold inline emphasis.
  • :::read-aloud -- a gold-bordered tan callout box with dark italic text.

Assign it from the Stylesheet: dropdown to give any journal that look.

docs.title: Syntax cheat sheet
docs.text: You write You get # Title ... ###### Title Headings 1-6 - item or * item Bulleted list 1. item Numbered list {.name text} Inline class span :::name ... ::: Block class callout box > quoted Blockquote --- Divider [[macro:...]] Macro button (takes the button skin)

docs.title: Good to know (current limitations)
docs.text:
• Fonts: you can now pick a per-element font (a different face for headings vs. body, lists, quotes, and named classes), drawn from the faces configured for this build. An unavailable font falls back to the standard typeface, and the book display faces lack the straight apostrophe/quote (use curly quotes).
  • Clear to inherit: once you set a field in the editor it stays an override. To make a field inherit again, clear it via import/code (a blank number field does clear that one value).
  • Inherited classes: the class editor shows a stylesheet's own classes; to change a class it inherits from a parent, re-declare it by name.
  • Colors: the editor uses literal colors from the picker.
  • Where it applies: inline {.class} spans work in body paragraphs (not inside table cells or blockquotes), and block ::: callouts don't nest.

This page is also a demonstration: viewed with the MCDM stylesheet, its headings, bullets, the {.emphasis ...} span above, and the :::read-aloud box all render in the styled look they describe.

docs.title: Action Log redesign - design brief (DRAFT, in discovery)
docs.text: Status: Phase 1 framing signed; Phase 3 decision map next. Started 2026-10-23.

docs.title: 1. Framing
docs.text:
• Problem: when something happens that a player or the Director did not follow, they cannot find out what happened quickly. The log is hidden behind a rail button, shows a noisy stream of bespoke cards, and buries the actual outcome (who lost how much Stamina, which condition landed) in hover tooltips.
  • Example question it must answer in seconds: "I did 7 damage, why did the monster only take 5?" -> poison damage, the monster has poison immunity 2.
  • Who asked: David; Ricky raised it too. The dev team rarely refers to the log.
  • Not bound to today's form. Same spirit as the tabletop HUD, which reframed VTT play from map-first to table-first: the table holds the map and other things.
  • Personas:
  • Player who missed something ("why did I lose 14 Stamina?").
  • Director settling a dispute or recovering from a mistake ("did the mark apply?").
  • Set-and-forget player who never opens it.
  • Primary job: recall first. Full-session needs are served as outputs, not as the log's core design (see Open questions).
  • Done looks like: TBD.
  • Pillars (DRAFT, proposed 2026-10-23):
  • Outcomes first, mechanics on request.
  • Answer from where the question comes up (the creature, your hero, the round), not only from a panel. At a physical table nobody keeps a log: memory is spoken and tied to the creature and the moment.
  • Record what happened when it happened; never re-draw history from live state.

docs.title: 3. Open questions
docs.text: • Which full-session "whys" are worth an output (encounter recap, session summary to a journal, catch-up since your last turn)? Candidate list in Appendix C.

docs.title: Surface
docs.text:
• ChatPanel/ActionLogPanel.lua: DockablePanel.Register{name = "Action Log"}, a rail panel. Unread badge with a count of entries from other users since the panel was last on screen (actionlog:lastviewed per-game preference).
  • Chrome per entry: CreateActionLogCard - 40px token portrait, name, 6px colour bar (player colour, or hard-coded #AA0000 for monsters), indented 20px when "out of turn".
  • Lazy history: builds the newest 12 entries, loads 12 more on scroll to top.
  • DM-only: right-click Delete Message / Clear Chat / Hide from players; per-roll visibility eye.
  • No search, no filter, no grouping beyond cast-adoption (below).

docs.title: Data model
docs.text:
• The log is a filtered view of the chat store: every message that is not plain chat, data, object or a custom message on the "chat" channel.
  • Engine cap: ChatPanel.cs:2193 keeps only the newest 128 messages, shared with chat. One ability cast writes several messages (cast + roll + modifiers, heals, resources, notes), so a busy combat holds a few rounds at most. Full-session search is impossible on this store.
  • Entries store ids, not snapshots: names, portraits and the out-of-turn indent are read from LIVE state at render time. A deleted token makes its entries render as 0x0 (they vanish); a renamed token renames history; "out of turn" is computed against the current initiative, not the one at the time.

docs.title: What feeds it
docs.text:
Roll messages (every dice roll: power rolls, tests, damage, initiative, Dice panel, macros, roll-on-table, downtime, montage). A power roll whose castid matches a cast card is nested under it. The power-roll card is also a LIVE interaction surface: amend edge/bane after the roll, tier rows highlight, amendable rows.

17 custom card types:

Type File Shows CastActivatedAbilityChatMessage DMHub Game Rules/ActivatedAbility.lua:2886 ability name, type, "Executing...", 28px target portraits; per-target outcomes only in hover ActivatedAbilityDamageChatMessage Draw Steel Ability Behaviors/AbilityDamage.lua:454 "N type damage" - only when the content author typed a chatMessage; also squad overflow damage (MCDMCreature.lua:6224) DamageModifierChatMessage Draw Steel Core Rules/MCDMCreature.lua:5308 immunity/weakness changed a hit: shield chip, +/-N, source HealChatMessage DMHub Game Rules/AbilityReplenish.lua:147 "Regained N Stamina" ResourceChatMessage Draw Steel V/ResourceChat.lua resource gain/consume, reason, Undo button MaliceSpentChatMessage Draw Steel Core Rules/DSResources.lua:112 Malice diamond, ability, hover = ability card ActionLogNoteChatMessage DMHub Game Rules/AbilityReplenish.lua:203 title + detail for a bonus already folded into a roll ActivatedAbilityTemporaryStaminaChatMessage Draw Steel Core Rules/DSTemporaryHitpoints.lua:20 temp Stamina granted ActivatedAbilityPurgeEffectsChatMessage DMHub Game Rules/AbilityPurgeEffects.lua:24 effects removed ActivatedAbilitySaveEndsToEotChatMessage Draw Steel Core Rules/MCDMAbilitySaveBehavior.lua:834 save-ends converted to EoT TeleportChatMessage Draw Steel Ability Behaviors/AbilityTeleportToLineEnd.lua:9 teleport StartOfTurnChatMessage Draw Steel Core Rules/MCDMInitiativeBar.lua:6785 "Start of Turn" card for every turn BeginRoundChatMessage Draw Steel Core Rules/MCDMInitiativeBar.lua:6715 "Draw Steel!" / "ROUND N" banner RollInitiativeChatMessage Draw Steel UI/DSInitiativeRoll.lua:1173 initiative roll PatronsGazeChatMessage Draw Steel Acolyte/Acolyte.lua:509 Acolyte risk roll (suppresses the standard roll card) SpoilerRevealChatMessage Timeline/EmbeddedRollDialog.lua:568 Director revealed a hidden modifier AudioLogChatMessage DMHub Core Panels/Audio.lua:1014 "Now playing" / sound effects

Per-target outcomes recorded only in the cast card's portrait hover (ActivatedAbility.RecordTokenMessage, ~25 call sites): damage dealt, tier achieved, conditions applied/removed, potency resisted or not, Stamina regained, grabbed, surges lost, temp Stamina, carrier effects.

Not found in the sweep (no log entry): forced movement (push/pull/slide), conditions applied or removed outside a cast, manual Stamina edits, winded/dying/death, end of turn, end of combat, Victories, respites.

docs.title: Overlap with newer surfaces
docs.text: • Timeline/AbilitySidebar.lua + EmbeddedRollDialog.lua: the live ability card and roll dialog, with a read-only copy other players see. The log's "watch it happen" job is now largely done there.

docs.title: Dormant: the Battle Log document
docs.text:
• Draw Steel Core Rules/MCDMEncounter.lua:2661-2825: when an encounter ends, the Director's client appends a permanent record to the dsBattleLog shared document (max 200 battles): what was fought, outcome, duration, per-hero headline numbers (damage, taken, prevented, kills, downed). Its own comment calls it "the reviewable campaign history". Nothing outside the file reads it: no UI shows it.
  • The outcome screen (Draw Steel UI/DSVictoryScreen.lua) already turns per-hero stats into awarded roles at the end of combat.

docs.title: Style debt
docs.text: Hard-coded colours (#111111, #AA0000, white, #1194FF, #DE1E47), a bespoke layout per card type, 40px dice faces and 28pt totals beside 11px subtext; not on the STYLE_GUIDE row grammar.

docs.title: Appendix B - A real log, read cold (James's screenshot, 2026-10-23)
docs.text:
About nine entries fill a tall panel. Problems, in order of cost to the reader:

  1. Subject and object are ambiguous. "Orc Conduit / Roll Resistance vs Might / 10 damage; slowed (EoT)": did the Orc deal it or take it? Targets are tiny portraits on some cards and absent on others.
  2. The result line is the ability's tier text, not what happened. "5 damage" with three targets: to whom, and how much landed after immunity? Whether "slowed" applied (potency) is not shown.
  3. The biggest things on screen are the least useful: dice faces and a 28pt total. The outcome sits in small text below.
  4. Contradictions: a Free Strike marked "Aborted" still shows a roll and "6 damage"; Free Strike labelled "Main Action".
  5. Duplication: "Reactor 1 / 2 fire damage / 2 fire damage" (author text plus the automatic line).
  6. One action spreads across several cards ("Power Roll Test" card, then a separate "Power Roll Test: Power Roll" card).
  7. The colour bar is red on every entry, so it carries no information. Director-only eye icons sit in every roll.
  8. No round or turn structure is visible in a scroll of this length.

docs.title: Appendix C - Why would anyone want a full-session log? (reasoned guesses)
docs.text: Why Better served by Writing session notes or a recap A generated session summary written to a journal document "Who carried the fight" / bragging rights An encounter recap (the Battle Log record and outcome-screen stats already exist) Catching up after being away from the table or joining late "Since your last turn" catch-up, scoped to your hero Disputes about something two rounds ago Recall of the current encounter, searchable by creature Resource bookkeeping ("how many Recoveries did I spend?") The hero sheet's state, not a log Bug reports and support Developer logging; out of scope for the player-facing design

docs.title: Appendix D - Precedent scan (web, 2026-10-23)
docs.text:
Items marked [unverified] rest on search snippets only.

  • Pathfinder Kingmaker / Wrath (Owlcat): one line per action; hover lists every bonus and penalty with its source; Combat / Dialogue / Events tabs; enemy stats gated by knowledge ("?19-34"). Closest precedent for the "why". https://www.gamebanshee.com/kd8qf
  • Baldur's Gate 3: players treat the combat log's math as the source of truth when tooltips were wrong (2024). https://mein-mmo.de/baldurs-gate-3-luegt-seit-monaten-tooltips-falsch/
  • Solasta: a tooltip saying why a roll had advantage was "one of the most requested" features; without it players could not adapt their next turn. https://www.gamebanshee.com/3df88
  • Hearthstone history bar: icons for the last ~7-10 plays, blue border yours, red theirs, hover for detail. Cautionary case: an entry showed cast-time damage (20), not what landed (30). https://hearthstone.wiki.gg/wiki/History
  • Into the Breach: prevents the question by telegraphing outcomes in advance.
  • Foundry core: no search; GM export to .txt. Modules fill the gap: Chat Trimmer (combat rounds summarised, originals one click away, full-text search), Damage Log (HP changes with undo; non-owners see less; no "why"), Dice Chronicle (end-of-session stats and awards), and Draw Steel: Battle Log - a direct competitor that groups the chat by battle phase. https://foundryvtt.com/packages/draw-steel-battle-log
  • Roll20: chat persists across sessions; the Chat Archive has no search since 2019. Users: players Ctrl+F the logs "to locate details in the story". https://app.roll20.net/forum/permalink/7658843/
  • D&D Beyond Game Log: campaign-wide, cannot be cleared; complaints from 2021 to 2026.
  • Owlbear Rodeo: deliberately minimal ("Recent Rolls").

Why people want long history (evidence): finding story details later (Roll20), writing recaps (bloggers scan the roll log for rolls that changed what characters knew, chose, lost or risked), stats and awards (Foundry modules). Recap tools for absent players work from voice transcripts, not the VTT log. Weak or no evidence for streaming or AFK catch-up.

Gaps nobody fills (opportunity): 1. Dealt vs taken, with the reason ("7 dealt, 5 taken: poison immunity 2"). 2. Sessions as a unit (split, clear, recap by session). 3. Built-in search and filter. 4. Per-creature history ("what happened to this goblin"). 5. Hidden information: what detail each viewer may see. 6. Glanceable and deep together. 7. Log to recap material.

docs.title: Appendix E - Option B explored (2026-10-23, provisional)
docs.text: Mockup: https://claude.ai/artifact/UpyCsCKpcPuCcsdcrpgzXN (two panels: James's screenshot re-expressed as B, interactive; and the awkward cases). All copy in it is placeholder.

docs.title: Anatomy of an entry
docs.text:
• Head: actor portrait, actor, ability, action type, expand caret.
  • One line per target: portrait, name, condition chips (struck through when resisted), a reduction marker when immunity/weakness changed the number, net Stamina change.
  • Cost line when something was spent (Malice, Heroic Resource).
  • Triggered actions nest under the action they interrupted.
  • One click opens the detail: rolls with dice, every edge/bane and its cause, the printed tier text, per-target math ("7 damage - 2 (damage immunity 2) = 5 taken; Stamina 30 -> 25"), potency checks, movement, who rolled and when.
  • Grouped under Round and Turn headings.

docs.title: The awkward cases and how B handles them (recommendations)
docs.text: Case Handling Triggered action mid-action Nested under the interrupted action, tagged Triggered Effects with no actor (Bleeding, aura damage, save ends) Compact effect row under the turn it happened in Resource ticks (start-of-turn Heroic Resource, Malice gain) Compact row under the turn; Malice on the round heading Director's manual edits (Stamina, conditions) Compact "Director changed X" row. Not logged today Forced movement, winded, dying, killed, minions killed Chips on the target line. Not logged today Minion squad One entry for the squad Hidden creature name "Unknown creature", as today Director-hidden roll Shown only on the Director's view, marked hidden Cancelled action with no effect One muted line Tests, free dice rolls, out-of-combat play Same row grammar, outside any round Sound log (signed HoH feature, per-player opt-in) Kept as a muted compact row for those who opted in

docs.title: Tested against the needs
docs.text: Need B alone "I did 7, why did it take 5?" Yes: reduction marker at a glance, math one click away "Did the condition apply?" (Director dispute) Yes: chips, resisted ones struck through, potency in the detail "What did the monsters do while I was away?" Yes: round/turn headings plus one line per action "Why did I lose 14 Stamina?" Partly: needs a per-creature lens (search/filter category) Set-and-forget player No: needs outcomes surfaced outside the log (surface category)

docs.title: Where B strains
docs.text:
1. An entry is complete only when the action resolves: it needs an in-progress state.
  2. Nesting a trigger needs a link from the triggered cast to the one it interrupted (engine check; the roll dialog's trigger phase is the likely place).
  3. Revert Turn: entries after the checkpoint must be struck or removed.
  4. It needs a structured record per action, written when the action resolves.

docs.title: Engine reality for B
docs.text:
• The spine exists: CastActivatedAbilityChatMessage already carries castid, caster, targets, status, and per-target outcomes via RecordTokenMessage (~25 call sites), but as display strings. B makes them structured and snapshots names and portraits.
  • DamageModifierChatMessage is sent from InflictDamageInstance, which already receives symbols.cast, so the reduction can attach to its action.
  • Roll messages are separate chat messages and get pruned at 128; the detail layer must snapshot roll results into the action record rather than point at them.
  • B writes roughly one record per action where today writes three to five messages, so the same cap holds more history (a data-model decision later).

docs.title: James's reaction to the text version (2026-10-23)
docs.text:
"Easier to read, but I still see a wall of text and bounce off it." Diagnosis: - Reading is serial; a glance needs things the eye picks up without reading (faces, big numbers, icons, position). Every row was sentences at near-equal weight. - Names repeated three times per action (turn heading, actor, targets). - Every action from every round at the same level of detail. - Partly the mock: initials instead of token art, no condition icons.

Two picture-first variants added to the canvas: - B2 "pictures first": the turn heading names the actor once; each action is its ability name plus target portraits carrying the Stamina change, a condition badge (slashed when resisted) and a shield badge when immunity changed the number. Text lives only in the one-click detail. - B3 "older play folds up": as B2, but the further back, the coarser. Earlier turns fold to one line (actor, then who they hurt and by how much); earlier rounds fold to one line (who lost how much). A "New since you looked" divider marks where to start.

docs.title: Appendix F - Surface options: rail panel vs tabletop (2026-10-23)
What the tabletop offers (verified)
docs.text:
• The table is personal: maps live in windows on it; each user arranges their own table; the Director shares items with a share button (DMHub Game Hud/Tabletop.lua, dmhubclient/TABLETOP_MAP_WINDOWS.md).
  • Combat is per map: round, initiative and combat banner belong to the map's window, and several windows can each be in combat. A banner missed because no window showed the map plays when the map is next shown. Today's log is global, so two fights on two maps interleave in it.
  • Modules can put their own items on the table: Tabletop.itemKinds[kind] (available, exists, name, size, face), moved, resized and removed like NPC cards, saved per user. First user: the Audio soundboard pad.
  • Rail entries for other modules: RailEntryTypes in DocumentSystem.lua.
  • NPC/creature cards (built from the EotW hero card) and token HUDs exist.
  • Table dice are deliberately unlogged "fidget rolls": a precedent for leaving things out of the record.
  • The Director's Screen: a private band for the Director's own items.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Where it lives Reaches the set-and-forget player Fights on two maps Respects "users arrange their UI" Main risk Build S1 Rail window A window opened from the rail (today's surface, B3 content) No Needs a map filter Fully Still hidden; only opened when confused Low S2 Table item An object you lay on the table (a battle record), per user; the Director can share it Only if placed Needs a map filter Fully It is S1 with different chrome; new users never place it Low-medium (itemKinds exists) S3 On the map window A history strip on each map window, like the initiative bar: last few actions as portraits and numbers; click opens B3 Yes: it is where they already look Scoped per map by nature Partly: it adds to the window's chrome (must fold away) Takes map space; tight in small windows Medium S4 On the creature Token hover and creature/hero cards show what happened to that creature, with causes Yes, for their own hero Per creature Fully Answers creature questions only; hover needs a non-hover path Medium S5 Pushed moments Each resolved action leaves a short card on the table that settles into a history pile or strip Yes Per map if it settles on the window No: it takes attention Noise mid-turn; overlaps the ability sidebar High

docs.title: Recommendation (pending James)
docs.text: Layered, with no single "log" surface: - S3 is the glance: a per-map history strip on the map window, collapsible, whose latest turn reads like B3. - S4 answers "what happened to me / to it" on the creature itself. - B3's full view opens from either, in a window the user places (rail or table: S1 and S2 are the same view in two containers). - S5 only as a transition: the ability sidebar's live card shrinking into the strip when the action resolves, which teaches where history lives.

docs.title: Appendix G - Playable tabletop mock of the layered approach (2026-10-23)
docs.text:
Canvas board "Layered approach on the tabletop (playable)" (the canvas now opens on it): https://claude.ai/artifact/UpyCsCKpcPuCcsdcrpgzXN

Real material from the running Codex (bridge, read-only; the bridge session was told before and after): the Inn of Beginnings map window with its tokens (screenshot), the app title bar and action bar, the rail buttons, token art and condition icons copied from the image cache with assets:ResizeCachedImage, and the marble surface texture from the engine repo (Assets/Resources/Tabletop/TabletopMarble.jpg). Numbers and copy are mock.

What it shows: - S3 strip hanging from the map window's title bar (where Round 2 lives). Newest on the right, pinned next to Full log; older turns shrink, Round 1 is one chip; the oldest slide off the left edge. History in the title bar folds it away. Click an entry for the B3 detail (rolls, tier, immunity math). - S4: click any token for what happened to it this encounter, with causes. The player's hero card ("Your turn") lists what happened since their last turn (-14 Stamina). - Full view: Full log on the strip, or the rail's Action Log button, opens B3 as a window on the table. - S5 transition (Play): the ability card slides in, dice roll, Tier 2 lights, -5 with a shield and "8 - 3 immunity, pushed 2" rises over Reactor 1, then the card shrinks into the strip's newest slot and the strip makes room for it.

Open questions the mock raises: - The strip covers the top of the map: acceptable, or should it sit outside the window frame (below the title bar, on the table)? - Does the token-click history clash with the existing token click (select) and the token HUD? A hover card plus a click path may be needed. - Where does the hero card live for a player who already has the hero sheet open?

docs.title: Appendix H - James's play-test of the mock, and the code behind it (2026-10-23)
Feedback
docs.text:
1. The top of the map window is the initiative ribbon: the strip cannot hang there. Outside the map might work, but a maximized map has no "outside".
  2. Hero cards are small (132 wide) and are getting a flip-to-back: no stacking information on the face; at most a hover button that opens the log.
  3. Hovering a token shows the character panel; clicking gives the radial menu. A "history" slot in the radial for your own hero is plausible; what a player sees for a monster is an open point.
  4. The S5 fold (ability card into the history) is liked, with performance concerns.

docs.title: What the code says
docs.text:
• Map HUD: the initiative bar, and the Director's villain-action, reinforcements, cues, encounter-actions and boss bands, move into the live window's overlay at the top (Tabletop.lua PlaceMapHuds, ScaleMapHuds: full width 1180, shrinks in narrower windows). Maximized, the window's titlebar rows move into a strip hung from the app title bar and the map HUD starts below it.
  • Maximized maps sit at the bottom of the stack; journals, panel windows, NPC cards and other table items float over them. The Director's Screen is hidden while a map is maximized.
  • Table items from modules (Tabletop.itemKinds): moved, scaled and removed like NPC cards, saved per user with the layout, keyed by a string. First user: the Audio pad.
  • Action bar: bottom centre of the screen, not the map; its drawers already show the last-used ability's icon; the trigger reaction panel is bottom centre too.
  • Hero card (Codex Titlescreen/EotwHeroCard.lua): 132 x ~200. Card back (HeroCardBack.lua, Lisa, prototype on main): a 26 px hover-only flip chip at top centre (CreateFlipButton), back pages turned by footer arrows.
  • Radial menu (DMHub Token UI/TokenUI.lua:2633-2860): on a token you control, Character Sheet, Inventory and Emotes, plus the slots below. On a token you do not control there is a radial too, with one or two slots: Monster Info (when the monsterinfo setting is on) or View Portrait, and Rename (when players may rename monsters). Free angles remain.
  • Ghost animation precedent (Tabletop.lua:2374 AnimateGhost): minimizing flies one image panel (think every 0.01 s, about 0.26 s) and destroys it; the real window collapses at once. No live panel tree is animated.
  • Turn Rewind (MCDMInitiativeBar.lua:411-1440, prototype, on by default): while you play your turn it keeps checkpoints before and after each ability and move, with a plain-text list of what happened between them (Turn History dialog, /rewind). Local to the acting client and that turn only. Opportunity: "rewind to before this" from your own entries.
  • Hero sheet performance rules (build plan, round 3): no per-frame work while idle, push not rebuild, frost on one surface only. The log should meet the same bar.

docs.title: Appendix I - Revised layered design after the play-test (proposal, 2026-10-23)
Where the glance layer lives (open: James to pick)
docs.text:
P1 History tray (table item) P2 Under the map window P3 On the initiative ribbon What A compact B3 strip as a table item (Tabletop.itemKinds), showing the live map's combat Hangs from the window's bottom edge, outside the frame Each creature's ribbon entry gets an outcome badge; hover or click shows its turn Maximized map Floats over it, like cards and journals do No outside: needs a second home (screen bottom-left) Comes along: the ribbon moves with the map HUD Covers the ribbon or map Only where the user puts it No Adds to the ribbon's crowding Users arrange their UI Yes: move, scale, put away; default spot in the built-in Views Fixed to the window Fixed Out of combat (tests, rolls) Yes Yes No ribbon out of combat Build Low to medium (item kinds exist) Medium, two homes Medium; touches a busy file

Recommendation: P1. One home whatever the window does, no new map chrome, and it follows the rail philosophy. P3's idea (history keyed to turn order) is worth keeping as the tray's own grouping, which already runs by turn.

docs.title: Per creature
docs.text:
• Radial: a History slot on any token you can see. Your own hero: yes. A monster: open question; recommendation: the events players already saw (no hidden numbers), with Stamina only as Monster Knowledge allows.
  • Table cards: a hover chip beside the flip chip, opening the same creature history. Nothing added to the card's face.
  • Both open one creature-history popover; "See all" opens the full log filtered to that creature.

docs.title: The S5 fold, built cheaply
docs.text: As the Tabletop's minimize does: the ability sidebar closes as it does today, and a single small ghost (the tray entry's look: two faces and a number, 3-4 panels) flies to the tray slot in about 0.3 s, then the real entry is appended (never a rebuild). No fold when the tray is not on screen; reduce-motion turns it off. Budget: under 0.5 ms CPU a frame during the fold, nothing while idle.

docs.title: Appendix J - P1 mock (2026-10-23)
docs.text: Canvas board "P1: History tray on the table (playable)"; the canvas opens on it. The earlier strip board is kept, marked superseded. - History tray: a table item at the left of the table (hover titlebar with close, corner grips), B3 inside: Round 1 folded, earlier turns folded to one line, the latest turn open with picture rows; click any turn or action for its detail. "Full log" grows the same item to full height with every turn open. The rail's chat-bubble button puts the tray on or off the table. - Radial: click any token. The History slot (gold, top) sits beside the real slots: Character Sheet, Inventory, Emotes, View Portrait on your own hero; Monster Info on a monster; View Portrait on another hero. It opens the creature's history; "Show only them in History" filters the tray to that creature. - Hero cards (132 x 192): a History chip (gold, top left) shows on hover beside the flip chip; nothing added to the face. - S5 fold: Play runs Dwarf Fury's Brutal Slam; the ability card closes as today and a small stand-in (two faces and -5) flies into the tray's newest slot, then the entry appears and the previous turn folds. No fold when the tray is off the table, filtered or grown to the full log. - Monster history shows Healthy / Winded rather than numbers, to illustrate the Monster Knowledge rule (open question).

docs.title: Appendix K - Every case in the P1 tray (2026-10-23)
docs.text: Canvas board "P1 tray: every case, Director or player view" (the canvas opens on it): four trays side by side. Switch Director / Player in the board's Tweaks (viewer).

docs.title: Row grammar it settles (proposal)
docs.text:
• Action row, glance: ability name, then chips for what shaped the roll, then the targets (face, net number, condition badge, one or two captions).
  • Chips: Edge / Double edge (green, up triangles), Bane / Double bane (red, down triangles), Cancel out (muted), surges (gold, with what they bought), Heroic Resource cost (blue diamond), Malice (red diamond), Critical (gold fill), and neutral chips for Rerolled, Changed after the roll, +N from an ally.
  • Captions under a face: Push N / Teleported N / Collision, Immunity -N, Fire weakness +N, N soaked by temp, Resisted, Winded (amber), Dying (red), Killed and N of M killed (red fill), Spent a Recovery, Ended X.
  • Numbers: damage red, healing green, temporary Stamina blue.
  • Action row, detail: Power roll (dice + characteristic + edges), the edge/bane line naming each source and the tier change, the printed tier text (italic), surges and what they bought, per-target math, cost, movement, who rolled and when.
  • Compact rows for everything without an action: resource ticks (with the hero's face), start/end-of-turn effects, saving throws (end of turn), auras, Director hand edits, hidden rolls (hatched, Director only), dice, tables, class roll cards, sound.
  • Banners: Draw Steel! with initiative, Combat ended with a link to the victory screen.
  • Undo and revert: the undone row or the reverted turn stays, struck through, under a "Director reverted..." row.
  • Out of combat: tests, montage and negotiation rows end in a result chip instead of target faces.

docs.title: Player view differences
docs.text: Hidden rolls disappear; a hidden monster shows as "Unknown creature" with a dark face; monster Stamina numbers become Winded / Killed; Malice totals are kept (players already see what Malice bought).

docs.title: Rules checked (ClaudeRefHeroes.lua and draw-steel-rules memory)
docs.text: Edges +2, double edge or bane = one tier, edge and bane cancel; natural 19-20 = Tier 3 and a critical (another main action) on a main action; surges: up to 3 for extra damage equal to the highest characteristic each, or 2 for +1 potency on one target; cover = bane, high ground and flanking = edge; prone = edge for melee against it; Weakened = bane on power rolls; Bleeding = 1d6 + level on a main action; saving throws at end of turn, d10, 6+.

docs.title: Not yet shown
docs.text: Several creatures' triggered actions on one roll (a stack), a roll with several damage types, an ability that hits allies and enemies alike, and a long minion squad fight.

docs.title: Appendix L - Shareable P1 prototype (2026-10-23)
docs.text:
Standalone link for reviewers: https://claude.ai/artifact/UPWo9XvYuaDiZ388xRES35 (private until James shares it). The design canvas (UpyCsCKpcPuCcsdcrpgzXN) opens on its P1 board again, so the link already sent still shows P1.

A two-round encounter on the Inn of Beginnings, from James's view (Dwarf Fury), with a "View as" control for the Director. The tray folds Round 1 and earlier Round 2 turns; everything unfolds, and every action opens its detail. It folds in the catalogue cases plus the four that were missing: 1. A trigger stack on one roll: numbered rows under the action, in resolution order, tagged Before the roll / After the roll / Free (Zakaarior's bane, the Censor's 3 holy, the Null's Discipline +1). 2. Several damage types in one hit: the caption reads "6 fire, 4 cold" and "Fire immunity -3"; the detail does the math per type. 3. An ability that hits allies and enemies: foes first, then an amber "Ally hit" group, plus a "Hit an ally" chip. 4. A minion squad across turns: one face for the squad, "2 of 4 killed", then "Squad destroyed". Also: edge, double edge, bane, surges for damage and for potency, Malice costs, an ally bonus, conditions applied and resisted, winded, a hidden roll (Director view only), and monster Stamina as Healthy/Winded for players. The demo's roll card carries the roll dialog's edge/bane bar (BANE BANE X EDGE EDGE with chevrons) and surge bolts, lighting the double edge, the tier jump and two spent surges before the card closes and the stand-in flies into the tray.

docs.title: Appendix M - Ricky's feedback, triaged (agreed by James 2026-10-24, with the change below)
docs.text: Ricky (dev, has thought about the log for a while) reviewed the P1 prototype. A data point, not a direction. He liked the roll moving into the log and the fold-and-drill.

docs.title: Proposed rule: the glance budget
docs.text: The glance line shows only what changed the outcome or spent something: who, the ability, the tier, edges and banes, surges, costs, a critical, the net number per target, conditions (applied, resisted, immune), a state change (winded, dying, killed) and movement distance. Everything that explains how (sources, flat modifiers, per-target edge lists, paths, rolls) lives in the detail. Exceptions earn a place on the glance line only when they differ between targets.

docs.title: Verdicts
docs.text:
# Ricky's point Verdict Where 1 Show why surges came (banked vs granted by e.g. Trained Assassin) Include Detail: each surge's source, and "lost if unused" (the roll dialog already knows this, EmbeddedRollDialog.lua:3747) 2 Show roll modifiers (e.g. +1 rolled damage on Fire abilities) Include Detail only: already inside the number; a chip each would crowd the line 3 Different tiers per target (edges/banes per target; minion squads) Include Glance: per-target tier only when targets differ; detail lists each target's edges and banes (per-target boons exist, EmbeddedRollDialog.lua:1668) 4 Tier at a glance Include One tier badge per action (the roll card's <=11 / 12-16 / 17+ badge); per-target badges only when they differ 5 Minion squads attacking Include Caption "2 minions" on each target when they differ; detail per minion 6 Forced movement shown as a path, falls Include, on hover Caption "Push 3, fell 10"; hovering it (or clicking, for a non-hover path) shows the side-on movement cross-section the targeting tooltip already draws (MovementCrossSection.cs, dmhub.SetMovementCrossSection, MOVEMENT_CROSS_SECTION_REFERENCE.md), with its red collision and fall badges. James 2026-10-24. Needs the path stored at the time and a way to rebuild it for the renderer (engine check) 7 Turn numbers ("look at turn 15") Include A small number on each turn heading; round headings stay 8 Turn auto-populates Main / Maneuver / Move slots, colour coded, collapse after 30 s Partial Three small action pips on the current turn's heading only, filled as used. No empty placeholder rows. Turns fold when the next turn starts, not on a timer (a timer moves rows under the reader). Colour only alongside text 9 Saving throws and condition ends, with the cause (save, end of turn, Healing Grace) Include A row each; the creature's history shows applied and ended. Not recorded today 10 Target deaths Include Already: Killed caption; a row when death comes outside an action (Bleeding) 11 Trigger consistency (Tactician's mark +4 damage, Talent's Feedback Loop source) Include, as a rule Every triggered or free effect sits under the action that set it off and names it. Engine work: link a triggered cast to its cause 12 Condition immunity when a condition is inflicted Include Struck condition badge with an "Immune" caption, the same grammar as resisted 13 Always open vs open when needed (Matt, Ricky: always; Lisa: hide by default, players found the old one confusing) Both, via defaults The tray is a table item; the built-in Views decide the default. Proposal: on for the Director, one click for players. Defaults category

New persona: the always-on follower (Matt, Ricky): keeps it open and glances at it between turns. The tray's fold-by-age already serves them.

Kept out on purpose: flat modifiers on the glance line, empty placeholder rows, timers, paths shown by default, per-target edge lists on the glance line.

docs.title: Appendix N - Prototype round 2: Ricky's points folded in (2026-10-24)
docs.text: Same link (https://claude.ai/artifact/UPWo9XvYuaDiZ388xRES35), now 13 turns over two rounds. - Turn numbers on every turn (folded and open); round headings stay. - Fold by age, one level more: the compact tray shows Round 1 as one line, Round 2's turns 5-9 as one "Turns 5-9" line, then turns 10-12 one line each, then the current turn open. Full log opens everything. - Current turn heading carries Main / Maneuver / Move markers (Move used; Main fills when Play resolves the Brutal Slam). - Tier badge on every action line (the roll card's <=11 / 12-16 / 17+); per-target tier badges only where targets differ (turn 6: Orc and Null Tier 2, the Fury Tier 1 because of cover). - Minion squad attacking: "2 minions" / "1 minion" under each target (turn 2). - Surge sources in the detail (turn 10: 1 banked, 1 from Trained Assassin, lost if unused); roll bonus in the detail (turn 11: +1 rolled damage on Fire abilities). - Saves and condition ends: the Null's end-of-turn save (turn 7), Slowed ending at end of turn (turn 9), Grabbed ended by Healing Grace (turn 9) and by the grabber being pushed away (turn 12). - Trigger causes: the Tactician's Mark +4 nested under the Shadow's strike that set it off (turn 10); death shown as Killed. - Condition immunity: Frightened struck through with "Immune: frightened" (turn 12). - Forced movement: "Push 3 · fell 4" (turn 12) shows the side-on cross-section on hover (click pins it), modelled on the targeting tooltip: ground silhouette on the tile grid, pusher and mover, blue push arrow, red fall arrow, landing ghost with a red -6 fall badge.

docs.title: Appendix O - Play runs two turns and a round change (2026-10-24)
docs.text: Play on the prototype now runs about 16 seconds: 1. Turn 13, Dwarf Fury: Brutal Slam (double edge, two surges) as before; the card closes and its stand-in folds into the tray; Main fills on the turn heading. 2. Turn 14, Reactor 1 (enemy): the turn heading appears and turn 13 folds to one line; the read-only roll card a player sees while the Director rolls; the Troubadour's trigger arrives before the roll (blue ring on the Troubadour, a "Triggered" strip on the card, BANE lights); 13 - 2 = 11, Tier 1; -4 fire rises over the Fury and the Elementalist; the Fury's hero card flashes red (the EotW card's hurt wash) and drops to 9 / 33; the stand-in folds the attack, with the trigger nested, into the tray. 3. Round 3: Round 2 folds to one line, the Round 3 heading shows the Malice gain, and the Troubadour's turn opens with Drama +2. The "Turns a-b" group grows as turns pass (5-9, then 5-10): fold by age, live.

docs.title: Appendix P - "Not there yet" (James, 2026-10-25)
docs.text: After the longer Play: better than today, but hard to parse what was going on, and "something about the design doesn't sit right". James's read: we may be tied to what an action log is in the current system and in other games, without having settled what it means for the Codex and Draw Steel. Re-opening the framing through an interview (candidate reframes in the session, not yet in the brief).

docs.title: Interview, round 1 (James, 2026-10-25)
docs.text:
• Real questions at the table: "What just happened? Where did that damage come from? Why am I slowed?" Worst with collision and forced-movement damage, triggers and auras. The answer is in today's log, but clicking in to get it is part of the problem. People open the log or ask the Director.
  • The longer Play was hard to parse: matching tray entries to tokens, a lot happening at once, and telling prototype pieces from today's interface.
  • Ideal in one sentence: "The Codex is great, it's clear what's happening and if I ever miss anything, the action log catches me up in no time, I can even get a blow by blow if I need it."
  • Reframes: A partly (the answer at the thing that changed, but order of events still matters); some B (the enemy turn); C on theme for cinematic moments; D cool but too slow; E solved elsewhere.
  • The cross-section on hover was not discoverable.

docs.title: Code check
docs.text: When damage lands, the token floats only the number (DMHub Token UI/TokenUI.lua:2150, red floatlabel), though the damage entry already carries its type (including collide and fall) and the attacker id (used for the hit sound).

docs.title: Emerging hypothesis (to test with James)
docs.text: Three layers, of which we have only designed the third: 1. In the moment: the effect names its cause where it lands ("-2 collision", "-3 aura", "Slowed: Power Roll Test"). Prevents most questions; the data already exists. 2. Catch-up: the tray answers "what happened since I last looked", in order, folded, with cinematic moments marked. 3. Blow by blow: the detail one click away. Tying them together: hovering an entry lights its tokens on the map (and the reverse). Draw Steel angle: much of what hits you is indirect (forced movement, collisions, falls, triggers, auras, ongoing effects), often on someone else's turn; making the indirect visible is the Codex's job here. Anything with more to show (the cross-section) needs a visible cue, not hover on text.

docs.title: Interview, round 2 (James, 2026-10-25)
docs.text:
• The three-layer reading is not the whole answer: "something else is still nagging".
  • Causes on the map: clutter is a real concern; a turn can have a lot of damage flying around. Sound effects per damage type already help. A reason might help, but carefully.
  • When people need catching up: when they weren't paying attention, not at a game phase: someone came into the room, they were reading something else, they went to the toilet.
  • Cinematic moments: tokens already show visual effects; marking them in the history is an event row, and the map shows it. The list so far covers the moments James can think of.

docs.title: Interview, round 3 (James, 2026-10-25)
docs.text:
• "Welcome back" card: asked how we would know the user wasn't there.
  • "Told, not decoded": interesting; math-focused groups may find it harder to parse, but with the blow-by-blow behind it, it could work.
  • "One place" (live card and history as one strip): no. The Codex works hard to keep the play space clear: only what players and Directors put there, plus what is needed when it is needed (the roll dialog appears only as needed).
  • "Your story first": no. A tactical game about synergising with teammates.

docs.title: Finding: the Codex already remembers state on the things themselves
docs.text:
• StatHistory (DMHub Game Rules/Creature.lua:22-120): each creature keeps its last 8 changes to Stamina, temporary Stamina, max Stamina, Heroic Resource, surges and other resources: the note (cause), resulting value, who, when, disposition, attacker. Synced with the creature.
  • Shown on hover: the character panel's Stamina bar shows the Stamina history tooltip (MCDMCharacterPanel.lua:5313, gui.StatsHistoryTooltip); table trackers (Malice, hero medallions, counters) show their change history in a tooltip (TableDice.lua:2617-2660).
  • Ongoing effects record who applied them (casterInfo.tokenid, OngoingEffect.lua:384).
  • Absence: the engine tracks app focus (Application.isFocused, InputController's background throttle; frame-time windows count focusedSeconds) but exposes no plain Lua field for focus or input idle time. Small engine addition. It cannot tell "looking at the screen but talking"; the new-since-you-looked marker and an on-demand button cover that.

docs.title: Candidate reframe (to test)
docs.text: Not a log, but memory on the things: every piece of state on the table (Stamina, conditions, resources, Malice, trackers) remembers its own recent story and shows it when you look at it. The History tray is those memories woven into time order, for catching up and the blow by blow. Builds on systems that exist instead of a separate log store.

docs.title: Interview, round 4 (James, 2026-10-26)
docs.text:
• The conversation drifted away from the prototype; the latest prototype is the much better direction, though still visually confusing.
  • The real questions: on a table people control, how do they know there is something in the history, and how do they bring it up fast? Idea: the minimized block (as other tabletop HUD pieces) gets a small notification.
  • Keep: the timeline power roll folding into the history (a great indicator); search.
  • "Why am I slowed?": people hover the condition on their token (it shows who applied it and with what), or open the log. Few know the Stamina history hover exists, and it only answers about your own creature; only the Director sees everything. Splitting history across many places segments it.
  • Idle detection is unreliable (reading a phone at the desk). "Since your last turn" is more promising.
  • Replay and rewind: interesting, but performance worries on older laptops (Transparent UI off, lowered settings); nobody should be locked out.
  • Wants the missing piece that ties it together into an "oh, I understand" moment.

docs.title: Appendix Q - What players actually report (in-app feedback, 2026-10-26)
docs.text: Searched 2,085 feedback tickets (titles and triage areas; full text for the 12 most relevant), read-only via the bug-fix scripts. 1. The log is the source of truth, so it must show what landed. - FRAKESH6: "action log shows the wrong damage when orc conduit uses their trigger to give double edge" (rolled 7, the trigger made it 12, the log showed 7 and 9 damage). - XP78F954: "I didn't get a second main action after my crit despite the log saying I would." - D2HJ593U: the dice showed 1, the log showed 2. J6JDYWGT: a double bane still logged Tier 3. - XJNFC7VA: a player reports a bug citing "you can see the roll in the action log": players use it as evidence. 2. Getting to it in the rail era. - 7M3H2C59: "I can't pull up my Action Log." Pop-out bugs: 4FJ5VYME, K6H9J536, ZDNC938Z, Y4AGUAW5. - AM79CDYV: "Action Log and Chat windows always have a red dot on them." A notice that is always on means nothing. 3. Completeness and teammates' results. - P94P9TDZ: "Missing 2 players rolls in the action log." JVDB4DH4: "My action log is not updating." 985MMSPH: "Can't see other players result on Presence Test." 4. "Why" questions beyond damage. - M4QPGE2V: "Why did I get my Maneuver back?" XJNFC7VA: Drama gained on a roll that was not a natural 19. 47Y6C8ET: "I don't really know what happened when I used Dramatic Reversal." 5. Noise: MYEJSNWK: "Provide a way to clear the action log. There is a bunch of junk in there from my players experimenting." 6. Hidden information: 48NDEWA9: the Draw Steel banner listed monsters still hidden. No GitHub issues in VerisimLLC mention the action log.

docs.title: Interview, round 5 (James, 2026-10-26)
docs.text:
• Not the roll card: the timeline roll card is not in its final form, and it does not show everything that influenced a roll. Edges and banes cap at a double and cancel each other: 3 edges and 1 bane show only as a double edge, and the player never learns there were 3 edges. People go to the action log for that; the history detail must show it.
  • The prototype's expanded detail is not as readable or quick to parse as it should be; possibly just prototype finish, but it needs work.
  • "Since your last turn": torn. It assumes how a player will use it. Player types (Robin D. Laws' archetypes: tactician, storyteller, casual and the rest) all play Draw Steel in the Codex; a round-up serves one or two of them. If we cannot tell what a player cares about and serve the wrong thing, they dig anyway and it is no better than today.
  • Conclusion: the latest prototype was closer; it may need better presentation and more functionality rather than a new concept.
  • Search terms people would use: creature names, ability names, conditions ("slowed" shows why you are slowed). Not "turn 15".
  • Turn numbers: James is not sold (order of turns rarely matters to him), but he is one player type; open.

docs.title: Persona lens update
docs.text: Design for Robin D. Laws' player types rather than a single "player": Power Gamer, Butt-Kicker, Tactician, Specialist, Method Actor, Storyteller, Casual Gamer. Each pulls a different layer: glance (Casual, Butt-Kicker), the roll's full arithmetic (Power Gamer, Tactician), search (Specialist, Tactician), cinematic moments (Storyteller, Butt-Kicker). Principle: let each pull what they want fast, rather than guessing and pushing a summary.

docs.title: Appendix R - What players say in public (web research, 2026-10-26)
docs.text:
Sources: r/drawsteel (all Codex posts Jan-Oct 2026 via the Arctic Shift archive, comments on ~25 threads), ~39 Steam reviews and Steam discussions, EN World. Quotes paraphrased except one; links in the session report. Some Steam reviewers and Reddit posters are testers or team-adjacent.

Themes (independent sources): - Can't tell what the automation did or why: ~10. zupancia (23 Oct, regrets choosing the Codex over Foundry): "Every session we have problems figuring out what the automations have done and why." Also: is that right or a bug; a Null "pinballing" around the map leaves a new Director asking what happened; stability and conditions applied without explanation. - The log is too thin for the why: ~5 plus the team's own acknowledgement. Triggers fired without anyone knowing which event they answered; a Recovery spent from a prompt nobody could trace (HornScrub, 1 Sep). "See why a roll hit tier 3 and what made up the final damage" (ThrowbackPie, 9 Jan). Codex team (10 Jan): plans for a more complete log with references on everything. - Collapsing into one damage total felt less impactful than seeing the forced-movement- into-a-wall maths (johnleeuk21, 9 Jan): clarity and drama. - Trigger prompts fleeting or hard to source: ~6. Whose step is next in multi-actor resolution (Dramatic Reversal): ~3. - Requests: inventory changes in the log ("bookkeeping game changer"). - Praise: conditions clear on tokens, initiative greys out who acted, minion grouping, allies' trigger prompts help table talk, rewind, less bookkeeping: ~12. - Not found: complaints about Malice or the Director's turn; YouTube and other socials had nothing indexed.

Read: the strongest public pain is the why, especially for triggers and composite damage. It touches retention (a group considering moving to Foundry).

docs.title: Appendix S - Readable detail: proposal (2026-10-26, awaiting James)
docs.text:
Board "Expanded detail: three layouts" on the prototype link (image: detail-options.png). One roll opened three ways: Dwarf Fury's Brutal Slam, three edges (flanking with Zakaarior, target prone, high ground) and one bane (Reactor 1's trigger when targeted) netting to one edge: 7 + 2 + 2 = 11, Tier 1; then two surges and damage immunity 2: 7 taken.

Rules note: three edges and one bane net to a single edge, not a double edge (edges count up to two; one bane cancels one). The code agrees (MCDMAbilityRollBehavior.lua:80, GetRollModFromEdgesAndBanes). That is the case the detail must explain: the player saw three reasons for an edge and got Tier 1.

Options: - A. Receipt (recommended): two sums (power roll, then each target's damage) in the order they happened, one fact per line, every number in one right-hand column, each edge and bane named under the line it changed, with who or what granted it (face or icon). Familiar maths for Power Gamers and Tacticians; the right column scans in a second. Taller than today's grid. - B. Sum line: each sum on one line of chips; sources wait behind a hover. Shortest, but it repeats the roll card's problem (the net hides the sources until you dig) and hover is weak on touch and for people who do not know to try it. - C. Pictures: the roll dialog's edge/bane bar, a tier track showing how close the roll came, the damage as a bar. Most visual; most to build; grows tall with several targets.

Rules for any layout (the finish James asked for): - The detail uses the tray's full width, not the indent under the turn face. - Body text 14-15px; one fact per line; numbers in tabular figures in one column. - Order of resolution: roll, edges and banes, tier, then per target, then cost and who. - A trigger sits at the point in the chain where it fired and says what set it off ("when targeted", "after the roll"), answering "which event did it respond to". - When a cancelled or capped source changed the tier, one muted line says what it would have been ("Without the bane: double edge, Tier 2"). Only then. - Same symbols as the roll dialog: chevrons for edges and banes, the surge bolt.

Engine check: a stored roll keeps only the net counts (boons, banes, and per-target offsets in multitargets; CalculateMultitargetsFromRollProperties caps each at two). The roll dialog knows each named source at roll time (m_activeModifiers, snapshotted per target as modifiersUsed, EmbeddedRollDialog.lua:5642), and edges added with the dialog's own +/- buttons have no source. Showing sources means writing a small list (source name, edge or bane, from whom, before or after the roll) into the roll when it is accepted, plus a "set by hand" entry for the buttons.

docs.title: In play (2026-10-26)
docs.text: James asked to see the three layouts in play. The prototype link now has a "Detail layout" switch (A receipt / B sum line / C pictures) in its controls, applying to every action's detail in the tray, plus "Open the Brutal Slam" after Play. - Play: the Fury's roll card starts on a double edge (three edges); Reactor 1's trigger fires when targeted (blue ring, "Triggered" strip) and the bar drops to one edge; 4 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 11, Tier 1; two surges; 7 taken after damage immunity 2. - Every action's detail is now structured data (roll, edge/bane sources, per-target sums, triggers, costs) read by all three layouts, so the comparison holds across the tray: per-target cover bane (turn 6), two damage types with a bonus and fire immunity (turn 11), surge sources and a triggered Mark (turn 10), a bane that cost a tier (turn 14), healing (turn 9), a fall (turn 12). - Scenario changes for consistency: Reactor 1 has damage immunity 2 (so turn 7 deals 4) and was knocked prone in turn 7 (the prone edge's source); turn 11's two-type hit moved to Test Monster Z 1 (fire immunity 3).

docs.title: James's play of the three layouts (2026-10-26)
docs.text:
• The layering confuses: the action row is indented, but its detail folds out unindented (my full-width rule), so it is hard to tell whether there is more to expand, or where one row's detail ends and the next row begins.
  • All three layouts were hard to parse; it was hard to understand what had happened. Read: two problems. Structure: the detail has no container of its own, and the tray now has five nested levels (round, turn, action, detail, target) in 410px, with one signifier (a caret) doing two jobs. Content: every layout opens on arithmetic, not on what happened and why; the reader has to work the story out of the sums. Proposal (awaiting James): a detail card beside the tray instead of folding inline; the card opens on what happened, then why (each thing that changed the result, phrased as a contrast: "Tier 1, not Tier 2: ..."), then the numbers as a receipt.

docs.title: Built: the detail card (2026-10-26)
docs.text: Same prototype link. Clicking an action row (chevron on the right) opens its card beside the tray; the tray keeps its shape and the row stays highlighted. Carets on the left only fold. The card: header (actor, ability, action type, round and turn, close), What happened (one sentence per creature, with face and number), Why (each change to the result as a contrast; "a straight roll" when nothing changed it; the fall line shows the side view on hover), The numbers (the receipt), who rolled and when. The A/B/C switch and layouts B and C are gone; the static comparison board stays on the canvas as a record. All 14 actions have What happened and Why copy, placeholder until signed off. Known gap: "Open the Brutal Slam" opens the card but does not scroll the tray to its row.

docs.title: Appendix T - What it takes to build (feasibility, 2026-10-26)
docs.text: James: the History tray with the detail card is the direction; with search, and the token and hero-card history showing the same detail, it solves the problem. Question: how much works with today's code, and what has to change.

docs.title: Works today (UI work only, the data already exists)
docs.text:
• The tray as a table item and a rail toggle: Tabletop.itemKinds (the Audio pad is the precedent).
  • History from a token: the radial menu exists on tokens you control and on tokens you do not (DMHub Token UI/TokenUI.lua:2633-2860, free angles left).
  • History from a hero card: hover chips, as the flip chip does (Codex Titlescreen/EotwHeroCard.lua).
  • The roll card folding into the tray: one-image ghost, as AnimateGhost does (Tabletop.lua:2374).
  • Round and turn grouping: the round is readable when an event happens (dmhub.initiativeQueue.round); turn starts are already logged.
  • Roll facts: dice, total, net edges and banes, tier, per-target edge/bane offsets are on the roll (boons, banes, multitargets); a power roll links to its cast by castid.
  • Immunity and weakness: the damage code already works out the amount, rating, damage type, source name, attacker and ability (InflictDamageInstance, MCDMCreature.lua:5590-5660), and how much temporary Stamina soaked.
  • Search, filters and the player view: client-side over the records; hidden rolls are flagged, hidden tokens and monster Stamina are known.

docs.title: Codex changes (known in the moment, not kept today)
docs.text:
1. One history record per action. Today the per-target results are display strings (RecordTokenMessage, 29 call sites, e.g. "9 untyped damage", "Tier 3 (...)") inside the cast card, and names and portraits are read live (renames and deletions rewrite history). Start the record in ActivatedAbility:Cast (ActivatedAbility.lua:3133, the one funnel every ability goes through, with castid, caster and targets) and fill it as the cast resolves: per target, the damage steps (tier damage, surges, bonuses, immunity or weakness, temp Stamina, final), conditions (applied, resisted with potency, immune), movement, state changes. Snapshot names and portraits. The largest piece.
  2. Edge and bane sources: the roll dialog knows each named source (m_activeModifiers, modifiersUsed per target, EmbeddedRollDialog.lua:5642); save the list on the record when the roll is accepted, plus "set by hand" for the dialog's +/- buttons.
  3. Damage bonuses and surge sources: from the same modifiers (e.g. "+1 rolled damage on Fire abilities"); banked surges vs a feature's surges lost if unused (the dialog already knows this, Appendix M).
  4. Trigger causes. Ability-use triggers already receive the cast that set them off (symbols.cast, TriggeredAbility.lua:1545); reactions to attacked, damaged, collide and similar events get the attacker but no cast id (e.g. the "attacked" event, ActivatedAbility.lua:3986). Add the resolving cast's id to event info and stamp each triggered cast with its event, triggering creature and cast, so it nests under its cause. Triggers that add an edge or bane already appear as named roll modifiers.
  5. Conditions ending, with the cause: not logged today. creature:RemoveOngoingEffect is central (Creature.lua:7687); callers pass why (end of turn, save, an ability, the grabber moved away).
  6. Forced movement, collisions and falls: not logged today. Record distance, collisions, fall and collision damage, and the path (LuaPath:Serialize()).
  7. Winded, dying and death, and the Director's manual Stamina edits: not logged today (Stamina history keeps the last 8 per creature, too short to rebuild from).
  8. The card's words: a sentence builder that turns a record into "What happened" lines and "Why" contrasts (one template per outcome type). All wording needs James's sign-off.
  9. Storage: the chat store keeps only the newest 128 messages, shared with chat (ChatPanel.cs:2193), so a history long enough to search cannot live there. Put records in a shared document per encounter (the dormant dsBattleLog document is the precedent), keep the current and previous encounters, and decide what Revert Turn does: register the document for checkpoints (entries roll back with the board) or mark entries reverted (the struck-through rows the catalogue shows).

docs.title: Engine checks and small engine work
docs.text:
• Document limits: confirm a per-encounter document of a few hundred records, written on every action, is within size and write-rate limits.
  • Cross-section from history: dmhub.SetMovementCrossSection takes a live token and a path, and draws today's terrain from the token's current position. Needs a way to build a LuaPath from saved data (it has Deserialize, but Lua has no way to make an empty one) and a start-position argument.
  • Optional: the attack cross-section (dmhub.SetAttackCrossSection) could show why cover gave a bane, but it reads current positions; history would need stored positions.

docs.title: Still to design
docs.text: Search (where the box lives, what it matches, how results show), the minimized tray's notification, whether players can open a monster's history, the record's wording, turn numbers.

docs.title: Appendix U - Search: proposal (2026-10-26, awaiting James)
docs.text:
Needs it serves: "why am I slowed? just type slowed"; creature names, ability names, conditions (round 5); the creature filter from the radial and hero card is the same job. Lesson from the Stamina history hover: few people find what is hidden, so search is not.

  1. Where: a search field always visible in the tray header, beside Full log. Not behind an icon.
  2. What it matches, live as you type: creature names (who acted, who was hit, who triggered), ability names, conditions (applied, resisted, immune, ended), damage types, and outcome words (killed, winded, dying, pushed, fell, collision, triggered, surge, Malice, critical). Not dice or turn numbers.
  3. Suggestions while typing, grouped (Creatures, Abilities, Conditions, Other) with faces and icons. Picking one makes a chip; chips combine ("Dwarf Fury" + "Slowed" = when the Fury was slowed). The radial's and hero card's History open the tray with that creature's chip, so there is one filter, not two. Free text still matches anything.
  4. Results (the fork): filter in place, recommended. The tray shows only matching actions, still under their round and turn headings, unfolded, with the match highlighted and a count; clicking one opens the detail card as now, the matching line marked. Alternative: a flat list of result sentences replacing the tray, each jumping to its place.
  5. Active now: a match whose effect is still on (Slowed until end of turn) gets an "Active" tag, so "slowed" answers why you are slowed today, not only that you were.
  6. Scope: what the tray holds (this encounter and the previous one); results from the previous encounter group under its own heading.
  7. Player view: search never reveals what the player cannot see (hidden creatures stay "Unknown creature" and do not match by name; hidden rolls do not match). Wording below for sign-off (placeholder until then).

docs.title: Built: search (2026-10-26)
docs.text: Same prototype link. A search field under the tray header ("Search creatures, abilities, conditions"). Typing filters live and shows suggestions grouped as Creatures, Abilities, Conditions and Other, ranked by names that start with what was typed, each with its match count; Enter or a click makes a chip, Backspace on an empty field removes the last one. Results filter the tray in place under their rounds and turns, unfolded, with a count; matching names, abilities and condition badges are marked; conditions still on carry "Active"; the detail card marks the matching lines. With a creature chip, a condition chip means that creature got (or gave) it, so "Dwarf Fury" + "Slowed" finds only the Reactor Pulse. History on a token's radial or a hero card opens the tray with that creature's chip (the creature popover is gone). Scenario change so "why am I slowed?" has an answer: Reactor Pulse now slows (save ends) on R<1; the Fury is slowed (Active), the Elementalist resists. The previous-encounter scope is not shown: the mock has one encounter. James, after playing it: "yep i like it" (2026-10-26).

docs.title: Appendix V - The minimised tray and its notification: proposal (2026-10-26, awaiting James)
docs.text:
Code today: windows minimise into a 40 px button floating on the table or docked on the icon rail (Tabletop.lua 2329-2740; other files' windows use Tabletop.MinimizeExternal, the PDF viewer is the precedent). The button already takes a badge (buttonOps.badge {icon, color} with badgeShown; a map window shows a red sword while in combat) and a hover preview (buttonOps.hover). Table items do not minimise. The current log's rail marker counts every message from anyone else since the panel was last on screen (ActionLogPanel.lua:43), so in combat it is always on (ticket AM79CDYV).

Proposal: - The block: History minimises like any window, into the standard 40 px button (floating or docked on the rail), with the History icon. Click opens the tray at "New since you looked". - Two levels of signal, so the strong one keeps its meaning: - Quiet: a small grey count of turns you have not seen (out of combat: entries). A turn with six entries counts once. - Strong: gold, when something happened to a creature you control that you did not do yourself: damage or healing, a condition put on or ended, forced movement, a fall or collision, a triggered reaction that hit it, winded or dying, the Director changing its Stamina or resources by hand. - Both clear when you open the tray; nothing fades on a timer. - Hover: a preview card in the style of the map windows' hover, "Since you last looked": up to three "What happened" lines, your creatures first, then "and N more turns", then "Click to open". - The Director: the quiet count only, plus gold when a player changed something by hand (Stamina, conditions, resources, an undo). Monsters are all theirs, so "your creatures" would always be gold. - A setting to turn notifications off. Not proposed: toasts or pop-ups near the map (the table stays clear), a dot for every message (today's always-on dot). Code: the badge needs a count (an addition to buttonOps.badge); the rail's new-content marker already takes a count (DockablePanel newContentCount).

docs.title: Built: the minimised tray (2026-10-26)
docs.text: Same prototype link. Hover the tray: its titlebar has a minimise dash; the tray becomes the 40 px History block on the table. Minimising remembers what was on show. Play: the Fury's own turn adds nothing; the Reactor's Pulse hitting the Fury turns the badge gold "1"; the Troubadour's turn makes it "2". Hovering the block shows "Since you last looked" with the Fury's line first (gold edge), then the others, "and N more turns" when there are more, "Click to open". Opening (the block, or the rail button) clears it, unfolds the new turns, folds the earlier turns of that round into one line, and puts "New since you looked" before the first new turn. View as Director: grey count only (the scenario has no player hand edits). New wording: "Nothing new since you last looked." (for sign-off).

docs.title: Appendix W - Closing the open decisions (2026-10-27)
1. Can players open a monster's history? (decided: yes, 2026-10-27)
docs.text: Recommendation: yes, on every token the player can see, in the same radial slot as on their own. It filters entries the tray already shows players, so it reveals nothing new.
