Numbers about a monster in the detail card follow Monster Info's knowledge (Draw Steel Core Rules/MonsterKnowledge.lua: per monster type, Stamina tier 0-3, characteristics, immunities, abilities; learned in play or revealed by the Director): Stamina at the tier players know (Healthy / Winded until exact), a characteristic or immunity value only once revealed; otherwise the line keeps its contrast without the number ("Reactor 1 could not resist" for "Reactor 1's Agility 1 could not resist"). Innate immunities that change damage are already revealed automatically when they do. Alternatives: only creatures you control (monsters through search), or only while the Director's Monster Info setting is on.

docs.title: 2. Wording (decided 2026-10-27)
docs.text: Signed off in two rounds; see COPY.md. Applied to the prototype.

docs.title: 3. Turn numbers (decided 2026-11-04: kept, after briefly dropping them)
docs.text: Today in the prototype: a small number on each folded turn, "Turn 13" in each turn heading, "Turns 5-9" on the folded group, "Round 2, turn 13" in the detail card. Ricky asked for them ("look at turn 15"); James is not sold; search does not use them. Recommendation: drop the encounter-wide turn number and name a turn by its round and creature, which is how Draw Steel and the table talk ("Round 2, the Fury's turn"). Folded group: "5 earlier turns" (faces as now). Turn heading: "Dwarf Fury · Hero turn". Card: "Main action · Round 2". A solo creature's two turns: "first turn" / "second turn". Alternative: keep the numbers small and secondary, as now.

docs.title: Appendix X - Design review before the build (2026-11-04, in progress)
Coverage audit: what today's Action Log does that History does not yet say
docs.text: Rule: coverage means nothing is lost; where today's way is weak, recommend the better one. Covered: the unread marker (the block's badge), round and turn starts, initiative, casts and per-target results, immunity and weakness, healing, temporary Stamina, conditions removed, teleports, Malice spent, bonuses folded into a roll, hidden rolls (Director only), pop-out problems (History is a table window). Amending edges, banes or the tier after a roll: today only while that roll is still the active roll (MCDMAbilityRollBehavior.lua:3327), the same control as the roll dialog's, so History loses nothing. Gaps: - G1 Director tools on entries. Today, right-click: Delete Message, Clear Chat, Hide from players / Reveal to players (ActionLogPanel.lua:885-910), plus a visibility eye per roll. Players asked for a way to clear experiment junk (ticket MYEJSNWK). History has none. - G2 Undo on resource changes (the Resource card's Undo button, Draw Steel V/ResourceChat.lua). - G3 The ability itself: today hovering a Malice spend shows the ability card. History names abilities but never shows what they do. - G4 Rolls outside an action: Dice panel, macros, roll on a table, tests, montages, negotiation, downtime, initiative, class roll cards (Acolyte), the Director revealing a hidden modifier, and "Now playing" audio. Appendix K says compact rows for most; the prototype shows none, and out-of-combat grouping (no rounds or turns) is undecided. - G5 Retention outside combat: History keeps this encounter and the previous one; what happens between encounters, and next session, is undecided (today: the newest 128 messages, across sessions). - G6 Content authors' own lines: a damage behavior's authored chat message (AbilityDamage.lua:454) has no place in the detail card yet.

docs.title: David's feedback after the demo (via James, 2026-11-04)
docs.text:
• D1 Chat and History on separate rail buttons by default. Today both built-in Views (Director, Player) group Chat, Action Log and Safety into one rail group (DocumentSystem.lua:26972, 27031). Change: History gets its own slot; the Chat group keeps Chat and Safety.
  • D2 A brief preview when something lands while History is closed or minimised; none when it is open; a setting to turn it off. Precedent in the app: the chat speech bubble (DocumentSystem.lua:16400): when chat is not on screen, a new message shows in a bubble beside its rail button, lingers 5 s past the last message, up to 4 rows, placed to avoid open windows, click opens chat. History would reuse it beside its button or block, with the "What happened" line.
  • D3 Hovering a forced movement also draws the movement arrow on the map where it happened. CharacterToken:MarkMovementArrow(targetLoc, options) draws from the token's current spot (Definitions/CharacterToken.lua:465); history needs it from a saved start. Same engine ask as the cross-section from a saved path: one request covers both.

docs.title: Independent design review (fresh-eyes reviewer, 2026-11-04; code references checked)
docs.text:
1. Glance numbers are not what landed: a face shows the strike's -13 while the card says 17 taken (the Mark's 4 sits on a trigger row); folds add up targets only and net damage against healing (Zakaarior -1 = 9 taken, 8 healed); "7 fire" is dealt, the story says 4 taken. Fix: faces show the total taken including nested triggers; folds show damage and healing apart; captions use taken numbers.
  2. Several creatures in one turn lose their actor: an initiative entry can hold several tokens (MCDMInitiativeBar.lua:38, a Director's group turn), and action rows carry no actor face. Fix: an actor face on any row whose actor is not the turn's only creature; decide where actions with no cause sit (a free strike from an enemy moving away).
  3. Several maps each in their own combat: one tray per map, or one that follows the focused map? Which fight the badge counts and search covers.
  4. Notifications only when minimised: "x" (off the table) silences everything; an open tray never gets the "New since you last looked" marker; defaults (M #13) never reached the ledger. Fix: decide defaults; the rail button keeps the badge when the tray is off; mark new rows on an open tray too.
  5. Rows move under the reader: turns fold as the next starts; a card whose row folds stays open with nothing highlighted. Fix: no auto-fold while the pointer is on the tray or a card is open; never fold the selected turn; hold scroll and show "N new below".
  6. Hover-only and colour-only signals: the hero-card chip (James's constraint, kept), the side view on hovered text ("Hover here for the side view"), creature names only in tooltips, duplicate portraits for numbered monsters, resisted shown only as a greyed icon, friend/foe by ring colour, gold vs grey badge by colour. Fix: an icon button for the side view, a "Resisted" caption, numbered duplicate faces, a shape or face on the gold badge.
  7. Monster Knowledge contradicts itself: minion Stamina appears in Y13 and the receipt; a monster's own receipt shows its characteristic, which players already see on the live read-only card; spoiler modifiers (EmbeddedRollDialog.lua:425) would be named as sources. Fix: one rule, the receipt shows what players saw live; spoilers stay redacted.
  8. Revert, undo and Turn Rewind: Appendix T considered registering the History document for checkpoints, which would erase history (pillar 3, dispute persona); Monster Knowledge itself rolls back with checkpoints (MonsterKnowledge.lua:59). Fix: do not register; append revert markers; count a revert once.
  9. Scale: ten targets wrap the strip and put ten sentences in the card; folds show 5 faces with no "+N"; Show all or a creature chip unfolds a long fight at once (vscroll ~3 ms a panel). Fix: "+N", grouped identical outcomes ("Goblins 1-4 each took 6"), lazy build.
  10. Wording between surfaces: "<=11" badge vs "Tier 1"; S5 says "this encounter" though search covers the previous one too; turn numbers kept but search ignores "turn 15"; "Active" in the tray only while searching but always in the card.
  11. Font Size and narrow windows: tray plus card need ~800 px; glance text at 9.5-10 px is ~8 px at 80%. Fix: open the card on the side with room, or inside the tray when narrow; a minimum glance text size. Questions it raised: one History per map or one following the focused map; the tray or block on by default for players; Revert Turn erases or strikes through; what replaces round and turn out of combat; History from a token adds to or replaces the search; a monster's receipt follows knowledge or the live card; is gold harm only, or any change.

docs.title: History: build plan
docs.text: Status: signed off by James, 2026-11-06. Design: BRIEF.md, REVIEW.md, COPY.md, prototype https://claude.ai/artifact/UPWo9XvYuaDiZ388xRES35 (version 26).

docs.title: How the work runs
docs.text:
• One chunk, one commit. Each stage is still one PR, but none goes up until the build is finished; then they are raised together (James, 2026-11-06), so a late change to an earlier stage's files needs no extra PRs. Everything stays behind an off-by-default setting.
  • A tag marks where each stage ends: history-stage-0, history-stage-1 and so on. Each stage works on feature/history-stage-N, cut from the last stage's tag. Tags and branches stay local until the PRs go up. Merge main in at each stage end, since these files change often there.
  • History runs beside the old log until the last stage. The old log and its messages stay untouched. The switch-over is one chunk.
  • History never breaks the game. Every hook sits in hot combat code, so each is wrapped the way LiveEncounter.TrackHeroStats is: it can fail, and the cast carries on.
  • Generic hooks only. No code for a particular ability. Content built from modifiers works without changes, including future content.
  • Wording comes from COPY.md. Anything not there gets proposed first.
  • Every chunk: smoke test in the Codex over the bridge, type check, ASCII only, new Lua files registered through the MCP CodeMod workflow, the UI performance rules. James clicks where nothing can be checked by script. data/ YAML is only edited with the Codex closed.
  • Layering: hooks in DMHub Game Rules/ stay system-neutral, with Draw Steel words in the Draw Steel layer, so Crows keeps working. Check Crows loads after stage 0.

docs.title: Stage 0: foundations
docs.text: Goal: one real action appears in a real tray, stored safely, behind the setting. | Chunk | What | Size | Done when | |---|---|---|---| | 0.1 | Performance test: a probe writes 300 records, one per action, with two clients connected, and measures the cost of a write and of a load | S | We know this encounter and the last one are cheap to keep, and the hard cap is set (starting figure 300 entries) | | 0.2 | Record store: entries keyed by id (the BattleLog.RecordBattle pattern); one document per map; this encounter, the last one and what lies between, under a hard cap that culls the oldest first; names and portraits snapshotted; one client writes each entry; not registered for checkpoints; the setting | M | Records survive a reload and reach a second client | | 0.3 | F1 actions, at ActivatedAbility:Cast (ActivatedAbility.lua:3133): actor, ability, targets, castid, round, turn, map, roll facts | M | Every ability cast writes one record, prompted triggers included | | 0.4 | The tray: table item (a rail panel since 2.1b), rail button below Chat, round and turn folds, turn numbers, target cells, starts closed; builds the newest 30-40 rows and more as you scroll up, as today's log does | L | Real rows in the tray, meeting the idle and drag budgets |

docs.title: Stage 0 notes (built 2026-11-06)
docs.text:
• Entries are JSON strings, not tables (PROBE-0.1.md), and the hard cap is 500. The tray parses only the rows it builds.
  • Written when the cast ends, stamped with when it began, so a cancelled cast leaves nothing and one action is one write. Stage 1 should add a cast's results to its entry before that write.
  • The setting is historyenabled, game-wide, with no UI: dmhub.SetSettingValue("historyenabled", true). It has no wording yet because it never reaches a screen. Turning it on puts the rail button below Chat for that user (PanelDocument.RailPlaceBelow); 6.4 can use the same call.
  • Generic hooks added: ActivatedAbility.RegisterCastObserver, available on a panel registration, place, Tabletop.HasItem, Tabletop.CloseItem and Tabletop.ResizeItem for table items, and InitiativeQueue.turnNumber, a running count, because turn starts again each round.
  • Measured at 485 entries: tray open 70 ms of Lua, worst frame 150 ms; Show all 89 ms; a new row under 35 ms with its cast; idle open equals closed (14 ms); dragging 22 ms a frame against 25.6 ms for a map window. Panel count stays flat.
  • Left for later, not in stage 0's list: the Main, Maneuver and Move markers (T8: Move is not recorded yet), the Draw Steel banner (T10), chips (T12), the hover titlebar's text (T2), the rail button's lit state while the tray is open, and text for an empty tray, which has no signed wording.
  • Cloud file list: History, HistoryCapture and HistoryTray are registered in Draw Steel V now, ahead of the code reaching main. A client without the files on disk runs the empty cloud stubs, so History simply isn't there for anyone on main until the PRs merge.
  • Not checked: Crows. Crowdex/ is not in this checkout and does not load in the test game. History is inert while the setting is off, but check a Crows game before merging.

docs.title: Stage 1: what happened in combat
docs.text: Goal: the "did it change the table?" rule, on the glance. One family per chunk. | Chunk | What | Hooks | Size | |---|---|---|---| | 1.1 | F3 damage, healing, temporary Stamina, from any source, with the number that landed; skip what changed nothing | InflictDamageInstance (MCDMCreature.lua), the heal behavior (ActivatedAbility.lua:5094), GrantTemporaryStamina, AuraDamage (:7144) | L | | 1.2 | F2 automatic triggers, nested under their cause; add the resolving cast's id to event info | TriggeredAbility.lua:1545, ActivatedAbility.lua:3986, DispatchEvent | M | | 1.3 | F4 effects and conditions starting and ending, with the cause, grouped; the Ended tag; failed saves. New "Hidden from History" checkbox (COPY H1) and the 40-marker data pass | RemoveOngoingEffect, RemoveMatchingOngoingEffects, RemoveOngoingEffectsOnTrigger, PurgeCondition, EndTurn, EndRound, the RefreshToken tidy-up, a turn-end check for lapsed timers, EndPersistentAbilityById | L | | 1.4 | F5 winded, dying, death, confirmed minion deaths, recovering | MCDMCreature.lua:6806-6871, :7069-7083, squadminiondeaths (:6109) | S | | 1.5 | F6 resources with a cause; Malice; the Undo button on resource lines | ConsumeResource, RefreshResource, CharacterResource.SetMalice | M | | 1.6 | F7 forced movement: distance, collisions, falls, wall breaks, the saved path | AbilityRelocateCreature, LuaPath:Serialize | M |

docs.title: Stage 1 notes
docs.text:
• 1.1 hooks moved, for the better. creature.TakeDamage and creature.Heal instead of the damage and heal behaviors: every route ends there, hand edits and falls included, and they know the number that landed. SetTemporaryHitpoints instead of GrantTemporaryStamina, so ongoing effects count.
  • One observer: GameSystem.RegisterPlayObserver replaces the cast observer. Later families add a moment to it, not a new mechanism.
  • Writes batch per frame. History.Write queues; an aura hitting eight creatures is one write.
  • Measured per hit: 1 us with History off, 3 us inside a cast, 40 us for a line, plus the write.
  • 1.2: events carry causecastid, which survives the trip to another client. A trigger's entry names its cause and the tray nests it, so client and order don't matter, and nothing rewrites the parent.
  • Prompted triggers stay action rows (REVIEW.md section 1). A prompted trigger does not nest yet; "Before the roll" and "After the roll" (T15) need roll data from stage 2.
  • 1.3: creature:EndingEffects(cause, fn) wraps every place something comes off a creature and works out what ended from what changed, so a new removal path needs one wrapper, not its own logic. Lapsed timers are cleared at turn end, which is how they get reported.
  • 1.3 data pass, still to run, with the Codex closed: data/ YAML is never edited while it runs. From the repo root: python docs/action-log-design/probes/mark-history-hidden.py.txt --apply ticks Hidden from History on the 40 markers. Without --apply it only lists them. Commit it in data/.
  • L13 has no hook. The Elementalist's 5 x Reason rule only shows floating text; nothing ends the persistence, so "Took {n} damage in one turn" cannot appear until that rule is automated.
  • 1.4: winded, dying and killed fire where the rules already decide them, in MCDMCreature.lua, so hand edits count. Minion deaths wait for the batch that confirms them, then name the squad.
  • 1.5: resources carry the number that really changed (ReportResource). Undo on a resource line goes through History.UndoResource, which marks the line undone and keeps it.
  • 1.6: the saved path is a plain list of {x, y, floor, altitude} from path.steps, because what LuaPath:Serialize returned never reached the entry. Chunk 4.1 rebuilds a route from that list. Collisions and wall breaks are stored for the detail card; the tray only shows distance and fall.
  • Falls land after the push. The engine adds the landing as one last path step, so numSteps is one too many and path.fallDistance reads 0 afterwards. The real distance only comes with the fall event, which the engine fires when the animation ends, outside any cast. So the push leaves its row in g_falling, and the landing and the Fall Damage trigger join that row, even if it has closed. A fall with no push behind it stays a line, cause Fall Damage.
  • A creature landed on joins the push's row with the caption Landed on. With no push behind the fall it is a line, cause Landed on by {name}. Nothing is guessed from the damage, which is called Fall Damage either way: the engine fires fallenon only on creatures in the landing square, and its symbols name the faller. Tested for real, pushes in both orders, falls with no push, and a second fall inside the push's window, which stays off the row. Not tested across clients: if a trigger runs on another client it finds no push there and reads as a line, which is still true.
  • Tested for real: Brutal Slam on two clients, real heal and temporary Stamina behaviors, a Reactor trigger nested across clients, real end of turn, a real passing save, a real push with Growing Ferocity nested, a real push off a ledge in both orders (row closed before and after the landing), real Undo, and a Player seeing no Malice lines.
  • Tested with fed data only: failed saves, persistence, dying lines, confirmed minion deaths.
  • Wordings: the ones the build needed are signed off, COPY.md Round 5.
  • Left for later: effects ended by a respite (5.1), "Hidden from enemies" effects reaching players (2.4), the Active tag on a target's badge (3.1). Crows is not checked: Crowdex/ isn't in this checkout, so check a Crows game before merging.

docs.title: Stage 2: the detail card
docs.text: Goal: why it happened, one click from the row. | Chunk | What | Size | |---|---|---| | 2.1 | Card shell, placement beside or inside the tray, the sentence builder for What happened (COPY N2, L lines) | M | | 2.2 | The numbers: the receipt, the roll, edges and banes, one tier label | M | | 2.3 | F10 named sources: modifiersUsed, kit notes (modificationLog), immunity and weakness, DescribeModifications for anything else; Why lines; typed messages; ability card on hover | L | | 2.4 | The visibility rule: secret modifiers follow the reveal, minion Stamina and monster numbers follow Monster Info | S |

docs.title: Stage 2 notes
docs.text:
• 2.1: the card is a floating child of the tray's face, so it moves, scales and closes with the tray and no layout has to remember it. Tabletop.ItemRect says where the tray sits; the card picks right, then left, then inside the tray with Back (B7), and rechecks once a second, so dragging the tray moves it. It is rebuilt whenever it changes, because a scroll bar only works if it exists on its first frame.
  • Sentences: History.Story turns an entry into rows, with no gui, so the hover preview (3.3) and the sidebar preview (3.4) can use the same words. New wordings are COPY.md Round 6.
  • Which rows open a card: actions, and the Encounter ended line (L17). Every other line already says everything; L16 joins with the Why lines in 2.3.
  • W10 is not built. "Took 6 damage from 2 minions" needs the count of minions that reached a target, which entries don't hold yet. Look at it with the numbers in 2.2.
  • New facts on entries: ability.area, player, resisted names the condition when the rule text does, endedconds. Rows written before this have none of them, so an old row reads "Director" in its footer and "and Slowed ended" for a condition.
  • T13 Ally hit was missed in stage 1; it is on the target cell now, from the same check as W11.
  • Tested for real: the card on the right, on the left and inside the tray (a narrow table was faked), row swap, same row closes, close button, wheel, scroll bar drag, a row rewritten while its card is open, 31 rows built in 19 ms. Fed data only: every sentence but falls, the Encounter ended card.
  • 2.1b, a rail panel (James, 2026-11-07): History registers as a dockable panel with content, so the rail opens it as a window like Chat: frame, transparency, pin, pop out, Font Size zoom. Two generic registration fields in PresentPanel: defaultWidth (the rows are laid out for 410, plus the 8 px resize strip) and dragInPlace (rail windows are dragged without it, which restyles the whole window every frame: History's drag went from 64 ms a frame to 15; Chat's is 18). Only History sets them; giving every rail window dragInPlace is a separate change. The table item and the Tabletop.lua additions from 0.4 and 2.1 are gone. The card is placed from the window's position; popped out, it opens inside. The roll card that folds into History later (S5) aims at this window.
  • 2.1c, rows (James, 2026-11-07): a hairline above every action, folded turn and turn group (@border at 31%, the prototype's 5% white); the seam under a round heading and in the card at 75% (12%). Trigger rows are one line: the result after a caret is never cut, the "{Owner} · {trigger}" part shortens with an ellipsis and shows whole on hover. Widths are estimated per character, generously, because the engine can't measure text before layout. Tested on the seven-trigger Brutal Slam turn.
  • 2.1d, the card (James, 2026-11-07): the rail windows' frame (gradient, rounded, blurred backdrop, shadow); no white edge on the card or the selected row, which is marked by @bgRaised instead (a see-through fill shows the table behind the window under Transparent UI). A tail, a square turned 45 degrees behind the card, points at the row. The card lines up with its row from the panels' distancesToScreenEdge, slides to stay on screen, follows the list as it scrolls, and holds at the list's edge with no tail when the row scrolls out of sight. Over the list (popped out, or no room) it is solid and has no tail.
  • Performance after the feedback rounds (James: feels fine, 2026-11-07): on a freshly started Codex, idle runs at the frame cap with History open or closed; a card opens in 23-26 ms; dragging runs at 14 ms a frame; wheel scrolling at 14 ms. Two one-frame hitches stay: opening History from the rail (~95 ms) and Show all (120-140 ms for ~33 rows, 29 ms of it Lua). Spreading Show all over frames is 6.2's. Measure on a fresh start: after a day of reloads and pop outs the Codex itself slowed to ~4 frames a second, which made Show all look like a 2.7 s stall.
  • 2.2, the numbers: the prototype's receipt under What happened: Power roll (the two dice, the characteristic, a flat Bonus, edges and banes with their counts and the C4 note, Total with its tier), then a sum per target (its own roll if it had one, Tier lines by damage type, immunity or weakness, Taken / Taken, each / Regained), then Triggered and Cost. Wordings are COPY.md Round 7 (Z1-Z7). New facts: roll.natural, roll.characteristic, roll.bonus, and a target's own roll (edges, banes, total), which the roll behaviour now keeps on the cast as targetRolls beside tokenToTier. Rows written before 2.2 show only the total, the tier and the targets' sums.
  • Left for 2.3: surges and kit bonuses are inside the Tier line's number until 2.3 splits them out with the named sources. Immunity is one line per target even when two hits each met it.
  • Tested: a real Brutal Slam (5 + 5, Might 2, an edge from Prone, 14, Tier 2, 8 taken) and a fed entry with three edges and a bane, a flat bonus, a target cancelled out on its own roll, typed damage with immunity, a weakness, two goblins grouped, healing, a damaging trigger and a Malice cost.
  • 2.3 in four commits: 2.3a edge and bane sources, 2.3b surges and kit bonuses, 2.3c Why lines and typed messages, 2.3d the ability card on hover, and (James 2026-11-10) a hover on every name in the Why and The numbers: a modifier's recorded dialog text, a trigger's card (COPY.md Round 15).
  • 2.3d, hovers: every name in brackets in the Why, and the same names in The numbers, hovers (the hovered name alone is underlined). A modifier shows the roll dialog's own hover text, recorded at the roll by RecordEdgeSource / RecordDamageSource (summary with formulas filled in for the roller, Inflicted by, justification lines; spoilers applied for whoever looks). History.Write moves each text into the map document's hovers (an id per distinct text, hoverused for retention) and leaves the id on the source. A modifier with nothing past its name (James 2026-11-10) and rows from before 2.3d don't hover. A trigger name (and G7a's plain "trigger") shows the trigger's card as its owner has it now; a monster's is Director only. The card title shows the ability card, found by name on the actor.
  • Tested 2.3d: a real Bifurcated Incineration on two Custom Targets, one with Fire immunity (took 0), one with two damage modifiers, a surge, an edge and a bane cancelling: the modifier hovers in the Why and The numbers, the title's ability card, and the Troubadour's trigger card on an older row.
  • 2.3d follow-up (James 2026-11-10): the card title's ability name is in brackets and only it hovers (option A: the same cue as the Why). Ability and trigger cards open on the side away from the History window (the card's tail says which side that is; the engine gives Lua no screen position). A target whose immunity stopped all its damage now records its parts, so its line names the surge and modifiers behind the damage that immunity took off.
  • Limits of 2.3d: cards are looked up live, so a creature that's gone or no longer has the ability shows none.
  • 2.3a, edge and bane sources: under each edge or bane line, one line per thing that added to it (COPY.md Round 8): its arrows, a trigger owner's face, its name as the roll dialog's badge showed it; edges first, Set by hand last on each side, then the C4 note. The roll dialog measures each enabled modifier's edges and banes as CalculateRollText applies it (so the sources add up to the counts) and keeps the list on each target row as edgeSources; the power roll copies it onto the cast as targetSources; capture keeps it on the roll (from a target with no roll of its own) and on a target's own roll. Spoilered names stay redacted for players, as in the dialog.
  • Limits of 2.3a: two targets with the same counts from different sources show the first one's under Power roll. (Removers were not listed either; 2.3a2 adds them.)
  • Found in 2.3a: pressing the dialog's Roll Dice by its text over the bridge hits the side tab's label, not the button; click it with the virtual mouse. 2.2's targetRolls path is live (it sits in the same per-target block, which a real cast reaches).
  • For 2.3c (James, 2026-11-08): the card should say which trigger caused a nested gain (Y15). A resource line keeps only the trigger's name (causetext, e.g. "Discipline"); capture must also keep the trigger's own text, which lives on the TriggeredAbility's description (the Null's reads "You gain 1 discipline the first time in a round that an enemy uses Malice.").
  • 2.3a2, removed edges and banes (James, 2026-11-08; COPY.md Round 9): the roll dialog also records what each modifier takes away (removedEdges, removedBanes, ignore for the Ignore modtypes, which run last with lateness = 100). A target's own remover carries the target as its owner. The card lists a remover last under its line, dimmed, as "Ignored by" or "Removed by"; a side that lost every edge or bane keeps its line ("Edge, ignored", value 0). Tested with a real Brutal Slam while the Dwarf Fury was Twisted (Prone's edge, Ignored by Twisted, Tier 2) and a fed entry with a target's remover, a partial removal and an ignored bane on a target's own roll.
  • 2.3a2 feedback (James, 2026-11-08): a side that lost every edge or bane is crossed out, not relabelled: its line (label and value, the value muted) and each source under it carry a strikethrough, and the reason sits once, after the line, in the aside style ("~~Edge~~ Ignored by Twisted"; James chose the top line only, since Ignore applies to the whole side). Only a partial removal keeps the remover's own line, since nobody knows which edge it took. The old dimmed remover line read brighter than the sources; reasons now use @fgMuted. The card's styles live on the tray, so a style change needs the History window closed and reopened after a reload.
  • Found in 2.3a2: MCDMCreature.lua wraps creature.ApplyOngoingEffect with no reload guard, so every hot reload of that file stacks another wrapper and one effect writes one History line per reload. Dev-only (a fresh start has one wrapper); restart before judging effect lines.
  • 2.3b, the Tier line split (COPY.md Round 10): each damaged target's sum lists the tier's own damage, then the kit (K1), the roll dialog's damage modifiers (K2, named as their badges, a trigger's owner with a face), then surges (C3s behind the surge bolt), then immunity and Taken. Each part comes off the line of the type it added to; if the parts don't fit the lines (a negative remainder, or a type with no line) the line stays whole. Sources: the kit from the ability's modificationLog note (the kit's type is the tier's first damage, as MCDMKit matches it); modifiers measured around each ModifyRollProperties in CalculateRollText with RollPropertiesPowerTable.DamageByType, kept per target as damageSources and on the cast as targetDamageSources; surges as targetSurges (count, the highest characteristic, the type a surge modifier names). Entries written before keep one line.
  • Tested in 2.3b: a real Brutal Slam with 2 surges at Tier 3 (20; Tier 3 11, Panther kit +4, Spent 2 surges (Might 2 each) +4, Taken 19) and a fed entry with the Mark and its owner's face, typed fire parts with fire immunity, one surge, and parts that don't fit. Not tried live: a real damage modifier (none on the Fury's Brutal Slam), so the dialog's measurement has only run with nothing to record.
  • Found in 2.3b: resource lines stack the same way after reloads (one surge gain or spend wrote eight lines). Surges spent on accepting the roll also write their own "spent 2 surges" line beside the action, which the receipt now repeats; worth folding into the action as a cost later.
  • 2.3c split (James, 2026-11-08): 2.3c-1 the Why lines from what entries already record; 2.3c-2 triggers (Y11, Y15: capture the trigger's own text) and typed messages; 2.3c-3 the tier comparisons (Y1, Y2). Later, outside 2.3: falls (Y7), potency (Y8, Y9), Y5b, minions (Y13, after 2.4), L32, L33, L16.
  • 2.3c-1, the Why section (COPY.md Round 11, G1-G6): History.Why(entry) builds the rows with no gui (area ability that hit an ally, damage modifiers, surges, immunity or weakness, condition immunity), one line per distinct fact, naming every target that shares it; G6 only when the roll and damage are exactly the tier's (a kit doesn't count as a change). Rendered between What happened and The numbers as in the prototype: bold lead, sentence, a rule down the left. An action whose only change is an edge or bane has no Why section until 2.3c-3. Tested on the real entries (the surge Brutal Slam gets G2, Slide One Target G6) and fed entries for every line.
  • 2.3c-2, triggers and typed messages (COPY.md Round 12, G7-G8; James 2026-11-08): the Why says a trigger fired and what it changed ("{Owner}'s {trigger} / Triggered by this action: ...", in What happened's words); its rules sit behind a hover on its name in 2.3d (a monster's: Director only), so no trigger text is captured. Resource lines an automatic trigger writes now keep trigger and triggerby. Typed messages: one-line typedmessage play-observer hooks where a step posts its author's chatMessage (damage, conferred conditions, healing, purge, temporary Stamina, resource reasons); capture keeps them on the running cast's row (messages), skipping the ability's own name and repeats. Triggers that change the roll move to 2.3c-3 with the tier comparison.
  • Tested in 2.3c-2: the real Convocation of Chaos card (Lv2 Human Null's Discipline); a real Brutal Slam with notes sent from inside the cast (the ability's own name skipped, a repeat kept once); fed entries for every line. The hooks in DMHub Game Rules (heal, purge, replenish) were not reloaded live; they load on the next restart.
  • Found in 2.3c-2: the Wode Elf Troubadour's drama trigger is named with its whole rule ("Whenever a creature rolls a natural 2 ..."), so its lead read as a sentence. James chose G7a: a name ending in a full stop or past 40 characters leads as "{Owner}'s trigger"; the rule shows on the hover.
  • 2.3c-3, the tier comparisons (COPY.md Round 13, G9-G11, Z8): the roll dialog also records each modifier's tier effect (Tier Up/Down tiers, autosuccess, autofailure, nottierthree, nottierone, measured from ParseRoll like the edges; James: they are power roll modifiers, so History can name them). The Why recomputes the tier with one side taken away, through RollUtils.DiceResultToTier itself: the edges, the banes, what ignored or removed them, each tier modifier, and the natural 19-20 rule; a target's own roll covers only its target-only sources. Roll lines come first. A roll whose recomputed tier doesn't match the recorded one (rows from before 2.3a) gets none. The numbers lists each tier modifier after the edges and banes (Z8).
  • Tested in 2.3c-3: real entries (Prone moved a Brutal Slam from Tier 2 to Tier 3; Twisted's ignored edge; Word of Guidance on Bluster's targets); fed cases for a cancelled double edge with Tier Up, a natural 19 under a double bane, automatic Tier 3, a target's Cover and Not Tier 3, and an unexplained tier (no lines). Not tried live: a real tier modifier in the roll dialog.
  • Limit of 2.3c-3: each side is recomputed alone, so two sources that only change the tier together (a bane and a Not Tier 3 on the same target) each read "stayed at". Several targets that got the same target-only source get one line each. (Both limits gone in 2.3c-4.)
  • 2.3c-4, one tier line per roll (COPY.md Round 14, G12-G12d, Z9): James found the per-part lines confusing: each claimed its own tier change. The Why is a sum: one line per roll ("Tier 3, up from Tier 2" / "Prone gave an edge."), worked out for all parts together in TierStory. Parts are grouped (all edge givers, all bane givers, what removed each, each tier modifier, each flat bonus, a natural 19-20); the line names the side the tier moved, and adds ", but ..." only when the other side changed where it landed. A rule that sets the tier outright is named alone. A target's own roll gets a whole line of its own, merged across targets, dropped when it reads like the main roll's. The roll dialog now also records each modifier's flat change to the roll (bonus, the sum of ParseRoll's category mods); The numbers shows it after the edges (Z9) and the "Bonus" line keeps the rest. Worked out when the card opens, not stored at the roll (James): same facts and same rule either way, rows stay small, and fixes reach old rows.
  • Tested in 2.3c-4: 23 offline cases through the real TierStory code with RollUtils.DiceResultToTier copied in (every row of the signed-off table, set by hand, a remover of an edge no part gave, both sides cancelling, Not Tier 1, three parts, the guard). Live 2026-11-10 after the rebase: the real Prone Slam reads "Tier 3, up from Tier 2 / Prone gave an edge."; the Twisted and 16 + Might Slams get no line. A fed card (Rune +2 with Prone ignored by Twisted, two targets held by their own bane) showed the line naming the ignored edge, and the "but" clause putting the bane before "Twisted ignored it"; fixed (a part is named only when it did something against the other side; removers lead the "but" clause). The numbers shows "Rune of Striking +2" after the edges and Bonus +1 for the rest. Not tried live: a real flat bonus in the roll dialog (no modifier on the map adds one); its ParseRoll measure was checked on the bridge.
  • 2.3c-5, names in small caps (COPY.md Round 15, G13): every rule or ability name the Why prints (the tier line's parts, modifier and trigger leads) goes through WhyName, which wraps it in <smallcaps>; owners, "Set by hand" and The numbers stay plain. The tier line capitalises the first letter after a leading tag. Offline: the 27 cases give the same words with the tags stripped. Live 2026-11-10: the real Prone Slam reads "PRONE gave an edge."; a fed card showed the tier lines and bold small caps modifier and trigger leads.
  • 2.3c-5b, names in brackets: James compared small caps with square brackets on the busy card and chose brackets (COPY.md Round 15): WhyName now writes "[Name]"; the tier line capitalises the first letter after a leading bracket.
  • 2.3c-6, a target's line says only what differed (COPY.md Round 16, G14-G14b): TierLines splits each target's sources into what applied to every target (counted as often as the target with fewest has it) and its own. The roll's line names the shared parts; a target's line names its own parts over the shared ones (TierStory opts: named, always, movedOnly), only when they changed its tier. The roll used to be whichever target was selected when rolling, so a Prone on that target sat in the roll's line. Capture now keeps a target's own list (sources) whenever it differs from the roll's, so two targets with the same edge count owing it to different things (Prone, Restrained) both read right; rows from before read as before (a target without a list had the roll's).
  • Tested in 2.3c-6: the 27 tier cases read the same; 12 target cases (James's prone example rolled from either target, the busy card, same count different sources new and old rows, a single target, an own bane that changed nothing, a target-only Not Tier 3, two targets sharing a line, a record that doesn't add up, one edge of a double removed, no targets, every target with its own part). Live: the busy fed card reads as signed off; a real Brutal Slam on Test Monster Z 2 wrote one row (no target list, as it matched the roll). Not tried live: a real multi-target roll whose targets owe the same edges to different things. Follow-up: The numbers still lists the rolled target's sources under the power roll, so for that case it shows Prone where Goblin 2 had Restrained.
  • 2.3c-7, one damage line that sums it up (COPY.md Round 17, G15-G15c): DamageLines replaces the G1-G3 lines. Each target's modifier, surge and immunity parts become HistoryDamageBits; its tier damage ("from") is what it took with those taken back off, so a kit stays in it. Bits every target that took damage shared (counted as for the tier lines) make the shared line; a target's own bits make its line. Different tier damage: the shared line is "N extra damage", or, when the shared bits took damage off, there is none and each target's line names everything.

  • Tested in 2.3c-7: 15 offline damage cases (one target with surges, one surge, same tier with one immune, the busy card's different tiers, tier and kit only, lowered, cancelled out, weakness, surges on one target, different tiers with a shared reduction, an owner's modifier, damage immunity, a miss beside a hit, typed surges, every target immune alike); the tier cases read the same. Live: the busy fed card with Goblin 2 immune to holy reads "12 extra damage" and "15 damage to Goblin 2, down from 20 / Holy immunity 5 took 5 off." Known limit: History records what immunity took off, not the creature's immunity value, so capped immunity names the amount it took ("holy immunity 3").

  • 2.4, what players see (COPY.md Round 18): History.Entry cuts each entry down for a player as it is parsed (ForPlayers in History.lua), so no view can show more by mistake; a Director looking through a token's eyes gets the same cut (MonsterKnowledge.LocalUserSeesAll). Cut: condition lines and names of effects hidden from enemies on a creature off the heroes' side (captured as secret / hidden); a roll hidden from players (the roll message's gmonly, captured on the cast as hiddenRoll) loses its roll, tiers, own rolls and damage parts and gets secretroll; a monster's roll loses its modifier hovers. The card title brackets a monster's ability only with Monster Info on and the ability revealed. A monster's characteristic joins Bonus for everyone. The Director's eye on "Rolled in secret." rewrites the entry with roll.revealed.

  • Tested 2.4: a real Bifurcated Incineration rolled hidden (privaterolls dm) and revealed with the eye; Not What I Seem on Custom Target Test 2; the player view by swapping LocalUserSeesAll over the bridge (dmhub.isDM stays true, so Malice and DM-only bits still showed there). Not tried live: the L28 eye (no unrevealed spoiler modifier on the map), a monster ability card with Monster Info on, a real second client.

docs.title: Stage 3: getting to it
docs.text: Chunk What Size 3.1 Search: field, suggestions, chips, filter in place, Active tag, "turn 15" M 3.2 History from a token's radial and a hero card's chip S 3.3 Minimised block, badges on block and rail, hover preview, History notifications, new-rows markers, nothing moves under the reader M 3.4 History Sidebar Preview and its setting, reusing the chat speech bubble's placement (DocumentSystem.lua:16400) S

docs.title: Stage 3 notes
docs.text:
• 3.1 (built 2026-11-12):
  • Bar: the search field, with chips and the count on a row under it. Suggestions are grouped Creatures, Abilities, Conditions, Other; arrows/Enter/Escape work as in the global search.
  • Matching: typed words match the card's own sentences. Rows filter in place. Marks use the @warning colour at 55 alpha.
  • Active: effects are matched exactly by their instance id (instanceid on effectstarted); bare conditions by the newest row that started them.
  • Show all replaced by Latest (James): it shows only when you are away from the default view (scrolled up, older rows loaded, a fold changed by hand). It resets the folds and jumps to the newest row.
  • Type search (James, option A): creature suggestions also match a hero's class for everyone, and a monster's organisation, role, keywords and monster name for the Director only. Types are read from the live token. When two or more creatures share a type there is an All {type} row and chip. Name matches rank above type matches.
  • 3.2 (built 2026-11-12):
  • Entry points: a History slot at the top of every token's radial (angle 0), and a History chip just left of the hero card's centred flip button. Both use the rail's History icon in the house look, with no gold (James); the card chip turns gold on hover like the flip button.
  • What they do: History.OpenFor(token) replaces the search with that creature's chip and opens or raises the window.
  • Placement: the card chip stays out of the top-left corner, which belongs to the trigger and downtime badges.
  • Closing: closing History clears the search and hand-made folds (James); minimising (3.3) will keep them.
  • Card chip availability: it is added when the card is built, so turning History on mid-game needs the cards rebuilt.
  • 3.3 split (James): 3.3a is the closed state (badge, hover card, opening at the marker, setting); 3.3b is the open state (B3, "{n} new below").
  • 3.3a (built 2026-11-12):
  • Rail button as the block: History is a rail window with no minimise, so the rail button carries Appendix V's signal (James, option A). Grey count of unseen turns, your own excluded; a gold diamond when one of them did something to a creature a player controls.
  • Director: the monsters are theirs, so only the heroes' turns count; their gold waits for hand edits (5.2).
  • Hover card: "Since you last looked" in the detail card's frame and rows, your creatures first with a gold edge, then "and N more turns" and "Click to open".
    • It waits 0.4 s, shows nothing when nothing is new (M5 retired, James), and closes on press.
    • It works on a group strip, where it sits below the member.
  • Opening: lands on "New since you last looked", with new turns unfolded and the turns before them folded. When the new rows don't fit, the marker is scrolled to the top.
  • Storage: "last looked" is a per-user preference (history:lastlooked). The first sight of a map sets a baseline, so old rows aren't news.
  • Rail hooks (generic, DocumentSystem.lua): newContentStyle() gives a colour or diamond badge, and railHover(element, placement) gives a panel its own hover card. History's hooks look up History.Notify when called, so a reload reaches them.
  • Race fixed: the rail marks History seen before the window is built, so the window uses the mark kept from before (g_sinceAtOpen).
  • Not built: the M6 screen-reader label; the rail has no accessible names.
  • 3.3b (built 2026-11-13):
  • B3, nothing moves under the reader: when new rows arrive while the pointer is on History or a card is open, every turn and round stays as open as it was, and no turn on show joins the "Turns 1-4" fold. panel.mousePoint is 0..1 inside the panel and out of range outside, not (0,0) as the stub says.
  • Anchor hold: when you are scrolled up, the row at the top of the view stays put through a rebuild. It takes a few frames of retries while layout settles.
  • H2 "{n} new below": a floating button at the foot of the list counts the rows that came in since you were last at the bottom. Clicking it, or scrolling to the bottom, clears it.
  • Divider clears once caught up: "New since you last looked" goes when a newer entry arrives while you sit at the bottom. A plain game refresh doesn't count.
  • Reload: the window builder is looked up through History.Notify too. Otherwise, after a hot reload, the rail's seen-mark and the window come from different copies of the file and the divider is lost.
  • 3.4 (built 2026-11-13):
  • One bubble for any panel (James, option A): the chat speech bubble in DocumentSystem.lua now takes a panel key and name. PanelDocument.ShowRailBubble{key, panelName, rows} shows rows beside a panel's own rail button, FadeRailBubble(key) fades it, and PanelInFront and FindRailButton generalise the chat versions, which still exist. Bubbles avoid each other as well as windows.
  • Held under the pointer: a bubble waits while the pointer is on it, then lingers 5 s after the pointer leaves. Chat's bubble gets this too.
  • What shows: new entries from someone else's turn (the badge's rule), checked every 0.5 s. A batch waits one quiet tick so an action's triggers land in its row. An action is "Actor . Ability" (L46) over up to 2 sentences and "and {n} more" (L47); a line is its sentence.
  • Click: a row opens History scrolled to that action with its card (History.ShowEntry); elsewhere opens History as the button does. Hovering the button fades the bubble for the hover card.
  • Setting: history:sidebarpreview, on by default, General (L37, L38 revised).
  • Not built: a trigger landing in a later tick than its action is left out; a lone trigger with no action gets no row; there's no bubble while History is grouped away in a strip (as Chat).
  • Engine follow-up (Latest bounce): SheetScrollView keeps its wheel smooth-scroll target until the list gets within 0.001 of it. On a short list it can stall at 0.997, and setting vscrollPosition from Lua does not clear the target, so the list eases back. Fix in dmhubclient: the setter (SheetPanel.cs vscrollPosition) clears the target. Nothing on the codex side.

docs.title: Stage 4: movement views
docs.text: Chunk What Size 4.1 Engine PR: draw the movement arrow and the side view from a saved start and path (MarkMovementArrow, SetMovementCrossSection, a way to build a LuaPath in Lua) M 4.2 Side-view button on movement captions, arrow, CreateGhost at the start square S

docs.title: Stage 4 notes
docs.text:
• 4.1 (built 2026-11-13, engine d9eb2b9af on dmhubclient feat/saved-movement-path, from upstream/master): dmhub.CreatePath(steps, {forced, flying, teleport}) builds a LuaPath from {x, y, floor, altitude} steps (altitude defaults to the ground). token:MarkMovementArrow(nil, {path = p, separate = true}) draws it as given and returns {path, marker}. The side view (SetMovementCrossSection) already drew from the path's steps. Checked live in the dev build: arrow, ghost at the start, side view renders, normal arrows unchanged.
  • For 4.2: History saves a path as positional lists {x, y, floor, altitude}, so 4.2 maps them to named fields. The ghost (CreateGhost) is parented to its token and follows it, which is fine for a hover preview. The side view shows other creatures where they stand now. Definitions/ needs regenerating from the engine before the type check knows CreatePath.
  • 4.2 (built 2026-11-13):
  • Where: a muted arrow-elbow button at the end of a forced-move row in the card's What happened. Only in the full card, on the map shown, while the moved creature is still there. No button on an engine without dmhub.CreatePath.
  • Hover: the arrow along the recorded path, a ghost on the start square (the path's first step, so it keeps its altitude), and the side view alone in a tooltip frame, as a drag shows it, with collision damage. All cleared on dehover.
  • L35 (James): the tooltip has no title, to match the drag tooltip; "Side view" shows only when the move can't be drawn side-on (it crosses floors).
  • Several movers in one row: each gets an arrow and a ghost; the side view is the first's.
  • Not built: L36 (panels have no accessible names); a button on a standalone moved line; fall damage in the side view (History records squares fallen, not the damage).
  • Straight arrow (engine 9207aabeb, feat/saved-movement-path): DrawArrowAlongPath runs Pathfind.MakePathDirect on a forced path, so a replayed push draws straight as its targeting arrow did. A fall's landing point stays in, so the arrow bends down at its end (James: keep it).
  • Definitions: only the CreatePath and MarkMovementArrow stubs from the dev build's regen; the rest of the regen was unrelated engine drift.

docs.title: Stage 5: everything else the old log shows
docs.text:
Chunk What Size 5.1 F8 play without an action: tests, Dice panel, tables, macros, montages, negotiation, respite, downtime; the Out of combat section L

James, 2026-11-10: replace the "Out of combat" section with the game mode the Initiative bar shows (InitiativeQueue.gameMode: Exploration, Respite; combat keeps its rounds). Each entry records the mode it was written in; a mode change starts a new section. Headings to sign off with 5.1.

5.1a f7fa100a (2026-11-14): headings signed and checked live. Respite entries record mode; Exploration records none, so older entries go under Exploration.

5.1b a04aec42 (2026-11-15), checked live by James: tests (character panel, roll dialog, Director Request Rolls) and Dice panel rolls write test / dice lines; each opens a numbers-only card (dice, characteristic, edges and sources, bonus, total, tier). The roll dialog passes {edgeSources} as completeRoll's second argument; requests carry director = true. Card titles "Gordon · Might test" / "Gordon · Dice" signed. A Recovery spend joins its heal row (bcb6e00d). Left in 5.1: tables, macros, montages, negotiation, respite, downtime.

5.1 copy signed 2026-11-15: COPY.md Round 21 (L48-L85). Build order, one commit each: 5.1c hidden rolls (GM only = no line for other players; Dice Tower = rolled in secret; follow Reveal/Hide; fixes the 5.1b test and dice lines), 5.1d respite, 5.1e montages, 5.1f negotiation, 5.1g downtime, 5.1h tables and macros. 5.1d (2026-11-19): a long rest fires resting and rested play-observer moments from creature:Rest; History writes L53-L55 from the difference, and RemoveOngoingEffectsOnRest reports L56 through EndingEffects("rest"). Checked with a fed no-change respite and the real Rest on a copy; a real respite with healing, XP and a Level is James's to run.

Also 2026-11-19, from the review: the Draw Steel banner (T10, combatbegan), a teleport of another creature (teleported), opposed power rolls (nested test lines, opposed outcome, dice on the card), and the cull guard (History.minEncounterEntries). Fed History tests must use a scratch map id: a fed encounter counts towards the cull.

5.1h (2026-11-19): tables and macros. RollOnTableProperties.NotifyRolled (DMHub Game Hud, system-neutral) fires tablerolled from the roller's completion callback: Request Rolls (Director requests, and an ability's table roll, which carries the cast id and nests under the action's row: James 2026-11-19), a player's journal table link, and the two Director project-event rolls (L77). After an override the roll dialog's synthetic rollInfo carries rolledTotal and overrideMessage, so the line is written once with the final row (L78). Card: "{Who} · {Table}" / "Director · {Project} event", then Dice, Bonus, Total (no tier), a Result subheading with the row's full text, and the override message (signed 2026-11-19). Macros fire awarded (L82-L85); /roll, /r and /dmroll are codex copies of the engine's commands with a complete callback into diceroll (L81). Not covered: the legacy RollOnTableDialog and RequireDCDialog (5e-era), and Dice Tower or GM-only table rolls, which the table dialog cannot make. A Director's table roll with no character leaves {...} formulas unfilled, as the chat card does. "1 Victories" reads "1 Victory". Checked with the handlers run over the bridge with writes captured, and the cards built; no real roll or macro run.

After James tested 5.1h (2026-11-19): a choice table (Conduit Prayer Choice) names the table its dice landed on, read from the roll's own properties (427d3da4); the History preview bubble builds only the newest four rows (b36615ac). Sections (cd0aed5a, James): a combat's rounds sit under one "Combat" heading, rounds one step in; an older combat folds to "Combat · Rounds 1–3"; when a combat begins, everything before it counts as seen (CombatStart in HistoryTray's Unseen). Doubled resource lines written between the two reloads that day are a reload artifact (MCDMCreature's resource wrappers wrapped twice), not a code fault; they stay in that game's History. | 5.2 | F9 Director actions: reinforcements, villain actions, overrides, hand edits, reveals; right-click Hide/Reveal, Delete entry, Clear History | M | | 5.3 | Revert Turn and Turn Rewind: Reverted rows, the Turn reverted line, out of the totals | M |

5.2 decided 2026-11-19 (COPY Round 22, L86-L94). Build order, one commit each: 5.2a right-click tools (Hide/Reveal, Delete entry, Clear History with its confirmation); 5.2b hand edits (who made them, Stamina set by hand, the Director's gold for players' edits); 5.2c reinforcements; 5.2d villain action tag; 5.2e overrides; 5.2f reveals.

5.2 done 2026-11-19, all six tested by James: 5.2a 04666850 + 5a6a9bb8, 5.2b 72f0354d, 5.2c ed86472b, 5.2d bae93fc3 + 188b93a6 (popout face 7ba06541), 5.2e bb3fb0f0 + 4a4594ab, 5.2f b114104f (reveals; tested on Devil Jurist 1 with a hand-added {#Soft Underbelly} trait, no compendium monster has one).

5.3 done 2026-11-19, tested by James: 03127a9d (Reverted rows, the Turn reverted line, out of the totals; Turn Rewind's steps in a turn share one line and rolling forward clears the mark, as James agreed) + 13955649 (struck through as well as faded, James's ask) + f643ca0e (Revert Turn marks the whole turn by encounter, round and turn, since a player's client stamps with a server time that can run behind the Director's checkpoint; a fully reverted turn's heading is tagged and struck; the replayed turn gets its own heading). Stage 5 complete. Next: 6.1.

docs.title: Stage 6: finish and switch over
docs.text: Chunk What Size 6.1 Several maps: follows the map last clicked, the switcher, badge and preview across maps M 6.2 Scale: "+N", grouped results, details built when opened; a long-fight test at the hard cap M 6.3 Font Size and narrow windows (the responsive-panel checks); full performance pass S 6.5 Gaps found 2026-11-20: stability on forced movement; the roll card folding into History (S5: to the new row when open, to the rail button when closed); empty History (L96); glance chips (T12); Before / After the roll tags (T15); damage from {n} minions (W10); turn pips on the current turn from live action use (T8); wall breaks; numbered faces on fold lines that share a portrait (B4); the per-target sources in the numbers and the duplicate surge line L 6.6 The signed Why lines never written (Y5b, Y7, Y8, Y9, L26, Y13, L25, L32, L33, L16, C4); strained, rampage and captain changes (F5) M - Before 6.4: the 1.3 data pass (Codex closed) - 6.4 Switch-over: History on for everyone; old log off the rail; the built-in Views give History its own button; stored rail layouts repaired (g_railRenamedPanels); tooltip "History (was Action Log)"; old messages keep posting, because other code reads them M

docs.title: Stage 6 notes
docs.text:
• 6.1 done 2026-11-19, checked by James. History follows the map last clicked (pressing a map window makes it current), held while the pointer is on History or a card is open. The switcher is a dropdown in the window's title row (COPY L95), shown while two or more maps the user can see are in combat; it uses a new generic rail-window hook, headerControl on a panel registration (PanelDocument:CreateInterface), floated in the header 6 px past the last tab chip (inside the tab strip it wrapped below the header). A Sidebar Preview row from another map now opens History on that map. Tabletop.MapName is exported for the switcher. Not tried: History sharing a window with Chat as tabs; reaching a map not in combat after opening another map's row (close and reopen History).
  • 6.1 shared window (d5f51eb1): sharing a window with Chat, the tabs keep the top row and the switcher sits on a row of its own under them. Overflow of the search bar and rows in a shared window is 6.3's.
  • 6.2 done 2026-11-20, checked by James. "+N", grouped results and cards built on open were already in from stages 2-4. Long-fight test: a scratch document of 500 entries (the hard cap), cloned from real rows. Before: search 155-256 ms in one frame, open 147-160 ms, a refresh with nothing new 34 ms. Now: History builds 12 rows (a few more than fit), tops up until a quarter of a view sits above the bottom one, and loads the next 12 while the reader is half a view from the top, ignoring the few frames a rebuild moves the view. Rows on show are the only ones signed. Search 97 ms, open about 100 + 70 ms, refresh 11-14 ms. Measured and not used: building over several frames (every pass re-lays out the whole list: worse) and hideObjectsOutOfScroll (scrolling 100 built rows is already 14 ms a frame). A combat broken by a line from outside it reused its section id, and two rows sharing an id lost a heading: repeated ids now get a count.
  • 6.3 done 2026-11-20, checked by James. History lays out to its window's width (James chose following the window over shrinking to fit or forcing 410): its own window resizes 320-600 px and opens at 410; in a window another panel owns (Chat) it takes whatever width it gets. Rows rebuild once a drag has been still for 0.25 s. Fold lines fit their faces to the width before "+N", and resting on a folded Combat, Round or Turns line shows a card of every creature with its name and what it took and regained (James, 2026-11-20); the faces on fold lines take no name hover of their own. The card opens to the right, or the left with no room. "Rounds" stays spelled out. Font Size with the rail on zooms the whole window, so it is the same width case. Performance: idle at the frame cap with History open; a rebuild of what shows costs 23 ms on a 50-entry map, about 100 ms at the 500-entry cap.
  • Audit 2026-11-20 (design against build), James's calls: dropped: audio "Now playing" lines (a notification bubble now), the "Cover: bane" caption (tier pills and the Why cover it), the "History · {map}" title (the map switcher), T8 as rows (it is pips on the current turn only, as the prototype had). Kept: numbered faces, on fold lines only. Wall breaks get shown (wording to propose). 6.4 changes shape: History is the default and a "Use Old Action Log" setting (off) brings the old log back and hides History. Crows gets a real load during testing. Negotiation's player side (pitfall or motivation choice takes no click; making a case does nothing and blocks the turn) is the negotiation module's, not History's; History's lines come from NegotiationRun.Note (began, adjust, reveal, ended).
  • 6.5a done 2026-11-20, tested by James (Knockback on a stability-2 Devil High Judge): stability and wall breaks (COPY Round 25, L97-L106). Stability is worked out in three places, and all three report through ActivatedAbilityInvokeAbilityBehavior.NoteStability: the tier-text forced movement in MCDMAbilityBehavior.lua (the common one; a push it stops shows "Too Much Stability" and never moves), and the two in AbilityInvokeAbility.lua. A push stopped entirely is reported from there; the rest ride on the clone as _tmp_forcedMoveStability to the move's forcedmove notice. A push blocked before it moved a square (collision, or stability first) used to write nothing and now writes "Push blocked". Not changed: a push handed to another client (InvokeAbilityRemote) has stability worked out again from the shortened range there, which looks like a double reduction; check separately.
  • 6.5b done 2026-11-20, tested by James: empty History (L96); edges and banes on the row as the roll dialog's chevrons (BRIEF 2026-10-23), with Critical as a chip, and nothing when they cancel; Before / During / After the roll tags (T15, L107): a triggered action used from the roll dialog (marked trigger on the dialog's edge and damage sources) gets its own row from entry.rolltriggers; "{n} minions" from the squad's targetPairs (W10); numbered faces on fold lines that share a portrait (checked on a scratch map); turn pips on the turn being played, filled until used (T8). Found while testing: the game resolved a Command +1 tier roll at Tier 2 (a rules bug, investigated in its own session), and the side view's collision badge is squares, not damage (left as is; a History Why line for "+2 into an object" goes in 6.6).
  • Data pass done 2026-11-20: Hidden from History on the 40 markers, committed in the data repo (not pushed).
  • 6.4 checklist, Encounter of the Week: its interface replaces the rail and keeps a corner strip of buttons named in EncounterOfTheWeek/EncounterOfTheWeekHud.lua (CreateCornerButtonsPanel): Journal, Chat, Action Log. History was added beside the Action Log on 2026-11-19, shown while historyenabled is on. At the switch-over, take "Action Log" out of that list and drop the History.Enabled check. Not yet seen running: the button is built with the strip, so turning History on mid-game needs the interface rebuilt.
  • 5.1e left out (James, 2026-11-19): delve turns and chest rolls write nothing.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Performance of two encounters (0.1). Today's log keeps about 140 messages and that has drawn one complaint, so there's no value in a really long history. If two encounters cost too much, the hard cap wins and the older encounter shortens. That's why it goes first.
  • Who writes. Two clients recording the same event would double it. Each hook needs one clear writer; lapsed timers are the likeliest trouble because no single client owns them.
  • Cost on hot paths. Damage runs often, so DescribeModifications only runs when a number actually changed. Measure in 1.1.
  • Trigger causes (1.2). Nesting relies on passing the cast through events. Some events may not have one, and those fall back to a line in the turn.
  • Old log readers (6.4). Roll dialogs, respite, Encounter of the Week and others use chat messages, so 6.4 removes the panel, not the messages.

docs.text:
1. Today's log keeps about 140 messages, culling the oldest, builds the last 30-40 and more as you scroll up, and has drawn one complaint. Try this encounter and the last, as long as performance holds; a really long history has no value.
  2. The engine PR for the arrow and side view from a saved start is already agreed in principle.

docs.title: History: wording for sign-off
docs.text:
Status 2026-10-27: all signed off, including Round 2 (James: "Yes, those work"). Applied to the prototype the same day. Signed off as listed: N1 (History), N2, T, C (except C4), S, M, E.

Every user-facing string in the prototype, grouped by surface. Reply with the IDs you want changed; anything not called out is signed off. Ability and trigger names in [brackets] are content, not wording. Rules applied: Hero and Stamina capitalised; condition names capitalised as names ("Slowed ended"), lower case inside sentences ("is slowed"); no pronouns for creatures (names instead).

docs.title: Three calls first
docs.text:
N1. The feature's name. Recommended: History. It is the word on the radial slot, the hero card chip and the tray, and it says what it holds without "log" (a text dump, the thing being replaced). Alternatives: keep "Action Log" (familiar to today's users); "Combat History" (wrong outside combat: tests, montages, negotiation). If History: the old name appears once in the rail tooltip for a release, "History (was Action Log)".

N2. "What happened" sentences. One sentence per creature, past tense, the result first: | ID | Pattern | Example | |---|---|---| | W1 | {Creature} took {N} damage. | Monster Test 1 took 11 damage. | | W2 | {Creature} took {N} {type} damage. | Dwarf Fury took 4 fire damage. | | W3 | ... damage: {split}. | Test Monster Z 1 took 8 damage: 4 fire and 4 cold. | | W4 | ..., was pushed {N} square(s) and is now winded. | Reactor 1 took 7 damage, was pushed 1 square and is now winded. | | W5 | ... and is {condition} ({duration}). | ... and is slowed (save ends). / ... slowed until the end of its turn. | | W6 | ... and resisted being {condition}. | Polder Elementalist took 4 fire damage and resisted being slowed. | | W7 | ... It was not {condition}. (immune) | It was not frightened. | | W8 | {Creature} took {N} damage and was killed. | Monster Test 1 took 17 damage and was killed. | | W9 | {Squad} took {N} damage: {k} of {m} minions killed. / ... the squad is destroyed. | Goblin Warriors took 5 damage: 1 of 4 minions killed. | | W10 | {Creature} took {N} damage from {k} minion(s). | Dwarf Fury took 6 damage from 2 minions. | | W11 | {Creature}, an ally, was caught in the burst and took {N} damage. | | | W12 | {Creature} regained {N} Stamina [and is no longer {condition}]. | Zakaarior regained 8 Stamina and is no longer grabbed. | | W13 | {Owner}'s {trigger} then hit {Creature} for {N} {type} damage. | Reactor 1's [Reactor trigger] then hit the Wode Elf Troubadour for 2 fire damage. | | W14 | {Creature} gained {N} {resource}. | Human Null gained 1 Discipline. | | W15 | ... pushed {N} squares off {place}, it fell {N} squares. | Test Monster Z 1 took 14 damage: pushed 3 squares off the gallery, it fell 4 squares. |

N3. "Why" lines. A short contrast, then one plain sentence: {lead} / {reason}. Only what moved the result away from the plain roll. | ID | Lead | Reason (example) | |---|---|---| | Y1 | Tier 1, not Tier 2 | Reactor 1's trigger added a bane when it was targeted, cancelling one of three edges. | | Y2 | {Name}: Tier 1, not Tier 2 | The Fury had cover, a bane against that target only: 13 - 2 = 11. | | Y3 | 7, not 9 | Reactor 1 has damage immunity 2. | | Y4 | 4 fire, not 7 | Test Monster Z 1 has fire immunity 3. The 7 includes +1 from [Elementalist feature] on Fire abilities. | | Y5 | +4 from surges | Two surges from the bank. / One from the bank, one from Trained Assassin (lost if not used on this strike). | | Y6 | +4 from the Mark | High Elf Tactician's Mark triggered when the strike hit. | | Y7 | 14, not 8 | The fall added 6. Hover here for the side view. | | Y8 | Prone | Two surges raised the potency from A<1 to A<2, so Reactor 1 could not resist. (Agility 1 shown only once Monster Info reveals it) | | Y9 | Fury slowed / Elementalist not slowed | R<1: the Fury's Reason 0 could not resist. / R<1: the Elementalist's Reason 2 resisted. | | Y10 | Not frightened | Test Monster Z 1 is immune to frightened. | | Y11 | Triggered | Reactor 1's trigger answered the strike on its ally ([trigger condition]). | | Y12 | Hit an ally | The burst catches every creature in the area, allies included. | | Y13 | 1 minion, not more | Each minion in this squad has 5 Stamina, so 5 damage kills one. | | Y14 | Grabbed ended | Healing Grace ends one condition. | | Y15 | Discipline +1 | The Null gains Discipline when an enemy spends Malice. | | Y16 | (nothing moved it) | Nothing changed the result: a straight roll. |

docs.title: Round 2: James's four changes (signed off 2026-10-27)
docs.text:
Draw Steel's own wording (Heroes book): you gain and spend surges; each surge spent deals extra damage equal to your highest characteristic score; two or more edges make a double edge; "a double edge and just one bane, the roll is made with one edge, regardless of how many individual edges contribute"; a creature uses a triggered action, and every triggered ability has its own Trigger: line.

R1. Why lines: the cause first, then what it did (replaces "X, not Y"). The lead names the rule or source in Draw Steel's words; the sentence says what changed, with "instead of" where a number moved. | ID | Lead | Sentence | |---|---|---| | Y1 | Bane from Reactor 1's [Reactor trigger] | It cancelled one of three edges, so the roll stayed at Tier 1 instead of Tier 2. | | Y2 | Cover | A bane on the roll against the Fury only: 13 - 2 = 11, Tier 1 instead of Tier 2. | | Y3 | Damage immunity 2 | Reactor 1 took 7 damage instead of 9. | | Y4 | Fire immunity 3 | Test Monster Z 1 took 4 fire damage instead of 7. The 7 includes +1 from [Elementalist feature] on Fire abilities. | | Y5 | Spent 2 surges | Each dealt 2 extra damage (the Fury's highest characteristic, Might 2). | | Y5b | Spent 2 surges | Each dealt 2 extra damage (Agility 2). One was gained from Trained Assassin and could only be spent on this strike. | | Y6 | Marked by the High Elf Tactician | The strike dealt 4 extra damage. | | Y7 | Fell 4 squares | The fall dealt 6 damage, for 14 instead of 8. Hover here for the side view. | | Y8 | Potency raised with 2 surges | A<1 became A<2, so Reactor 1 could not resist being knocked prone. | | Y9 | Reason 0 / Reason 2 | R<1: the Fury could not resist being slowed. / R<1: the Elementalist resisted. | | Y10 | Immune to frightened | Test Monster Z 1 cannot be frightened. | | Y12 | Area ability | The burst hits every creature in the area, allies included. | | Y13 | Minions | Each minion in this squad has 5 Stamina, so 5 damage killed one. | | Y14 | Healing Grace | It ends one condition: grabbed. | | Y15 | Discipline | The Null gains 1 Discipline when an enemy spends Malice. | | Y16 | (nothing changed it) | Nothing changed the roll or the damage. |

Alternative: no lead, one full sentence each ("Reactor 1's damage immunity 2 reduced the damage from 9 to 7."). Easier to read once, slower to scan, and the bold lead is also what search marks.

R2. Surges without "the bank". | ID | Where | Text | |---|---|---| | Y5 | Why | as R1 above | | C3s | The numbers | Spent 2 surges (Might 2 each) .......... +4 | | T12s | Chip | 2 surges (unchanged) |

R3. Triggered actions in Draw Steel's words (replaces Y11). The lead says who used which triggered action; the sentence quotes that ability's own Trigger line, which answers "what set it off" in the rules' words. | ID | Lead | Sentence | |---|---|---| | Y11 | Reactor 1 used a triggered action | Trigger: {the ability's Trigger text}, e.g. "An ally within 2 squares is targeted by a strike." | | Y11f | Human Null used a free triggered action | Trigger: {text} |

R4. The edge rule note (C4). | ID | Where | Text | |---|---|---| | C4 | Under the edge and bane sources | A maximum of two edges count (a double edge); with one bane, the roll is made with one edge. | | C4b | Two or more banes | A maximum of two banes count (a double bane); with one edge, the roll is made with one bane. | | C4c | Edges and banes cancel | Edges and banes cancel out: the roll is made without either. |

docs.text:
N2 covers most sentences. These are the cases it doesn't cover, as built in chunk 2.1. | ID | What | Draft | |---|---|---| | X1 | An effect that isn't a condition | {Creature} took 3 damage and gained {Effect} until the end of its turn. | | X2 | An effect ended (a condition keeps W12) | ... and {Effect} ended. / {Creature}'s {Effect} ended. | | X3 | A creature landed on | ... took 10 damage and was landed on. | | X4 | Temporary Stamina took some of it | ... took 7 damage, 3 of it to temporary Stamina. | | X5 | Temporary Stamina grew | {Creature}'s temporary Stamina went from 3 to 10. / ... and temporary Stamina went from 3 to 10. | | X6 | A fall with no push | ... took 6 damage and fell 4 squares. | | X7 | Resisted, the rule text names no condition | ... took 4 damage and resisted. | | X7a | Resisted, the rule text names an ongoing effect, no condition (signed 2026-11-20) | ... took 10 damage and resisted Can't Hide. | | X8 | Damage partly typed | ... took 10 damage: 6 fire and 4 untyped. | | X9 | W11 for any area, not only a burst | {Creature}, an ally, was caught in the area and took {N} damage. | | X10 | A trigger that did more than damage (W13 covers damage) | {Owner}'s {trigger}: {sentence} | | X11 | An action that changed nothing | {Creature} used {Ability}. | | X12 | C6 with no roll behind it | {player} · {time} | | X13 | L30, no plural | Goblin 1-4 each took 6 damage. |

Two N2 changes the data forces: - W15 loses "off {place}": nothing records the ledge's name, so it reads "pushed 3 squares, it fell 4 squares." - EoE stays out of sentences: the Codex also stores "no timer" as EoE, so a fall's Prone would read "until the end of the encounter" when it ends on standing up. The tray keeps its (EoE) (D1).
