docs.title: Round 13: the tier comparisons (signed off 2026-11-08; G9-G11 replaced by Round 14)
docs.text: History recomputes the tier with a side of the roll taken away, by the roll's own rules (RollUtils.DiceResultToTier), and says what each side did. One Why line per side: edges, banes, what ignored or removed them, and each tier modifier; roll lines come first in the Why. Leads name the sources as The numbers does (C5, C5t, C5h), joined with "and". Replaces Y1's and Y2's wordings. A roll whose recomputed tier doesn't match the recorded one (a row from before this) gets no tier lines. | ID | Where | Text | |---|---|---| | G9 | Why, edges or banes that changed the tier | It gave an edge (a double edge / a bane / a double bane), which moved the roll from Tier 1 to Tier 2. Several sources: They gave ... | | G9s | Why, edges or banes that didn't | It gave an edge; the roll stayed at Tier 2. | | G9r | Why, what ignored or removed them | It ignored an edge (a double edge), ... / It removed an edge, ... with G9's or G9s's ending | | G9t | Why, a target's own edges or banes (target-only sources) | It gave a bane against Reactor 1, which moved that roll from Tier 2 to Tier 1. / ...; that roll stayed at Tier 2. | | G10 | Why, tier modifiers | Tier Up: It raised the roll a tier, from Tier 1 to Tier 2. Tier Down: It lowered the roll a tier, from Tier 3 to Tier 2. Tier 3: It made the roll Tier 3 instead of Tier 1. Tier 1: It made the roll Tier 1 instead of Tier 2. Not Tier 3: It kept the roll from Tier 3: Tier 2 instead. Not Tier 1: It lifted the roll off Tier 1: Tier 2 instead. Unchanged: ...; the roll stayed at Tier 3. | | G11 | Why, a natural 19 or 20 that changed the tier | Natural 19 / A natural 19 or 20 is always Tier 3, so the roll is Tier 3 instead of Tier 2. | | Z8 | The numbers, a tier modifier (after the edge and bane lines; a trigger's with its owner's face) | {name} .... Tier 3 / Tier 1 / +1 tier / -1 tier / not Tier 3 / not Tier 1 |

docs.title: Round 14: one tier line per roll (signed off 2026-11-08)
docs.text: James 2026-11-08: the Why is a sum, not an explainer line per part. One line per roll says where it landed and what got it there, worked out for all its parts together (each part alone gave contradicting claims). "From" is the tier the dice and characteristic gave alone. The line names the parts on the side the tier moved, and the other side only when it changed where the roll landed. A rule that sets the tier outright (Tier 3, Tier 1, a natural 19 or 20) is named alone. Live check 2026-11-10: a part that did nothing against the other side (an edge Twisted ignored) is not named on a side that moved the tier; what took edges or banes away leads the ", but" clause so its "it" sits next to them. A target with a roll of its own gets its own whole line, merged with targets that read the same; one that reads like the main roll's is left out. No line when nothing moved or held the tier, or when the recorded parts don't come to the recorded tier. Worked out when the card opens (James 2026-11-08), so fixes reach old rows. | ID | Where | Text | |---|---|---| | G12 | Why lead | Tier 3, up from Tier 2 / Tier 1, down from Tier 2 / Tier 2, not Tier 3 (something held a move) / Tier 2 (both sides would have moved it) / Tier 3 against Gwynhyvyr, up from Tier 2 (a target's own roll) | | G12a | Why text, the parts | {names} gave an edge / a double edge / a bane / a double bane; {name} raised it a tier / lowered it a tier / made it Tier 3 / made it Tier 1 / kept it from Tier 3 / kept it off Tier 1; {name} added 2 to the roll / took 2 off the roll; a natural 19 or 20 is always Tier 3 | | G12b | Why text, what took edges or banes away | after the edges it took were named: {name} ignored it / removed it / removed one; otherwise: {name} ignored an edge / removed a bane | | G12c | Why text, joining | parts joined with ", and" (A, B, and C); the other side after ", but ". e.g. Prone gave an edge, but Twisted ignored it. | | G12d | Why text, set by hand (signed off 2026-11-10) | An edge was set by hand. / Prone gave an edge, and another was set by hand. | | Z9 | The numbers, a modifier's flat bonus (after the edge and bane lines, with Z8; a trigger's with its owner's face) | {name} .... +2 / -2. The "Bonus" line under the characteristic keeps only what no modifier accounts for. |

docs.title: Round 15: names in the Why (signed off 2026-11-10)
docs.text:
James 2026-11-10: a source named "Target is Restrained" read as words, not a name, in "Target is Restrained gave an edge". Marking the name fixes it without changing the prose. Compared live: a tinted chip (flush and padded), bold, small caps, italic, gold. Small caps chosen first; James then compared small caps with square brackets on the busy card (2026-11-10) and chose brackets: they show where a many-word name starts and ends, and in many games a bracketed name is one you can hover. | ID | Where | Text | |---|---|---| | G13 | Why, every rule or ability name (the tier line's parts, a modifier's lead, a trigger's lead) | The name in square brackets; its owner stays outside: [Prone] gave an edge. / Dwarf Fury's [Twisted]. "Set by hand" and the plain "Trigger" lead are not names. The numbers keeps names plain. |

Hover (James 2026-11-10, chosen over an underline at rest on a busy live render): the name's mark alone (now the brackets) is the cue that a name can be hovered; every name with something to show hovers. The underline appears only under the name the pointer is on (the text engine draws no dotted underline). A modifier's hover shows the text the roll dialog's own hover showed (its name and description, formulas filled in for the roller, "Inflicted by"), recorded at the roll, each distinct text stored once per map; a trigger's shows its card. Names recorded before this have nothing to show and don't hover. Built in 2.3d.

docs.title: Round 16: a target's line says only what differed (signed off 2026-11-10)
docs.text: James 2026-11-10: on a busy card every target's line repeated the roll's parts. Only modifiers that applied are ever named (the dialog records only the modifiers that were on, and only what each changed), and a modifier is never named for a target it didn't apply to. The roll's line names what applied to every target; a target gets a line only when something that applied to it alone changed its tier, and that line names only those things. With no roll line (nothing shared moved the tier), "from" is the dice alone. When every target's own parts moved it, the roll's line keeps a tier no target ended on: it is what the roll did before anything about a target. | ID | Where | Text | |---|---|---| | G14 | Why lead, a target's line | Tier 2 against Goblin 1, down from Tier 3 ("from" is the roll line's tier) | | G14a | Why text, what differed | only that target's own parts: COVER gave a bane. | | G14b | Why text, a remover of the roll line's edges or banes | Goblin 2's CAST AWAY ALL HOPE ignored the double edge. / ignored the edge / ignored one edge / removed the bane |

docs.title: Round 17: one damage line that sums it up (signed off 2026-11-10)
docs.text: Replaces G1-G3 (a line per modifier, surges, immunity). Built like the tier line: what the damage came to, "up from" what the tier dealt alone (a kit is the hero's normal damage, so it is in "from" and never named), then the parts that changed it. Only when something besides the tier and kit changed the damage; G6 is unchanged. The shared line names what changed the damage of every target that took some; a target gets a line only for what applied to it alone. When targets started from different tier damage, the shared line gives only the extra ("12 extra damage"); if the shared parts took damage away there, there is no shared line and each target's line names everything, from its tier damage. Targets whose lines read the same share one. Modifier names in brackets (G13); surges and immunity plain. Each part says exactly what it changed; a modifier that adds different amounts on different tiers is not shared. Order: modifiers, surges, weakness; what lowered it after ", but". | ID | Where | Text | |---|---|---| | G15 | Why lead, the shared damage line | 19 damage, up from 15 / 6 damage, down from 8 / 8 damage (parts cancelled out) / 12 extra damage (targets on different tiers) | | G15a | Why text, what raised it | [Empyrean Boon] added 10 holy / [Upholding High Standards] added 2 / 2 surges added 2 each (Dwarf Fury's highest characteristic, Might 2) / 1 surge added 2 (...) / fire weakness 3 added 3 | | G15b | Why text, what lowered it, after ", but" | holy immunity 5 took 5 off / damage immunity 2 took 2 off / [Name] took 2 off | | G15c | Why lead, a target's damage line | 15 damage to Goblin 2, down from 20 ("from" is what the shared line gave that target) |

docs.title: Round 18: what players see (signed off 2026-11-10)
docs.text: The rule (REVIEW.md B5, James 2026-11-10): with Monster Info off, players see what the Action Log shows them; with it on, also what Monster Info has revealed. Immunity and weakness always show (the damage gives them away). A monster's ability card shows only with Monster Info on and that ability revealed; modifier hovers on a monster's roll never reach players; monster triggers stay Director only. Effects hidden from enemies, on a creature off the heroes' side, don't reach players. | ID | Where | Text | |---|---|---| | Z10 | The numbers, a monster's power roll | Its characteristic is not named: the stat block gives a flat number, so it joins the Bonus line ("Bonus .... +2"), for everyone. | | Z11 | The numbers, a roll hidden from players | Rolled in secret. (players: in place of the roll, with no tier lines in the Why; Director: above the numbers, after an eye) | | Z11a | Z11's eye, Director | tooltip: Hidden from players / Visible to everyone (the Action Log's words); clicking shows the roll to players or hides it again | | L28 | Secret modifier, Director (built here) | The name with an eye after it, tooltip: Hidden from players | | L28a | An effect hidden from enemies, Director's History line | the line with an eye after it, tooltip: Hidden from players |

Granted downtime rolls and fishing write nothing; project event rolls use the table line. | ID | What | Line | Cause line | |---|---|---|---| | L69 | A project roll | {Hero} rolled {n} | {Project} · project points {b} to {n} of {goal} | | L70 | For another hero's project | {Hero} rolled {n} | {Owner}'s {Project} · project points {b} to {n} of {goal} | | L71 | A breakthrough | L69 + Breakthrough tag | the second roll writes its own L69 | | L72 | A follower's roll | {Follower} rolled {n} | {Project} · project points {b} to {n} of {goal} | | L73 | A milestone reached | {Project} reached a milestone | The Director rolls a project event | | L74 | Completed | {Project} completed | {Hero} · project points {n} of {goal} | | L75 | Director adjusts points | {Project} project points {b} to {n} | Director |

Withdrawn 2026-11-19 (James): L69-L72 and L75. A project keeps its own rolls and adjustments, and the Respite shows what everyone rolled, so these lines only repeated them and crowded the respite out of History. docs.title: How a chunk is built here
docs.text:
Every capture chunk has the same three parts. 5.1d (respite, commit 31f73117) is the shortest worked example; read its diff before writing a new one.

  1. The rules code tells play observers. One call where the thing happens: GameSystem.NotifyPlayObservers("<moment>", ...). Keep it generic: say what happened, not what History should write. Hooks in DMHub Game Rules/ stay system-neutral.
  2. Draw Steel V/HistoryCapture.lua handles the moment. Add a handler and list it in the GameSystem.RegisterPlayObserver("history", {...}) table at the foot of the file. Start it with if not History.Enabled() then return end. Write a line with WriteLine (when it has a creature) or build an entry and call History.AddCombatFacts then History.Write.
  3. Draw Steel V/HistoryTray.lua words it. A branch in LineWords for the new family; the small text under a line is the entry's causetext. Add the family and any new fields to the HistoryEntry annotations in Draw Steel V/History.lua.

Things that are easy to get wrong:

  • One writer per event. Decide which client writes (the one that rolled, the host, the Director who clicked). Two clients writing the same event doubles it.
  • What players may read is cut in one place: ForPlayers in History.lua, applied when an entry is read. Put a new visibility rule there, never in the tray. The Director check is dmhub.isDM everywhere, the Codex's standard.
  • Wording comes from COPY.md. Anything not signed there is proposed to James first, in the reply, and built only after he agrees. Withdrawn lines are marked in COPY.md.
  • A line that opens a detail card must be listed in HasCard (HistoryTray) and handled in History.Story and the title code in HistoryCard.lua.
  • Does it earn a line? History answers "what just happened and why" during play. James cut the downtime roll lines because the project and the Respite already record them. When another surface already holds the record, write only what changes the table.

docs.title: Checking and committing
docs.text:
• Syntax: /d/dependencies/lua/bin/luac.exe -p "<file>"
  • Types (ceiling is zero): from PowerShell in the repo root, & D:\tools\lua-typing\check.ps1 -Files "<file>","<file>". To see the problems, pipe to Select-Object -First 30. A comment block placed between a function and its doc comment causes undefined-doc-param; keep doc comments directly above their function.
  • ASCII only in Lua, comments included.
  • Edits: several of these files are CRLF. Edit with exact-string replacement that keeps line endings (a small Python script using io.open(path, newline='') has worked all day).
  • Commit one chunk at a time: git -c core.autocrlf=false add -- <paths>, check git diff --cached --stat, then git commit -q -m "history: <what>" -- <paths>. Always name the paths: the index is shared. The pre-commit hook re-runs the type check.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
• Use the dev Codex, D:\dmhubclient\MCDMHub\Codex.exe, test game TwistedRainbowWaywornGuardian. It reads Lua straight from D:\draw-steel-codex.
  • Restart, do not reload. The bridge's reload does not reliably re-read changed files. Stop only the Codex.exe whose path is the dev one (leave any other codex.exe), then Start-Process it with -WorkingDirectory "D:\dmhubclient\MCDMHub" and -ArgumentList "--gameid","TwistedRainbowWaywornGuardian", and poll http://localhost:19876/health until inGame is true and loading is false. About 15 s.
  • Bridge: POST /execute with {"code": "<lua>"}; GET /screenshot; POST /mouse?action=move|click&x=&y=&button=left (send an empty body with -d ""). Use the bridge's virtual mouse, never the OS cursor.
  • Fed tests go on a scratch map. Write test entries with map = "probe-<name>". A fed entry with an encounter on a real map counts as an encounter and can push real rows out; that happened once today. Where a handler writes to game.currentMapId and cannot be redirected, feed only entries with no encounter, and tell James what you left behind.
  • Prefer the real code path over a fed notification. Today's best checks ran the real function on a detached object: creature:Rest on a DeepCopy of a Hero, DTProject:AddRoll on a project attached to no sheet. Neither changed the game.
  • Do not change James's game state without saying so first. Anything that heals, levels, completes a project or shows a banner to every client is his to run.
  • Engine changes: close the dev Codex and Unity, then powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "D:\dmhubclient\build.ps1" windows -DevKey in the background (1 to 2 minutes incremental). Success is 0 error CS lines and [BuildScript] Windows build succeeded in D:\dmhubclient\build-windows.log.

Fixed in the working copy: 1, 2, 3, 7-11 except 7 (see below), 12, 14 (fade only), 15, 16, 17 (RollUtils.NotifyTested and RollOnTableProperties.NotifyRolled are now failure-safe), 18, 19 (xpcall + traceback), 20, 21, 22, 23, 27, 28; minor: hover dwell, squad order, "1 surge", UndoResource not undoable, open card closes when its row goes, legacy "deprecated" effect ids, EncounterMontage doc comment. Mechanism notes: - 1 + 12: PanelDocument.OnRailLayoutApplied hook, run at the end of DocumentSystem's EnterGame coroutine (after the first-entry View and the update check) and after every ViewsApplyLayout. HistoryTray's own EnterGame handler is gone. - 2: History.lua Flush holds a batch for a document that reads isnew until EnterGame has fired (or the module loaded in a game); drops everything when not dmhub.inGame. - 13: standsInFor on a DockablePanel registration; History and the Action Log name each other, so a dock saved with one shows the other. - 6: table rolls and saves now carry rollInfo/details in their notify payloads; History records RollUtils.RollPrivacy.

No change needed: 24 (initiative is per map, and Revert Turn is clicked from the current map's bar, so the current map is the combat's); 11's opposed total (the card and tray only print totals when OpposedTotalsShown says so); EotW corner (rails rebuild on the setting change, which re-asks the custom interface for its corner); 26 left as is (it prunes inert expired instances; moving it to rules code changes nothing a player sees).

After the merge with main (the code is main's): Iron Grip logActorCondition, Immune to Forced Movement (needs wording), NoteStability before the immunity check, nested-invoke kit bonus. Not done (unmeasured perf): History.Keys caching, searchResults walk, MergeStyles per linger, GetConditionImmunities; g_links growth (small).

Later the same day (all signed by James): 7 and Malice (players see Malice lines only in Encounter of the Week; monster Stamina numbers follow the Stamina bar's rule) in 297c59da; 5 (unseen creatures) and the no-map Table record in 4404c634; 4 (notes), 14 (caption toast) and 25 (Turn Rewind by rewind point) in c6c68704; origin/main merged in b37e87e8; the post-merge items (immunity line and order, Iron Grip, nested kit bonus) in 85dcc34b. Live checks over the bridge, 2026-11-21 (merged branch): all passed. Enemy Stamina line (written with its key, hidden from players until Monster Info reveals it); Iron Grip escape (row credits the Null, 4 damage, rider note in the Why); Faster than the Eye on two targets, one Prone (Prone target's own roll 19 with one edge from Prone, the other 17); Get In Get Out's nested strike (Tier line "Cloak and Dagger +1"); audio caption bubble, still up with Chat in front; dock UI (caption toast; a docked Action Log restored as History); a new game's first entry (built-in Director View, History on the rail). Invoked abilities (James 2026-11-21, after a content scan: 263 actions invoke one that opens its own card): the row is always the outer ability. A Custom Ability invoke is a step of that ability (marked _tmp_partOfAbility on the clone) and joins its row whatever card it shows, so "Invoked Ability" rows are gone and Get In Get Out is one row. docs.title: 1. Fix before merge
docs.text:
1. New users never get their built-in View. Checked. HistoryTray.lua:6333 runs PlaceRailButton() synchronously on EnterGame; RailPlaceBelow("history", "chat") writes iconraillayout. DocumentSystem's EnterGame coroutine (DocumentSystem.lua:27224) waits for the documents layer + 5 frames, then finds iconraillayout non-empty, so nothingOfTheirs is false and ViewsSwitchTo("builtin:player"/"builtin:director") never runs. Every first entry to a game (layout is per-game). Crows same via the Action Log. Also: a pristine v6 user's rail no longer matches the stamp, so they get the "updated / Keep mine" prompt instead of a silent update. Fix: skip when the layout is empty (v7/v8 already place History), or run after the View auto-apply.
  2. A History write before the document has synced can wipe that map's History. Checked. History.lua:303 WriteEntries has no doc.isnew / loading gate; on an empty snapshot it seeds tables and CompleteChange PUTs over the cloud doc (the playlist wipe mechanism). Any capture while a client is still loading or rejoining. Fix: requeue while doc.isnew or the game is loading.
  3. Undo on a reverted resource line applies twice. Checked. HistoryTray.lua:2489 ignores entry.reverted. Revert Turn restores the Recovery, then Undo on the faded line takes the heal off and refunds the Recovery again. Same for Turn Rewind. Fix: and entry.reverted == nil.
  4. main's new Action Log Note behavior (f2a2b312) shows nowhere by default. Checked the path. ActionLogNoteChatMessage.Post (AbilityReplenish.lua:213) is a plain chat.SendCustom, which only the old Action Log renders, and it has no play-observer notify. A trigger whose only effect is the note writes no History row (ChangedTheTable, HistoryCapture.lua:412, ignores messages). The older Post callers (AbilityDamage.lua:482 bonus note, MCDMCreature.lua:7558 heal bonus) have the same gap. No data uses log_note yet; Condemned (Gerold) is the intended user.

  3. Monster Stamina numbers. Checked. staminaset (Capture:2200) and temporarystamina (Capture:1206) store exact values; the tray prints "X Stamina 40 to 25" (HistoryTray.lua:2217) with no Monster Knowledge gate.
  4. Malice lines in the rail badge and hover card. Checked. Unseen() (HistoryTray.lua:5944) runs every line through LineWords with no malice filter (the list and bubble both filter it). Players also get phantom unseen turns from ownerless Malice lines; the Director gets quiet Malice lines.
  5. Monster trigger cards through the ability title. Checked. AbilityCard falls back to TriggerCard (HistoryCard.lua:737); the header (:897) gates only on PlayersMaySeeAbility, which is revealed on any use. Breaks COPY Round 18.
  6. Side view of a token the player can't see. Checked. RowMovers (HistoryCard.lua:1032) tests token.valid, not canSee; the ghost shows its live appearance and path.
  7. Smaller: a hidden roll's total survives in who.opposed (History.lua:526); surge origin hovers (part.freefrom[i].hover, gainedfrom) aren't cleared by WithoutHovers (History.lua:535, card :2843). Malice filtering lives in the tray, not ForPlayers, so any new reader leaks it.

docs.title: 3. Old Action Log, Crows and dock-mode regressions
docs.text:
1. Applying a built-in View drops the Action Log for old-log and Crows users: ViewsApplyLayout (DocumentSystem.lua:27934) stores v7/v8 as-is (no "action log"), and PlaceRailButton runs only on EnterGame / the setting change. Crows on a pristine v6 view loses it for the session after the silent update.
  2. Dock mode loses a docked Action Log with nothing in its place. PanelPermittedForUser now checks available (DockablePanel.lua:2259); History is never added to a dock. Medium confidence (depends on rail-off users).

They moved from chat to the Chat rail bubble: they fade within about 1.3 s when Chat is in front (the bubble think at DocumentSystem.lua:17386 ignores evenInFront), and show nothing in dock mode, with Chat grouped/overflowed, or on the old log (Audio.lua:1238-1363). The 10 s freshness check compares two clients' server time (skews).
  4. The sidebar preview keeps running for old-log users. Checked. BubbleTick (HistoryTray.lua:6233) gates only on History.Enabled(); it sorts keys for every map every 0.5 s and builds bubble panels that ShowRailBubble then drops unattached. Fix: bail on History.UsingOldLog().
  5. History radial item (TokenUI.lua:2818) and card chip (HeroCardBack.lua:1559) show for old-log users and do nothing; gate on UsingOldLog(). The EotW HUD (EncounterOfTheWeekHud.lua:1220) reads UsingOldLog() once at build.

docs.title: 4. Robustness: a History error can stall play
docs.text:
1. Tests can hang. Checked. RollCustomPowerTableTest's completeRoll (MCDMCreature.lua:5517) calls NotifyTested before the pcall'd onComplete; the notify's own work (RollUtils.NotifyTested) is outside the observer pcall. A raise there leaves a montage or puzzle test waiting with its card hidden. Same order in ShowCharacteristicRollDialog (:5632, drops "rollpower" triggers) and DSRequestRollsDialog.lua:1104 (the Director's request waits forever). Fix: pcall or move after.
  2. A nil map drops the whole frame's batch. Checked. Flush (History.lua:355) indexes byMap[entry.map] outside the pcall after clearing g_waiting. Possible for off-map heroes (respites through GetCharacterById).
  3. HandEdit, ForCast, EndingEffects (Creature.lua:80, :98, :9105) pcall and re-raise with error(err, 0): every RemoveOngoingEffect, purge, end-of-turn removal and TacPanel hand edit now loses its stack trace in bug reports. Use xpcall(fn, debug.traceback).
  4. Roll details (AddRoll, AddDamageParts, AddRollTriggers, EdgeSources, Capture:792-833) run before History.Write; one error silently loses the row. The up-front spend's 0.5 s Schedule (Capture:1450) doesn't check token.valid.

docs.title: 5. Wrong or stale display
docs.text:
1. Merged "ended" lines never show Reverted (HistoryTray.lua:3668): the sig omits reverted; the rebuild also drops hidden/secret (HiddenEye missing) and appends to the shared sources table, widening the Director's Delete/Hide.
  2. Action row sig ignores nested-entry rewrites (HistoryTray.lua:3685): Hide/Reveal on a nested trigger or roll doesn't rebuild the row or open card; the menu keeps offering "Hide from players"; a revealed secret opposed roll stays "rolled in secret". Fix: tostring(kid) in the sig.
  3. Per-target roll data by loop index (MCDMAbilityRollBehavior.lua:2415-2460): with promptWhenResolving, every target reads multitargets[1]'s edges, banes, sources and surges. The in-play surge count has had the same bug since before the branch. main's b64b3c71 narrows it to forced-movement tiers. Match by tokenid.
  4. Lines filed under game.currentMapId (Malice with no caster Capture:1541, Hero Tokens 1568, downtime 1613, negotiation 1662, montage 1722, OnTurnReverted 2320): a Director looking at another map files them there, and Revert Turn marks nothing on the combat map.
  5. Turn Rewind still matches by time (History.lua:754, :775), the skew Revert Turn already fixed.
  6. OnTurnEnded (Capture:2365) runs ModifyProperties on every token with lapsed effects from inside History, on whichever client clicked End Turn, once per token in a group turn: game state that only changes when History is on.
  7. Card scroll maxHeight = args.maxHeight - 62 (HistoryCard.lua:3675) assumes a one-line header; a wrapped title runs the bottom past the frame.
  8. The fold-animation copy (HistoryTray.lua:5574) isn't MakeNonInteractiveRecursive: a map click in its 0.9 s flight can land on the copy.

docs.title: 6. Minor
docs.text:
• "Potency raised with %d surges" reads "1 surges" (HistoryCard.lua:3286); wording needs James's sign-off.
  • Squad-death rows in hash order (HistoryCard.lua:569); two hover dwell timers can open a hover twice (:806).
  • Iron Grip's escape damage ignores main's logActorCondition (AbilityDamage.lua:58); Immune to Forced Movement leaves no trace, and at AbilityInvokeAbility.lua:1502 NoteStability runs before the immunity check; nested-invoke strikes (3d0dce40) may drop the kit bonus part from the Tier line.
  • UndoResource's ModifyProperties is undoable (Ctrl+Z restores, line still says Undone).
  • Perf: History.Keys re-sorted per map on every BubbleTick and Unseen; searchResults tree walk per refresh; MergeStyles(Styles()) per linger and keystroke; GetConditionImmunities extra walk per InflictCondition.
  • Small leaks: g_links/g_linkIds, g_parsed, g_closing/g_falling/g_provoking; History.Clear leaves data.counts.
  • Open card left showing a deleted or filtered-out entry (HistoryTray.lua:4752).
  • Old saved effect instances share id "deprecated" (Creature.lua:9078).
  • NoteHistory sits under TotalsFromLog's doc comment (EncounterMontage.lua:338).

docs.title: Housekeeping before the PRs
docs.text:
• Two uncommitted HISTORYDIAG prints (MCDMAbilityRollBehavior.lua, EmbeddedRollDialog.lua).
  • Definitions/dmhub.lua stubs (CreatePath, MarkMovementArrow path) were hand-copied from engine feat/saved-movement-path (af03f472): land with that engine PR. HistoryCard pcalls the call.
  • Whole-codex type check on the merged tree not run.
  • Rules fix 4d265199 (ResetMods clears nonwastedSurges) reviewed correct; name it in the PR as a gameplay fix (strike-only surges can no longer be banked).

docs.title: Checked and clean
docs.text: Syntax (luac -p) and ASCII on all 59 changed files and the 24 merged shared files. Observers are pcall'd and re-register on reload without doubling; every handler is gated on History.Enabled() (Crows writes nothing); one writer per event; all CompleteChange calls are undoable = false and the document isn't checkpoint-registered; entries are compact JSON with a 500 cap and culling; wrappers keep return values and argument order; no nested ModifyProperties; no game.Refresh; no per-frame work beyond gated thinks; vscroll set at creation; Schedules guarded; cond() and forward declarations safe; old saved entries read safely in the card and tray; historyenabled referenced nowhere on main.

docs.title: History chunk 0.1: what a record costs
docs.text:
Measured 2026-11-06 in the live Codex (build 13), game TwistedRainbowWaywornGuardian, on a cloud game server, with two clients connected: Director and Player accounts on one machine (the app's "new player window"). The Director client wrote, the Player client watched. Scripts are in probes/; they run over the bridge (/execute), fill the ARG_ values with sed first.

The record used was as full as stage 2 will make it, to be safe: two targets, a roll, three named sources, one trigger, about 3.2 KB of JSON, most of it ids. A stage 0 record is much smaller.

docs.title: Result: nested records fail, packed records pass
docs.text:
The design said entries keyed by id, as BattleLog.RecordBattle does. Storing each entry as a nested table does not scale. BeginChange deep-copies the whole document and CompleteChange walks it twice to find the difference, so each write costs in proportion to every value in the document (about 100 values per record).

Storing each entry as one JSON string, still keyed by id, costs a tiny fraction of that, because a string is one value to copy and compare (ScriptSerialize.DeepCopy, LuaValuePatch).

Cost of one write, on the writing client, in ms (average; the worst single write in brackets):

Records in the document Nested table One JSON string Under 50 47 (155) 1 (3) 100 248 (550) 2 (3) 200 462 (695) 3 (5) 300 674 (929) 4 (5) 450 not run 7 (13) 600 not run 10 (67)

The nested run was stopped at 330: the Director client was down to about 2 frames a second. The worst packed writes (54 to 88 ms) came a few times a run, and are not tied to document size.

docs.title: The other client
docs.text:
• Idle, this client runs at 14 ms a frame, worst 41 ms.
  • At one write a second with 330 records (the realistic case), frames stay at 14 ms; around most arrivals one frame takes about 40 ms. That is the worst frame it shows idle anyway, so a write costs at most about 30 ms on the receiving client, on one frame.
  • At ten writes a second (far above real play) frames average 18.5 ms.
  • Each write arrived 0.8 s after it was stamped, flat at every size. Part of that may be the two clients' clocks; it reads as "under a second".

docs.title: Reading it back
docs.text:
On the Player client, in ms:

Records Document Find and sort the keys Parse the newest 40 Parse everything (search) 330 1.26 MB under 1 1 16 614 2.34 MB under 1 2 28

docs.title: Joining the game
docs.text: Restarting the Player client with 660 packed records in the document: the game snapshot went from 1.71 MB to 4.22 MB, and still completed 0.2 s after subscribing here. On a slow connection the extra size is what counts: about 0.4 MB per 100 full records.

docs.title: On the server
docs.text: All of a mod's documents share one row (game::modDocuments/{modid}), rewritten at most every 4 s while writes come in, and split automatically if it outgrows a row. So History's size is added to that row. It is not a limit at these sizes.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Entries are stored as JSON strings keyed by id. Same store, same merge behaviour, same document per map. The tray parses only the rows it builds, so opening it stays cheap.
  • One write per action, at the end of the cast. Writes are cheap enough now that this is about keeping a cast's facts together, not about cost. Stage 1 should still batch a cast's results.
  • Hard cap 500 entries. Two encounters fit: about 12 turns a round, 5 rounds, 3 entries a turn is 180 an encounter, and big fights reach 240. At 500 a write costs about 8 ms even with full-sized records and the document is at most about 1.9 MB. The cap is one constant, History.hardCap. Check it again in 6.2 with real records.

docs.title: History: design review before the build (2026-11-04)
docs.text: Inputs: an independent fresh-eyes review of the design and prototype; a coverage audit of today's Action Log; David's feedback after the demo; a rules review in four parts (rules-review/core.md, classes-1.md, classes-2.md, director.md, about 700 events). Details and code references: BRIEF.md Appendix X and the four rules files.

docs.title: Step by step (from 2026-11-05)
docs.text:
James asked to take this in small steps. Step 1 decided the rule below; step 2 sorts each gap by it and says whether the fix is code, data or both; then the fixes and decisions.

Step 1, decided 2026-11-05: what earns a place. Did it change the table? - Glance: Stamina up or down; a condition or effect starting or ending; moved by someone else, or falling; resources (Heroic Resource, surges, Malice, Hero Tokens, Recoveries); winded, dying, death, minions dying. - Card only: what explains a number (edges and banes, kit bonuses, potency, immunity amounts, which surge went where). - Left out: what changed nothing (walking on your own turn, a trigger that did nothing, a start of turn where nothing happened). - Exception (James, 2026-11-06): a roll the table watched gets a line even if it changed nothing, so a failed save shows, at the end of that turn, with Active on it.

Step 2: the gaps, one at a time. Gaps 1 and 2 below turned out to share one cause, so there are five: (1) results with no card or authored message; (2) effects ending; (3) winded, dying, death, minion deaths; (4) Malice; (5) passive modifiers unnamed.

Gap 1, checked in data 2026-11-05. Prompted triggers (the player is asked, e.g. Wellspring of Grace through the shared "Spend Recovery" prompt) already post a card; what they lose is the cause. Truly automatic ones (no question asked) show nothing without a typed message: Righteous Phalanx (15 damage on entering, classes/conduit.yaml:12006), Edict of Unyielding Resolve (10 temporary Stamina each turn, characterongoingeffects/ edict-of-unyielding-resolve.yaml:52), start-of-turn area damage (MCDMCreature.lua:7144). History replaces the Action Log, so today's cards and typed messages have nowhere else to show; History writes its own lines.

Marker effects (proposed 2026-11-05, James's idea): ongoing effects already carry the editor's "Hidden" checkbox (statusEffect = false, DMHub Compendium/OngoingEffectEditor.lua:182; 83 effects, Righteous Phalanx Target among them), which every token and sheet display honours (DMHub Token UI/TokenUI.lua:337). History leaves Hidden effects out. "Hidden from enemies" (26) follows the token rule. "Hidden on token" (98) is mixed: markers (Moved This Turn, Blitz Tracking, Chain Reaction Target) and real effects (Vanish, Levitate, Rivalry), so History shows them and the pure markers get "Hidden" ticked in data. Withdrawn the same day: "Hidden" also takes an effect off the Tac panel's chips, the only place a Director removes it by hand (James). The markers need their own History signal; the list is in marker-effects.md. Decided 2026-11-05 (James): a new checkbox on ongoing effects, ticked on markers, keeps them out of History and changes nothing else. Its label waits on the feature's name, which James reopened the same day.

Gap 1 closed 2026-11-05 (James). Code: History records damage, healing, temporary Stamina, conditions and resources where they happen, names the cause, and skips changes that changed nothing (temporary Stamina keeps the greater amount, DSTemporaryHitpoints.lua:6). Lingering area damage goes through one function (creature:AuraDamage, MCDMCreature.lua:7144), so one fix covers Wall of Fire, monster auras and zones. Data: tick "Hidden from History" (COPY.md H1) on the markers in marker-effects.md once James has checked the list. Prompted triggers already post a card; they gain their cause.

Gap 2, where effects end (checked 2026-11-05). A handful of places, not one per ability: removal (creature:RemoveOngoingEffect/BySeq, RemoveMatchingOngoingEffects, RemoveOngoingEffectsOnTrigger, PurgeCondition: saves, abilities that end a condition, dying, end of encounter, by hand); end of turn and end of round (creature:EndTurn, creature:EndRound, DMHub Game Rules/Creature.lua:11183, :11230); a sustain formula failing (creature:RefreshToken tidy-up, :6134); timers and concentration that lapse quietly (CharacterOngoingEffectInstance:Expired, OngoingEffect.lua:531, filtered out with no removal; History checks them at each turn end). Persistence adds its own piece (creature:EndPersistentAbilityById, MCDMCreature.lua:7512) for the cause and for walls and areas, which are not effects on a creature. Gap 2 closed 2026-11-05 (James): the broad fix plus the persistence piece; effects that end together are grouped (one line per turn end; one closing entry for the encounter, listing what ended by creature). Wording in the later sign-off round.

Gap 3, winded, dying, death, minion deaths (checked 2026-11-05). Detected in two places, taking damage (MCDMCreature.lua:6806-6871) and Stamina set directly, e.g. a hand edit (:7069-7083); each fires an event and a sound, never a log entry. Confirmed minion deaths fire once per batch (squadminiondeaths, :6109). Proposal: captions on the row that caused it (T14, signed off), a line when nothing did, recovery shown too, minions only once confirmed. Gap 3 closed 2026-11-05 (James), as proposed. Code only.

Gap 4, Malice (checked 2026-11-05). Correction to section 1: spending Malice on an ability already posts a card everyone sees (MaliceSpentChatMessage, DSResources.lua:272). Every other change goes only to the Director's counter tooltip. All changes pass through CharacterResource.SetMalice (DSResources.lua:79) with a reason already attached (start of combat, each round's gain, traits, "Manually set", end of combat), so the fix is one hook. Open: the rules leave it to the Director whether players see Malice (CRM:785-790). Who sees what today (from code, 2026-11-05): gains are Director-only (the action-bar counter's tooltip, the Encounter Wrangler). Players see every spend card, and a Malice tracker the Director places on the table as public (DMHub Game Hud/TableDice.lua:2316), whose hover shows the same history with reasons (:2641). So the codex's "Director's choice" is that tracker; the earlier "on by default" proposal was withdrawn. Revised proposal: keep today's split in History (players see spends, the Director sees every change); sharing stays the public tracker's job. Gap 4 closed 2026-11-05 (James), with the revised proposal. Code only (one hook in SetMalice); no new setting.

Gap 5, passive numbers (checked 2026-11-05). Card only by the rule (they explain a number). Most names already exist in three places: roll modifiers kept by the roller (rollProperties.modifiersUsed, DSRollDialog.lua:3963), kit bonuses written onto the ability ("Includes +2 damage from {kit} kit", MCDMKit.lua:475), immunity and weakness in the damage code. Left over: changes made outside a roll, e.g. healing halved through the "Stamina Regain Halved" attribute (ActivatedAbility.lua:5089), where the code knows the change but not which effect caused it. Possible data side: a bonus written straight into a formula instead of a named modifier shows as an unexplained total. Generic answer (James asked for no per-ability code, 2026-11-05): creature:DescribeModifications (DMHub Game Rules/Creature.lua:7147) and DescribeModificationsToNamedCustomAttribute (MCDMCreature.lua:222) already list every modifier that changed an attribute, with the value before and after; the Hero sheet's stat sources use them (EotwHeroSheetData.lua:424-477). So each place a number lands (the gap 1 hooks) asks those for the attributes it read. Any ability, item or DLC built from modifiers is named with no new code; only content that bypasses modifiers (a script editing numbers, a bonus typed into a formula) cannot be. Gap 5 closed 2026-11-05 (James), with the generic approach. Step 2 is done: all five gaps closed. Still open from it: James checks marker-effects.md; the new line wording (trigger results, temporary Stamina, effects ending and grouped endings, recovering from winded or dying) goes in one sign-off round. Next: the fixes in section 2, one at a time, then the decisions in section 3 (decision 1 is mostly settled by the gaps; its open part is whether F8 and F9 join the first build).

docs.title: 1. The big finding: History has to record at the source, not from chat
docs.text:
Most of what players can't explain never reaches today's log, for a handful of reasons: - Automatic triggers post no ability card (TriggeredAbility:ShowChatMessageOnCast returns not mandatory, TriggeredAbility.lua:2644; mandatory is the default). Their per-target results are written onto that card, so with no card they are dropped (ActivatedAbility.lua:3174). Their damage still shows when the author filled in the damage behavior's chat message (AbilityDamage.lua:56), and immunity/weakness always posts its own line. (Correction 2026-11-05: an earlier wording said they post nothing.) - Chat and the log are split by a filter: everything that is not plain chat goes to the Action Log (ChatPanel/ActionLogPanel.lua:31), so nothing log-worthy is stuck in chat. - Damage, healing, temporary Stamina and resource lines appear only when the content author typed a chat message on that behavior. Flat rule-text damage ("2 fire damage") posts nothing. So coverage depends on authoring, ability by ability. - Nothing records an effect ending: end of turn, saves, dying, end of combat, a sustain condition lost, persistence broken (the Elementalist's 5 x Reason rule only shows floating text, elementalist.yaml:4869). - Winded, dying, death and minion deaths are events with sounds, never entries. Minion deaths are chosen by whoever hit the squad, so History must record the confirmed deaths. - Malice changes are recorded only in a hover tooltip on the Director's counter. - Passive numbers (kit bonuses, captain, auras, the Mark) fold into rolls unnamed.

Proposal R: record at the source. History does not read chat. Each family of event is written where the game already handles it, so every ability and trait is covered without per-ability authoring, and the old chat cards can stay as they are. | Family | Recorded at | Shows as | |---|---|---| | F1 Actions, prompted triggers | ActivatedAbility:Cast | action row | | F2 Automatic triggers (traits, auras, class features) | the triggered cast, mandatory too | nested under its cause, else a line naming the feature | | F3 Damage, healing, temporary Stamina from any source (auras, terrain, start/end of turn, falls, collisions, hand edits) | the damage, heal and temporary Stamina code | numbers on the action, or a line with its source | | F4 Effects and conditions starting and ending, with why | inflict / remove condition and ongoing effect, persistence end, end of combat, dying | condition badges, "Ended" lines | | F5 Thresholds: winded, dying, death, confirmed minion deaths, strained, rampage, captain changes | the existing creature events | captions and lines | | F6 Resources with a structured cause: Heroic Resource, surges, Malice, Hero Tokens, Recoveries, Victories, losses at end of combat | the resource code (it already keeps a stat history) | lines, chips | | F7 Movement: push, pull, slide, stability, teleport, falls, collisions, wall breaks, with the path | AbilityRelocateCreature | captions, side view, map arrow | | F8 Rolls and play without an action: tests, montages, negotiation, respite, downtime, Dice panel, tables | the roll and those panels | compact rows | | F9 Director actions: reinforcements, villain actions, overrides, hand edits, reveals | the Director's tools | lines (players see what was visible) | | F10 Named modifiers for Why lines | roll dialog modifiersUsed, the damage code | Why lines | Recommendation: F1-F7 and F10 in the first build (every combat); F8 and F9 next.

docs.title: 2. Fixes (taken one at a time from 2026-11-05)
docs.text:
Adopted: B1, B2, B3 with "{n} new below" counting rows (2026-11-05). B4 part 1 adopted 2026-11-05: side-view icon button on the movement caption; hovering it draws the movement arrow on the map. The engine change (draw an arrow and the side view from a saved start or path) is built here and proposed as an engine PR (James). James added: a faded ghost of the creature at its start square. The engine already has it, CharacterToken:CreateGhost(loc) (Definitions/CharacterToken.lua:497, used by the Monster AI's plan preview), so no engine change for that; a creature whose token is gone (a dead minion) gets no ghost. B4 part 2 adopted 2026-11-05: "Resisted" caption (T14), numbered faces on shared portraits, the gold badge becomes a diamond (the quiet count stays a circle). B5 adopted 2026-11-05: players see what they could see live. Spoiler modifiers follow the existing reveal (PowerRollSpoilers, Timeline/EmbeddedRollDialog.lua:437); minion Stamina and a monster's own numbers follow Monster Info unless the live roll showed them. Y13 without the number goes to the wording round. B6 adopted 2026-11-05: "+N" when faces don't fit, identical results grouped (pattern to the wording round), details built when opened. B7 adopted 2026-11-05: the card opens on the side with room, else inside the tray with a way back (label to the wording round); glance text at least 11 px at 100% Font Size. B8, "Active" decided 2026-11-05: always shown, in tray and card, as a small tag on the condition badge only. B8 adopted in full 2026-11-05: "Tier 1" everywhere ("<=11" under it on the roll card only), search finds "turn 15", S5 now reads: Nothing matches "{search}". All eight fixes adopted. Wording still to propose (one round): trigger and temporary Stamina lines, effects ending and grouped endings, recovering from winded or dying, Y13 without minion Stamina, grouped identical results, the in-tray card's way back.

Built into the prototype 2026-11-05 (artifact UPWo9XvYuaDiZ388xRES35, version 19; source in the session scratchpad actionlog-proto/project/Main.dc.html; checks check3-6.js pass, and each fix was looked at in the browser). Scenario additions so every fix shows: Zakaarior's free strike inside Test Monster Z 1's turn (B2); the Power Roll Test also hits the Tactician, Censor and Shadow for 10 each (B6 "+3" and grouping); a secret "Ambusher" edge on round 1's axe (B5); a "Window: wide/narrow" demo button (B7). Draft lines in the prototype, for the wording round: "5 damage was enough to kill one minion."; "Knocked prone: it did not resist"; "{names} each took {n} damage."; "Taken, each"; "Back"; the button's tooltip "Side view"; the free strike's "Free strike" and "Moved away without shifting" Why line. Not shown in the prototype: damage and healing apart in a fold (Zakaarior sits behind "+N"; checked in code), the card opening on the other side, lazy building.

James's review of the build, 2026-11-06 (prototype version 21). - Target cells: face on the left, number and full name beside it, captions on the line below. One target takes the full width; two to four sit in two columns; past four, three cells and "+N" with the rest named beside it. "Ally hit" became a caption on the cell (T13). Rows are about half their old height. The tier pill sits on the caption line so names aren't cut. - Side-view button: sits on the movement caption's line. Icon is the real Phosphor glyph phosphor/arrow-elbow-right-down-bold.png (the full ~9k set is in StreamingAssets/phosphor-icons.zip, any name works; assets.GetPhosphorIcons searches it). - David's preview (D2), which had been parked in decision 2: when an action finishes and History is closed or minimised, a "what happened" card shows beside the rail button or block for about five seconds (longer with the pointer on it); never over an open tray; clicking opens History on that action; gives way to the hover preview. The prototype's "Beside History" button stands in for the setting. Setting wording goes to the wording round. D1 (own rail slot) stays in decision 2.

Font check for wording (2026-11-06, read from the TextMeshPro assets). Berling is a static atlas. Not available: the arrow U+2192 and less-or-equal U+2264 (no label font's table has them; Berlingske Regular's fallback Newzald-Medium is dynamic and its source has them, but Bold has no fallbacks, so it can't be relied on). DrawSteelGlyphs has no arrow (it has the tier glyphs). Labels have no inline images, so a Phosphor arrow can't sit inside a sentence. Available: middle dot, en dash, times, single guillemet, curly quotes. Minus U+2212 is Regular-only through a fallback, so bold numbers in the Codex use a plain "-". Lua source stays ASCII, so these go in as byte escapes. This hits T5 ("Malice +{n} → {n}") and the card's "Stamina a → b" notes.

Wording group 1 signed off 2026-11-06 (COPY.md Round 4), with the caret rule: a lone number shows the new value, the Builder's caret (HeroSheetCard.Mark) and the size of the change; inside a sentence, "to". The players' round heading drops Malice, matching gap 4. Prototype version 22, with two sample lines: Reactor 1's Wall of Fire damage (turn 14) and the Troubadour's temporary Stamina (turn 15).

Reversed the same day after James tried it (prototype version 23): carets are out; they read like a sum and red clashed with the Builder. Every changed number now reads "{before} to {now}". Wording group 2 signed off with an Ended tag and the failed save line (COPY.md Round 4). The axe in turn 8 now slows Zakaarior (save ends) so his failed save shows in turn 12.

Wording round complete 2026-11-06: groups 1-5 signed off (COPY.md Round 4, L0-L38); no drafts left in the prototype. Still open: James checks marker-effects.md; decisions 1 (F8 and F9 scope), 2 (defaults, rail, whether the preview and notifications stay two settings), 3 (several maps), 4 (revert, undo, Director tools), 5 (out of combat, retention); then the build plan.

Decision 2 closed 2026-11-06 (James): own rail button below Chat; starts closed for everyone (he declined "on for the Director"); two settings stay; the rail button keeps the badge when the tray is off the table. Decision 3 closed 2026-11-06 (James): one History, following the map last clicked unless the pointer is on the tray or a card is open; a switcher only while two maps are in combat; badge and preview cover every map you can see; search covers the shown map and its previous encounter. Decision 4 closed 2026-11-06 (James): reverted rows stay, faded, tagged Reverted, out of the totals, with a Turn reverted line; History's document stays out of checkpoint backups. Undo stays on resource lines. Director tools stay on right-click (COPY.md L39-L42). Decision 5, three of four closed 2026-11-06 (James): Out of combat heading with compact lines; retention as above, across sessions, subject to the engine's document limits; ability card on hover in the card header (COPY.md L43-L45). Typed messages talked through: 759 fields in the data, 530 different messages, 210 identical to the ability name, but others carry real explanation ("Gained 2 surges (target killed, winded, or bleeding)"), so "ignore them" would lose information. Decision 5 closed 2026-11-06 (James): typed messages never reach the glance; in the card's Why they show as written unless they only repeat the ability's name. Decision 1 closed 2026-11-06 (James): all ten families before release (this replaces the "F1-F7 and F10 first" recommendation in section 1). Stages: combat first, then out of combat and Director actions. History runs beside the old log, off by default, until the last stage, then the old log goes in the same step that turns History on for everyone. All review decisions are closed. The prototype caught up with decisions 2-5 on 2026-11-06 (version 26; every item looked at in the browser): starts closed; Chat and History on separate rail buttons, History with Phosphor's clock-counter-clockwise-bold; rail badge; History notifications control; map switcher with a sample "Old Mill" fight; Reverted rows with a Turn reverted line; Out of combat; ability card on hovering the detail card's title; a typed message sample in turn 5's Why. Not in the prototype: Undo on resource lines, the Director's right-click menu, History following the last-clicked map. Next: the build plan. Prototype changes are batched until the fixes are through.

  • B1 Numbers on the glance are what landed: a face shows the total taken including nested triggers; folds show damage and healing separately; captions use taken numbers.
  • B2 An actor face on a row whose actor isn't the turn's only creature (a Director's group turn); an action with no cause sits as a line in the turn it happened in.
  • B3 Nothing moves under the reader: no folding while the pointer is on the tray or a card is open; the selected turn never folds; when scrolled up, hold position and show "{n} new below".
  • B4 Signals that are not hover-only or colour-only: the side view gets an icon button on the movement caption (drop "Hover here for the side view"); hovering it also draws the movement arrow on the map (David); a "Resisted" caption; duplicate portraits numbered; the gold badge carries a shape, not colour alone. (The hero card's hover chip stays: James's constraint.)
  • B5 One visibility rule: the record shows players what they saw live; spoiler modifiers stay redacted until revealed; anything not shown live (a monster's characteristic in a Why line, minion Stamina) follows Monster Info.
  • B6 Scale: a "+N" face when a strip or fold is full; identical outcomes grouped ("Goblins 1-4 each took 6"); results built lazily.
  • B7 Font Size and narrow windows: the card opens on the side with room, or inside the tray when there is none; glance text never smaller than 11 px at 100%.
  • B8 Wording: one tier label everywhere ("Tier 1", the badge showing "<=11" under it only on the roll card); "Nothing in this encounter matches" becomes "Nothing matches"; search accepts "turn 15"; "Active" shows the same way in tray and card. New wording in this block for sign-off: "{n} new below", "Nothing matches "{search}"."

docs.title: 3. Decisions, one per round
docs.text:
1. What History records (Proposal R above), and the first-build scope.
  2. Defaults, the rail and notifications: History on its own rail slot, not in the Chat group (David); what is on by default for players and the Director; the brief preview beside the button or block when History is closed, reusing the chat speech bubble, with a setting (David); the badge when the tray is off the table; the new-rows marker on an open tray.
  3. Several maps, each in its own combat: one History per map, or one that follows the focused map.
  4. Revert Turn, undo and the Director's tools: strike-through or erase on revert; Delete, Hide from players, Clear; Undo on resource lines.
  5. Out of combat and keeping history: how play without rounds groups; how long History keeps things between encounters and sessions; the ability card on hover; content authors' own lines.

docs.title: 4. Possible rules bugs found along the way (not History work)
docs.text: The rules agents noted implementation differences from the rules. None are verified; each needs checking against the book before anyone changes code. Lists: core.md "Surprises", classes-1.md "Rules deviations noticed", classes-2.md "Surprises and data issues", director.md "Gaps in rules automation". Examples: no damage for being thrown cleanly through a wall; save-ends effects continuing after combat; Prophecy marked Gold with no modifiers; Quick and Brutal granting a maneuver where the rule grants a main and a move action; Materialize using a flat 2 instead of Reason; features not implemented (Warmaster, Masterwork, Templar, Oracular Visions and others).

docs.title: How the codex decides what reaches the log
docs.text:
1. Automatic triggers post no cast card. TriggeredAbility.mandatory defaults to true (DMHub Game Rules/TriggeredAbility.lua:967); ShowChatMessageOnCast() returns not self.mandatory (:2644). Heroic Resource gains use the setting id game:heroicresourcetriggers ("Automated Heroic Resource Gains", default on, :44-51), a truthy string, so they post no cast card either.
  2. So an automatic event shows only if a behavior posts its own card, and most only do when the content author typed a chatMessage:
  3. Replenish (resource gain/spend): ResourceChatMessage when chatMessage is set or the behavior names a heroic-resource checklist item (DMHub Game Rules/AbilityReplenish.lua:717-728).
  4. Damage: ActivatedAbilityDamageChatMessage only when chatMessage is non-empty (Draw Steel Ability Behaviors/AbilityDamage.lua:55-57); dice damage also opens a roll.
  5. Heal (DMHub Game Rules/ActivatedAbility.lua:5136), temporary Stamina (Draw Steel Core Rules/DSTemporaryHitpoints.lua:136), purge effects (DMHub Game Rules/AbilityPurgeEffects.lua:286): only with a chatMessage.
  6. ApplyOngoingEffect, rule-text commands (slides, pushes, conditions, flat damage), Destroy, Script, FloatText: never. RecordTokenMessage writes into a cast card only if one exists (ActivatedAbility.lua:3173-3180).
  7. Prompted triggers (mandatory: false) post a cast card when the player accepts; outcomes sit in the portrait hover.
  8. Nothing logs an effect ending. There is no chat type for it. "Until the end of the encounter or until you are dying" effects are removed silently by creature:StartOnDying and creature:EndCombat (Draw Steel Core Rules/MCDMCreature.lua:8119-8135). An effect whose sustainFormula stops being true also just disappears.
  9. Unspent Heroic Resource is never "lost" as an event. The resource has clearOutsideOfCombat: true (characterresources/heroic-resource.yaml); the stored value is tied to the combat id and reads as 0 afterwards (DMHub Game Rules/Resource.lua:48-107).
  10. Passive numbers fold into rolls. Edges, banes, damage and potency modifiers appear only inside the roll; the roll record keeps the kept modifier names (rollProperties.modifiersUsed, Draw Steel UI/DSRollDialog.lua:3963-3976). Triggered options used from the roll dialog pay their cost silently (DSRollDialog.lua:3864-3881).

Logged today codes. RES = resource line with the quoted reason. DMG = damage line with the quoted text. TMP = temporary Stamina line. NOTE = ActionLogNoteChatMessage. CAST = cast card (prompted trigger accepted, or ability used). ROLL = only inside a roll. CHIP = immunity/weakness chip (DamageModifierChatMessage). FLOAT = floating text over the token, not in the log. NO = nothing.

Row types. Action = action row. Nested = triggered row under what set it off. Turn line / Resource line / Ended line = compact lines with no action. Why = detail-card Why line.

docs.title: Rules deviations noticed (not History work, but they change what History would say)
docs.text:
• Prophecy (Oracle 5th) is marked Gold (implementation: 4) with no modifiers: s/oracle.yaml:531.
  • Most Pious adds to every start-of-turn piety gain, not only when praying (c/conduit.yaml:1177; both a/piety-table.yaml and a/prayer-table.yaml read the attribute).
  • War domain triggers on a single hit dealing >= 10 + Level; the rule is a creature taking > 10 + level damage in one turn (s/war-domain.yaml:118, R:9424-9425).
  • Berserker Growing Ferocity 8 gives 2 surges from level 4 whenever ferocity is 4+ (quantity: 2 When Level >= 4 else 1, s/berserker.yaml:1319); Reaver checks ferocity.
  • Fury winded/dying: two separate 1d3 gains per encounter (c/fury.yaml:2563, 2684); R:12825 reads as one.
  • Inertial Dampener deals psychic damage on forced movement in the codex, not in this rules text (e/null-field.yaml:283).
  • Triggered Essence (c/elementalist.yaml:4615) is always automatic; other classes' "first time each round" gains follow the "Automated Heroic Resource Gains" setting.
  • Not implemented: Oracular Visions, Templar, Avatar's maneuver, Arrest's redirect, Chronokinetic Mastery surges, Discipline Mastery 12 temporary Stamina, The Green Defends Its Servants' explosion, Chaos Incarnate's fear, the outside-combat lockout.

docs.title: Reason strings in today's resource lines are inconsistent
docs.text: "Start of Turn" (Censor, Fury), "Begin Turn" (Elementalist), "Start of Turn (Discipline)" (Null), "Conduit Prayer" (Conduit); "Draw Steel" for combat start; free text such as "You slide a creature.", "Ally Aided Another!", "Creature Damaged". History should not show these strings; it needs a structured cause (feature id + trigger kind) so the line and the Why can be worded consistently.

docs.title: History rules review: Shadow, Tactician, Talent, Troubadour, Beastheart, ancestries, kits
docs.text:
Audit date 2026-11-04. Scope: class features, Heroic Resource rules, subclass features, ancestry traits and kit rules that fire on their own or change numbers without an action, plus abilities whose effect sets up a later automatic event. Ordinary abilities used as actions are skipped. Code and data were read, not run; nothing was checked in the app.

Paths. R:n = ClaudeBridge/ClaudeRefHeroes.lua line n (the Heroes book as text). B:n = beastheart-reference.md line n (it sits at the repo root, not in Draw Steel Beastheart/). Data paths are under data/objectTables/: c/ classes, s/ subclasses, e/ characterongoingeffects, cd/ charconditions, anc/ races, k/ kits, a/ adventuretables, sa/ standardabilities, g/ globalrulemods; m/ is data/monsters/. The YAML line is the feature or trigger that does the work. Implementation tags quoted as Gold/Silver/Bronze/Unimpl are the data's own implementation field (4/3/2/1).

Draft lines are proposals for sign-off, in COPY.md style (past tense, result first, names not pronouns, Hero and Stamina capitalised, conditions lower case inside sentences). Example names: Human Shadow, High Elf Tactician, Time Raider Talent, Polder Troubadour, Orc Beastheart and their companion Wolf.

docs.title: How the codex decides what reaches the log (same mechanism as classes-1.md)
docs.text:
1. Automatic triggered abilities never post a cast card: TriggeredAbility.mandatory defaults to true (DMHub Game Rules/TriggeredAbility.lua:967) and ShowChatMessageOnCast() returns not self.mandatory (:2644). Heroic Resource triggers use the setting id game:heroicresourcetriggers (a truthy string), so they post no cast card either.
  2. An automatic event is visible only when one of its behaviors posts its own card, and nearly all of them do so only when the author typed a chatMessage (Replenish, Damage, Heal, Grant Temporary Stamina, Purge Effects). Heroic Resource gains linked to a class checklist item always post a resource line whose reason is the checklist name (DMHub Game Rules/AbilityReplenish.lua:661-728), which also gates them once per round/encounter (:348-366).
  3. Flat damage from an automatic trigger with no chatMessage is silent: the damage roll is deterministic, so the roll dialog resolves it with silent = true (Timeline/EmbeddedRollDialog.lua:6890-6936).
  4. Prompted triggers (mandatory: false) post a cast card when accepted; per-target results sit in its hover.
  5. Power-table triggered actions (behavior: powertabletrigger, e.g. Defensive Roll, Parry, Repel) are taken inside another creature's roll or damage dialog; they post nothing of their own (Draw Steel Core Rules/PowerTableTriggers.lua has no chat call).
  6. Passive edges, banes, damage bonuses and cost changes fold into the roll. The roll record keeps the kept modifier names (Draw Steel UI/DSRollDialog.lua:3963-3976) but no card shows them as a reason. Kit bonuses are folded into the ability text before the roll; the ability card says "Includes +2 damage from Shining Armor kit" (Draw Steel Core Rules/MCDMKit.lua:471-476), the log says nothing.
  7. Effects ending (by duration, on dying, at end of encounter, or by a Purge with no chatMessage) are never logged. Recoveries spent because a feature allowed it log as a bare "Use Recovery" resource line with no cause (g/triggers.yaml:14-51).

Logged today codes. RES = resource line with the quoted reason. DMG = damage line with the quoted text. TMP = temporary Stamina line. HEAL = Stamina regained line. PURGE = effects removed line. CAST = cast card (ability used or prompted trigger accepted). ROLL = only inside a roll. CHIP = immunity/weakness chip (DamageModifierChatMessage). FLOAT = floating text over the token, not in the log. NO = nothing.

Row types. Action = action row. Nested = triggered row under what set it off. Turn line / Resource line / Ended line = compact lines with no action. Why = detail-card Why line (lead / sentence, COPY.md R1).

docs.title: Counts
docs.text:
241 rows: Shadow 38, Tactician 37, Talent 41, Troubadour 41, Beastheart 33, ancestries 37, kits 14. Some rows group several features of one kind (strained riders, condition immunities, saving-throw thresholds, performances, Melodrama events, companion advancements), so the number of distinct rule events covered is about 330.

By today's logging (first code in the column): 59 rows produce a text line of their own (RES/DMG/TMP/PURGE, sometimes alongside a cast card), 38 only a cast card, 11 only an immunity chip, 25 live only inside a roll, 95 produce nothing, and 13 were not verified.

docs.title: Gaps that matter most
docs.text:
1. Effects ending are invisible. I'm No Threat ending when the Shadow harms someone, Careful Observation lost by striking another creature first, Fake Your Death ending on damage, Mind Projection snapping back, force orbs lost, Mark ending when the Tactician is dying, a performance ending because the Troubadour is dazed, Shadowmeld exits: all silent. This is the same class of gap as the Elementalist's persisting ability.
  2. Talent strain is half visible. End-of-turn negative-clarity damage is logged ("Strain damage"), but becoming and stopping being strained is not, and six strained riders that hurt the Talent (Mind Spike, Spirit Sword, Materialize, Flashback, Perfect Clarity, Gravitic Nova) have no damage text. Psion's opt-out is not implemented.
  3. Rampage thresholds are not announced. Reaching 8 (rampaging) or 12 (immunity) leaves no record; the 16, 20 and 24 effects are display-only and not automated; the mandatory end-of-turn Feral Strike is a prompt, so a declined prompt breaks the rule silently.
  4. Heroic Resource lines lack their cause. Every gain is logged, but only with a checklist name ("Damage the Marked", "A Creature is Force Moved"); the creature, roll or forced movement that caused it is not linked, and losses (end of encounter, Spotlight's unspent resource, Borrow From the Future's lockout) are not logged.
  5. Triggered actions taken from the roll dialog have no entry. Defensive Roll, In All This Confusion, Clever Trick, Parry, Advanced Tactics, Repel, Again, The Pack Defends, Pyre, Draconian Guard, Resist the Unnatural, Foresight, Keeper of Order, Turnabout, Harmonize, Take Two!, Deleted Scene and Command change a result with no trace. History needs them as nested rows with the ability's Trigger line (COPY R3).
  6. Passive number changes have no Why. Mark's edge, kit damage and stability bonuses, Field Arsenal's choice, Improved Field Arsenal / Master of Arms / Grandmaster of Arms, Barbed Tail, Hit 'Em Hard!'s surges, Coat the Blade's poison, Stormheart, Psi Boosts and Trained Assassin fold into the roll; the kit bonus is only on the ability card.
  7. Recoveries spent because of a feature show only "Use Recovery". Revitalizing Limerick, Mark's benefit, Mind Game, Stay Strong and Focus!, Mindlink and Too Slow all heal through the same bare line; the reader cannot tell why a Hero regained Stamina.
  8. Automatic damage without text is silent. Stoned's failed-save damage, Mind Snare and Incinerate (not verified), falling after Wings give out, and the missing Continuity Error and Love Song effects. Whether an automatic event is visible depends entirely on whether the content author typed a chatMessage (Ballad of the Beast's surge is logged; Legendary Drum Fill's is not).

docs.title: Surprises and data issues found on the way
docs.text:
• c/troubadour.yaml Love Song and Continuity Error apply ongoing effects (598e4a51..., 2d5c18d6...) that do not exist anywhere in data/; the damage redirect and the start-of-turn 1d6 corruption cannot happen.
  • Materialize's strained damage (splash and self) is a flat 2, not the Talent's Reason.
  • Quick and Brutal grants a maneuver; the rule grants an extra main action and move action.
  • Triangulate's trigger is disabled with condition 0 ("Too many pings. Keep manual").
  • Thunder Mother rolls at the start of the next round, not the end of the round, so it never fires after the last round.
  • Not implemented (no modifiers): Warmaster, Psion's choice, Masterwork, Missed Cue, Formal Introductions, Dramaturgy, Applause's tier raise, Everyone's Best Friend, Hakaan rubble, Revenant inert state, Shadowmeld surface damage, Umbral Form's automatic hiding, Borrow From the Future's lockout, Omnomnom's swallow damage, Gummy Ball's Suck It Up.
  • Typos that reach players today: purge text "Enemies are suprised no longer"; Melodrama reasons use the checklist names, but the raw chat texts include "Vilian Action".
  • Vanguard's Commanding Presence is named "Imposing Attitude" in data.
  • The tactician focus trigger for marked creatures fires on any damage to the marked creature, including damage from enemies or the environment, not only from the Tactician or allies.

docs.title: History rules review: core rules
docs.text: Scope: the events the Draw Steel core rules create (Heroes book Ch. 1 The Basics, Ch. 5 general ability rules and conditions, Ch. 9 Tests, Ch. 10 Combat, Ch. 11 Negotiation, Ch. 12 Downtime Projects, the glossary, and the general Heroic Resource pattern). Class features and monster/Director rules are covered by the other two reviews. Written 2026-11-04 against branch feature/hero-sheet-party-picker.

docs.title: How to read this
docs.text:
• Rule cites H:<line> = ClaudeBridge/ClaudeRefHeroes.lua.
  • Codex today cites code with folder shorthand: DGR/ = DMHub Game Rules/, DSCR/ = Draw Steel Core Rules/, DSUI/ = Draw Steel UI/, DSV/ = Draw Steel V/, DT/ = Downtime Projects/, data/ = data/objectTables/. Most rules are global rule mods (data/globalrulemods/*.yaml) or condition rows (data/charconditions/*.yaml) implemented as triggered abilities.
  • Logged today? is the Action Log (ChatPanel/ActionLogPanel.lua, which shows every non-chat message: rolls and custom messages). Three things decide whether an automatic rule shows up:
  • a triggered ability posts a cast card only when mandatory is false (prompted) (DGR/TriggeredAbility.lua:2644); automatic rule triggers are silent;
  • a damage/replenish/purge/heal behavior posts its own card only when its chatMessage field is set (Draw Steel Ability Behaviors/AbilityDamage.lua:56, DGR/AbilityReplenish.lua:718, DGR/AbilityPurgeEffects.lua:286, DGR/ActivatedAbility.lua:5136);
  • per-target notes recorded on a cast card (RecordTokenMessage) render only as hover tooltips, and not at all for the caster (comment at DGR/ActivatedAbility.lua:5138).
  • Several silent changes are still recorded somewhere, just not in the log: per-stat histories (creature:GetStatHistory, DGR/Creature.lua:1899; stamina, temporary stamina, max stamina, every resource) shown as tooltips on the sheet, the global resource history for Hero Tokens and Malice (DGR/Resource.lua:40), the negotiation's own story log (DSV/NegotiationRules.lua:692), the montage tally (DocumentSystem/MontageDocument.lua:77) and the downtime project roll list (DT/DTProject.lua). History can read these instead of starting from nothing.
  • History should show uses the brief's row types: Banner (combat start/end), Round heading, Turn heading, Action row, Nested row (a triggered or automatic effect under the action that set it off), Turn line (compact line with no action: start/end of turn, saves, conditions ending; COPY T16 format), What happened sentence and Why line on the detail card (COPY N2/N3, R1 wording). Play outside combat (tests, montage, negotiation, respite) has no rounds, so it is shown as Scene rows (an action row grouped under the scene instead of a turn).
  • How often: every combat / often / rare.
